Company settings hold only name, city, country and a free-text taxId (SettingsTab.tsx:17-21) with no 9-digit check (validate.ts:170 checks only that it is not empty). There is nowhere to store branch ID, activity code, document type (I/C/D), UUID, submission ID, signature or ETA status. README says 'the tax ID and VAT data are already captured'.
findings.impact: B2B invoices issued from Bonyan are not valid ETA e-invoices and B2C sales cannot produce e-receipts, which are mandatory for VAT-registered Egyptian businesses. This blocks the Egypt-first launch and is where local competitors (Odoo with the l10n_eg_edi module, local ETA-integrated ERPs) win outright.
findings.recommendation: Add an 'Egypt e-invoicing' setup step: issuer RIN validation, branch ID and address, activity code, ETA client ID/secret, and a signing method (USB token via a local signer agent, or HSM). Add receiver type, ID and structured address as system fields on Customers (required when type = B or the invoice exceeds the ETA threshold for persons). Add EGS/GS1 item code and unit code on Products, and tax type/sub-type per line. Add a server-side serializer to the ETA canonical JSON, signing, submission, status polling (Valid / Invalid / Rejected / Cancelled), storage of uuid and longId, a printed QR, and e-receipt (POS) submission. The health check blocks 'Post' when required ETA fields are missing.
findings.auditor: The substance is right: Line has no item code, unit code or tax type (types.ts:6-14), there are no fields for ETA UUID, status or signature, and taxId is free text with only an empty check (validate.ts:170). Corrections: tax_id is not core-only. All 9 templates build Customers through core.accounts, which adds 'Tax registration no.' (templates.ts:36). It is a plain, deletable field rather than a system field. Suppliers also have tax_id (roles.ts:239). Some citations are wrong: roles.ts:27-33 and 78-84 are the ROLES description table, while the actual system fields are at roles.ts:176-181 and 227-232. The README's 'already captured' claim is overstated, as the panel says.

findings.title: VAT is a free-typed percentage: no tax codes, exempt vs zero-rated, recoverability, VAT return or settlement
findings.evidence: Any VAT value from 0 to 100 is accepted per line (engine.ts:395; RecordPage.tsx:290 is an editable number box). Zero-rated exports, exempt supplies and out-of-scope lines all look the same, as 0. Input VAT always goes to 1400 (engine.ts:494), even for unregistered suppliers or non-deductible items. There is no Table tax, stamp duty or VAT return (Form 10) report. 'VAT payable' is lifetime output minus input (Accounting.tsx:24) and can never be cleared, because the VAT payment to the ETA cannot be recorded (see ACCO-07).
findings.impact: VAT returns cannot be prepared from the system, the VAT payable KPI only ever grows, and a salesperson can type 13% or 0% on a taxable line with nothing stopping it. Tax-inspection exposure falls on the owner.
findings.recommendation: Add a Tax codes master seeded for Egypt (Standard 14%, Zero-rated 0% export, Exempt, Out of scope, Table tax 5/10%, plus non-recoverable input), each with GL accounts, ETA type/sub-type, and return box. Lines pick a code (defaulting from the product and customer fiscal position), not a raw percentage, and editing it needs a finance right. Build a monthly VAT return report by box, with drill-down, that generates a settlement entry (Dr 2200 / Cr 1400 / Cr VAT payable to ETA) and a payment.
findings.auditor: VAT 0-100 is the only check (engine.ts:395), and the line VAT input is free (RecordPage.tsx:290). Input VAT always goes to 1400 (engine.ts:494). VAT payable is lifetime output minus input (Accounting.tsx:24) and cannot be settled. One aggravating path the panel missed: Sales has RW on quotes (packs.ts:103), and quoteToInvoice copies quote lines with their VAT unchanged (engine.ts:561). A salesperson's 0% VAT on a quote therefore flows into the invoice that finance posts, with no warning against the product's vat_rate.

findings.title: No withholding tax (Egyptian WHT 1/3/5%) on supplier payments or customer receipts
findings.evidence: registerPayment books only Cash vs AR/AP for the full amount (engine.ts:545-550), and Payment has no tax fields (types.ts:66-75). Suppliers and customers have no WHT status or rate (roles.ts:85-91, 27-33). Nothing in src mentions withholding except the README's future list.
findings.impact: Egyptian companies must deduct and remit WHT on qualifying supplier payments and file the quarterly Form 41, and customers deduct WHT from what they pay these SMEs. Without it, every real payment either leaves a false open balance (customer paid net of WHT) or overpays suppliers, and the Form 41 has to be rebuilt in Excel.
findings.recommendation: Add WHT codes (rate, GL account, ETA classification) on suppliers and customers. In the payment dialog, show 'Withholding: EGP x (3%)' and post Dr AP / Cr Bank / Cr WHT payable (for customers: Dr Bank, Dr WHT receivable, Cr AR). Add a WHT certificate print and a quarterly Form 41 export listing supplier tax IDs.
findings.auditor: registerPayment books only cash against AR or AP (engine.ts:545-550). Payment has no tax fields (types.ts:66-75). Nothing in src mentions withholding; it appears only in README:97. Citation: roles.ts:85-91 and 27-33 are the ROLES table, while the supplier and customer fields are at roles.ts:234-240 and 176-181. A customer paying net of WHT cannot settle an invoice cleanly; there is no write-off path, so the balance stays open.

findings.title: Treasury is minimal: one cash account, no bank reconciliation, no cheque lifecycle, no advances or multi-invoice allocation
findings.evidence: Every method (cash, bank, cheque, instapay, card) posts to account 1100 (engine.ts:544). A payment belongs to exactly one document (types.ts:68) and cannot exceed its balance (engine.ts:539), so overpayments, customer advances and down-payments are impossible. The reference is PAY-<doc>-n (engine.ts:542), not a sequenced receipt voucher. Payment dates can be in the future (only checked against the document date, engine.ts:540). There is no receipt print, bank statement import or reconciliation screen.
findings.impact: In Egypt, post-dated cheques ('شيكات تحت التحصيل') and InstaPay or Fawry settlements are the norm. Without a separate cheque-in-collection account, bounce handling, multiple bank accounts and reconciliation, cash on the balance sheet is unverifiable and collections cannot be allocated the way customers actually pay (one transfer covering five invoices).
findings.recommendation: Add Bank/Cash accounts (each a GL account) and payment methods mapped to them, with InstaPay or card clearing accounts. Add a Receipt/Payment voucher document (RV-/PV- gapless) that can allocate across many invoices, leave an unapplied credit or advance (customer advances liability), and carry bank charges or discounts. Add a cheque register (received → deposited → cleared / bounced, with an auto-reversal on bounce). Add bank statement CSV import and a reconciliation screen that suggests matches. Block payment dates in the future.
findings.auditor: Every method posts to 1100 (engine.ts:544). A payment belongs to one document (types.ts:68). Overpayment is blocked (engine.ts:539). The ref is PAY-<doc>-n (engine.ts:542). My probe registered a cheque dated 2099-01-01 without error, because only payment date < document date is checked (engine.ts:540). There is no reconciliation or receipt print anywhere.

findings.title: The audit trail is truncated, unattributed and can be impersonated
findings.area: Audit trail (engine.ts log, types.ts, store.ts switchUser)
findings.evidence: log() keeps only the latest 500 activity rows (engine.ts:218), so a busy SME loses its history within days. JournalEntry, Payment and StockMove carry no createdBy or timestamp (types.ts:33-75), and Rec has postedAt but no postedBy (types.ts:28). Quote status changes are not logged (RecordPage.tsx:170-175). An admin can 'Switch user' (store.ts:267-272, Shell.tsx:90-93), and act() then runs as the impersonated user (useApp.ts:36), so log entries, approvals (decidedBy) and createdBy record the wrong person (engine.ts:217, 755).
findings.impact: Who posted, voided, paid or approved what cannot be proven, and audit standards (ISA 315/330 IT general controls) and the Egyptian tax-procedures requirement to keep records for the statutory retention period are not met. Impersonation lets an admin manufacture a 'Manager approved' trail.
findings.recommendation: Write an append-only audit_log table on the server (actor = the auth.uid() of the person who actually signed in, plus 'acting as' when impersonating, action, document, before/after, IP, timestamp), with no cap. Stamp postedBy, voidedBy and createdBy on every journal, payment and stock row. Make impersonation read-only, or at least block post, pay, void and approve while impersonating, and label actions 'by Admin as Sara'. Add an 'Audit trail' tab under Accounting with filters and export.
findings.auditor: The activity log is capped at 500 (engine.ts:218). StockMove, JournalEntry and Payment have no actor or timestamp (types.ts:33-75). Rec has postedAt but no postedBy (types.ts:28). setQuoteStatus writes no log (RecordPage.tsx:170-175). act() runs as the impersonated user (useApp.ts:36), so log() (engine.ts:217) and decidedBy (engine.ts:755) record the wrong person. The own-request check at engine.ts:753 also compares the impersonated id. An admin can therefore request as Sales, switch to Manager and approve, producing a two-person trail with no second person. Execution rows are not capped (only activity is), but they carry no actor.

findings.title: One 'finance' flag grants the whole procure-to-pay cycle; admins bypass every approval
findings.area: Segregation of duties (engine.ts canPost/canApprove, packs.ts roles)
findings.evidence: canPost (engine.ts:35-38) is one boolean that covers post, void and pay (engine.ts:425, 510, 534). The default finance role gets ALL rights on suppliers and purchases (packs.ts:105). ApprovalRule actions are only 'post' and 'stage' (engine.ts:715), with no approval for payments, voids, or changes to supplier master data. canApprove returns true for any admin (engine.ts:711), so guardApproval silently passes for admins (engine.ts:728), and the UI says 'You can do it yourself' (RecordPage.tsx:409).
findings.impact: One finance user can create a fictitious supplier, post a bill to it and pay it, with no second pair of eyes. That is the classic SME fraud pattern COSO and every auditor tests for. Odoo, NetSuite and Business Central let you separate these duties.
findings.recommendation: Split finance rights: Post sales, Post purchases, Register receipts, Register payments, Void/credit, Manage chart of accounts and tax, Lock periods. Add approval actions 'pay' (with amount thresholds) and 'void', and a dual-control rule for supplier bank-detail changes. Add an SoD check to the health check that warns when one role holds create-supplier + post-bill + pay. Admin approvals should be logged as 'override' with a mandatory reason instead of passing silently.
findings.auditor: The facts are right. canPost gates post, void and pay (engine.ts:425, 510, 534). Finance gets ALL on suppliers and purchases (packs.ts:105). Approval actions are only 'post' and 'stage' (engine.ts:715), and admins pass guardApproval (engine.ts:711, 728). Two overstatements: the UI does tell the admin ('You can do it yourself', RecordPage.tsx:409), so it is visible, just unlogged and with no reason captured. And the default approver is Management, which has no finance flag (packs.ts:102, 170-171), so the default finance user cannot self-approve large bills. Full SoD is also rarely achievable in 1-2 person SME finance teams, and QuickBooks and Zoho offer little more. Logging overrides and a 'pay' approval are the valuable parts.

findings.title: The credit limit is a decorative field; there are no customer payment terms
findings.evidence: credit_limit exists only as a plain field in the distribution template (templates.ts:226). Nothing in engine.ts reads it. The due date always defaults to date + 30 days (engine.ts:232), with no payment-terms master on customers. postDocument does not check overdue balances or exposure.
findings.impact: Wholesale and pharma distributors, two headline templates, extend unlimited credit to customers who are already 90+ days overdue. That is the 'late collections' pain the onboarding promises to fix.
findings.recommendation: Make credit_limit and payment_terms (Cash, 15, 30, 60, end of month+30) system fields on Customers. At post, compute exposure (open AR + this invoice) and block or route to an approval when it exceeds the limit or when an invoice is more than X days overdue. Show a credit bar on the invoice and customer page ('EGP 85k of 100k used, 2 overdue').
findings.auditor: credit_limit appears only at templates.ts:226, and nothing reads it. The due date defaults to +30 days (engine.ts:232). postDocument has no exposure check.

findings.title: Purchasing has no PO / goods receipt / 3-way match, duplicate-bill protection or landed cost
findings.evidence: A purchase bill both receives stock and recognises the liability in one step (engine.ts:474-497). supplier_ref is optional and not unique per supplier (roles.ts:97), so the same supplier invoice can be entered and paid twice. There is no way to add freight, customs duty or clearance to stock cost, and every non-stock line lands in 5100 (engine.ts:493).
findings.impact: Importers, a large share of Egyptian SMEs, understate inventory cost and overstate margins because customs and freight go to expenses. Duplicate supplier payments, one of the top AP losses, go undetected. Buying without a PO or receipt makes 'what did we order versus receive versus get billed' impossible.
findings.recommendation: Add an optional Purchase order → Goods receipt (GRN, posts Dr Inventory / Cr GRNI) → Bill (clears GRNI, with price/qty variance) flow that simple users can switch off. Make (supplier, supplier_ref) unique, with an error on a duplicate. Add a Landed cost document that allocates freight and duty to receipts by value, qty or weight and re-averages cost.
findings.auditor: The bill both receives stock and recognises the liability (engine.ts:474-497). supplier_ref is an optional, non-unique plain field at roles.ts:246 (not 97). There is no landed cost, and non-stock lines go to 5100 (engine.ts:493).

findings.title: No multi-currency documents or FX accounting
findings.evidence: One company currency, locked after the first posting (SettingsTab.tsx:23-26). Documents, lines and journals carry no currency or rate fields (types.ts:6-64), and there is no exchange-difference account.
findings.impact: Egyptian importers buy in USD/EUR and exporters invoice in USD. After repeated EGP devaluations, realised and unrealised FX (IAS 21 / EAS 13) is material. Users will keep foreign-currency bills outside the system.
findings.recommendation: Add currency and rate to documents and payments (with a daily CBE rate table and a manual override), and store both transaction and functional amounts on journal lines. Post realised FX on payment and run a month-end revaluation of open foreign AR/AP and bank balances to unrealised FX.
findings.auditor: Currency is locked once any journal exists (SettingsTab.tsx:23-26). Line, JournalEntry and Payment have no currency or rate fields. Note that the seeded sample journal (see the first missed issue) locks the currency on day one.

findings.title: Discount and rounding precision fall short of ETA and costing needs
findings.evidence: Only a line percentage discount exists (types.ts:12, engine.ts:359): no fixed-amount discount, invoice-level discount, early-payment discount or 'items discount' (after tax). The price input has step 0.01 (RecordPage.tsx:288), while ETA accepts up to 5 decimals on unit values. Moving-average cost and unit cost are rounded to 2 decimals (engine.ts:483-484), which causes the residual shown in ACCO-03(C).
findings.impact: Pharma and distribution price lists with 3-4 decimal unit prices cannot be invoiced exactly, and common commercial discounts (a header 'EGP 500 off', cash discount) cannot be represented, so totals will not match the ETA portal.
findings.recommendation: Keep unit price and cost to 5 decimals and round only line totals to 2 (ETA method). Add a discount type (percent or amount) per line, a document-level discount allocated pro-rata to lines before VAT, and an ETA 'itemsDiscount' after-tax discount. Add a rounding-difference account for cash rounding.
findings.auditor: Line.price is not rounded. lineNet rounds only the line total (engine.ts:358-360), which is the ETA method. step='0.01' (RecordPage.tsx:288) is only a browser hint outside a form, and typing 3.125 is stored as typed. So 'cannot be invoiced exactly' is overstated. The real defects are: the print shows price.toFixed(2) (RecordPage.tsx:366), which misprints 3-4 decimal unit prices; cost rounding (engine.ts:483-484), already counted in ACCO-03(C); and no amount or header discounts (types.ts:12).

findings.title: The printed 'Tax invoice' is incomplete, drafts can be printed as tax invoices, and there are no customer statements
findings.evidence: PrintView titles any invoice 'Tax invoice', including drafts that show 'DRAFT' as the number (RecordPage.tsx:335, 351). The Print button is shown for every status (RecordPage.tsx:88). Missing from the print: seller address and commercial registry, buyer address and receiver ID, VAT amount per line, VAT summary per rate, amount in words, Arabic/bilingual layout, ETA UUID or QR, bank details and payment terms. No customer or supplier statement of account (كشف حساب) exists anywhere.
findings.impact: Customers receive documents that are not valid tax invoices, or drafts mistaken for invoices, and finance teams keep making statements in Excel, which is the most-requested report in Egyptian B2B collections.
findings.recommendation: Print drafts with a 'PROFORMA / DRAFT — not a tax invoice' watermark and title. Build a bilingual (Arabic/English) RTL invoice template with all statutory fields, line VAT, a VAT summary, the total in Arabic words, and the ETA QR/UUID once submitted. Add 'Statement of account' on customer and supplier pages (opening balance, documents, payments, running balance, ageing footer), with PDF, WhatsApp and e-mail sending.
findings.auditor: The title is 'Tax invoice' for any invoice status, and 'DRAFT' appears as the number (RecordPage.tsx:335, 351). Print is shown for every status (RecordPage.tsx:88). The print has seller city and country plus the tax ID, and the buyer tax ID only if the field exists (RecordPage.tsx:346-360). It has no addresses, per-rate VAT summary, Arabic layout or amount in words. Only void gets a watermark (line 376). There are no statements of account anywhere.

findings.title: Business dates use UTC, so Cairo users get yesterday's date (and last year's number on 1 January)
findings.evidence: todayISO = new Date().toISOString().slice(0,10) (engine.ts:18), used for default invoice dates (engine.ts:230), due dates (engine.ts:232), void reversal dates (engine.ts:513) and scheduled automations. PaymentModal defaults the same way (RecordPage.tsx:311). Cairo is UTC+2, or UTC+3 in summer.
findings.impact: Documents created between 00:00 and 02:00/03:00 local time carry the previous day's date. On 1 January such an invoice takes the previous year's sequence (engine.ts:400) and lands in the wrong VAT period.
findings.recommendation: Add company.timezone (default Africa/Cairo) and derive business dates with Intl.DateTimeFormat in that zone, both in the engine and in the future server RPCs. Add a test for the 23:30 UTC case.
findings.auditor: todayISO uses UTC (engine.ts:18). The same pattern appears in PaymentModal (RecordPage.tsx:311), Dashboard.tsx:13 and seed day() (seed.ts:24-28). The impact is limited to 00:00-02:59 Cairo time (and the 1 January sequence edge), so medium is generous; the fix is S.

findings.title: Tests prove only a tautology; nothing reconciles the subledgers to the GL, and there is no 'books doctor'
findings.evidence: The 'sample data keeps the books balanced' test (engine.test.ts:34-43) and the balanced() helper check debits = credits, which journal() already guarantees (engine.ts:410). No test asserts GL 1200 = Σ open invoice balances, GL 2100 = Σ open bills, or GL 1300 = Σ stock value, nor covers voids after later movements, track_stock toggles or negative stock. All 33 tests pass while the 5 discrepancies in ACCO-03 reproduce. The Accounting page shows a green 'Books balance' banner (Accounting.tsx:34-37) that cannot be red.
findings.impact: The 'guardrails keep it correct' claim is not verified where it matters, and users get false reassurance. Criterion 11 (AI that diagnoses the user's system) has no finance foundation.
findings.recommendation: Add an engine function booksHealth(ws) that returns invariant checks: AR, AP and inventory subledger vs GL, negative stock, products with stock but track_stock off, sequence gaps or duplicates, documents dated in locked or future periods, VAT input claimed from unregistered suppliers, and unapplied cash. Run it in property-based tests (fast-check with random post/void/pay sequences) and show it as a 'Books health' card on Accounting, with plain-language causes and one-click fixes (for example 'Create stock adjustment', 'Post FX revaluation'). This is where the AI assistant explains anomalies.
findings.auditor: balanced() (engine.test.ts:20-25) re-checks what journal() enforces (engine.ts:410). The only subledger assertion is stock = onHand (engine.test.ts:41), and nothing checks GL to subledger. My probes reproduced every ACCO-03 discrepancy while the suite stays green. The green banner (Accounting.tsx:34-37) is effectively unconditional.

findings.title: Declined or expired quotations can still be invoiced, and sent quotes are edited without a revision
findings.evidence: 'Accept & invoice' shows for every status except invoiced, including declined (RecordPage.tsx:72-75). quoteToInvoice ignores status and valid_until (engine.ts:557-565). setLines allows edits while status is 'sent' (engine.ts:383), with no revision number or log entry, and setQuoteStatus writes no activity (RecordPage.tsx:170-175).
findings.impact: Prices and terms the customer never accepted can become invoices, and there is no evidence of what was actually sent, which leads to commercial disputes.
findings.recommendation: Require status sent or accepted and valid_until ≥ today (or a finance override) to convert. Editing a sent quote creates revision R2 and keeps R1 read-only. Log every status change.
findings.auditor: 'Accept & invoice' renders for any status except invoiced, including declined (RecordPage.tsx:72-77). quoteToInvoice ignores status and valid_until (engine.ts:557-565). setLines allows 'sent' (engine.ts:383). setQuoteStatus does not log (RecordPage.tsx:170-175). No 'accepted' status is ever set anywhere.

findings.title: Sample data is posted into the company's live books by default and cannot be removed, despite the UI promising it can
findings.evidence: Suggest.tsx:17 defaults 'Fill with sample data' to true, and Suggest.tsx:97 says 'Remove it any time from Settings'. SettingsTab.tsx (lines 1-61) has no remove function, and nothing in src implements one. On first publish, Builder.tsx:64-69 calls seedSampleData on the real workspace. That function posts 2 bills and up to 12 invoices through postDocument and registerPayment (seed.ts:150-180). It also adds demo users with @demo.local e-mails (seed.ts:30-38). My probe of a distribution workspace got 23 journal entries, 9 payments and sequences {BILL-2026:2, INV-2026:12}. Posted documents cannot be deleted (engine.ts:297), paid ones cannot be voided (engine.ts:512), and the currency then locks because a journal exists (SettingsTab.tsx:23).
findings.impact: Every company that keeps the default starts life with fictitious revenue, AR, AP, VAT, stock and cash in its real ledger. Its first real tax invoice is INV-2026-0013, not 0001, which breaks the gapless series an ETA inspector expects. Fake customers and suppliers appear in ageing. Because there are no manual journals or payment reversal, none of it can be cleaned up. The owner either lives with false books or abandons the workspace.
findings.recommendation: Never seed the production ledger. Option A: run sample data in a separate 'Demo company' workspace (or an in-memory preview, as ReportsTab already does at ReportsTab.tsx:31-43), with a 'Start my real company' button that copies only the schema. Option B: tag every seeded record and row with sample:true and use a reserved prefix such as DEMO-INV, and add Settings → 'Remove sample data'. That wipes the tagged records, journals, stock moves, payments, sequences and demo users, and is allowed only before the first real posting. Until then, default the checkbox to off and fix the false 'Remove it any time' copy.

findings.title: Customer 'Balance due' and 'Total invoiced' rollups include unposted draft invoices
findings.area: Receivables on customer records (packs.ts addSmartDefaults, engine.ts fieldValue/applyTotals)
findings.evidence: packs.ts:139-140 adds rollups that sum invoices.total and invoices.balance onto every customer. fieldValue filters only status !== 'void' (engine.ts:139), so drafts are included. applyTotals gives a draft balance = total (engine.ts:376-378). My probe gave a customer whose only invoice is an unposted draft for 1,140: balance_due 1140, total_invoiced 1140, while ageing() returned [] and GL 1200 was 0.
findings.impact: Collectors chase customers for invoices that were never issued. The customer page disagrees with the Ageing tab and the trial balance, and 'Total invoiced' is VAT-inclusive and includes drafts. This undermines the 'late collections' promise and trust in the numbers.
findings.recommendation: Let rollups take the source module's filters (default for document modules: status in posted, partial, paid). Seed 'Total invoiced' on subtotal, labelled 'Invoiced (excl. VAT)', and 'Balance due' with status ≠ draft. Add a validator warning when a rollup on a document module has no status filter.

findings.title: Average cost, margins and stock value are shown to every role, and every member downloads the full ledger
findings.area: Finance confidentiality (Inventory.tsx, Shell.tsx, App.tsx, RLS select policy)
findings.evidence: Inventory.tsx:9-13 has no permission check. App.tsx:58 routes /app/inventory unguarded, and Shell.tsx:53 shows the Stock link whenever a products module exists. The page shows Avg cost, Margin % and Value per item (Inventory.tsx:30-46) to Sales, Service and any custom role. Accounting is hidden in the UI only (Accounting.tsx:11). The RLS SELECT policy (migration lines 59-61) returns the whole doc, including data.journal and data.payments, to every member, so the browser holds it for any role.
findings.impact: In distribution and pharma, the headline templates, salespeople seeing landed cost and margin per SKU is a classic commercial leak: it hurts price negotiations and drives staff poaching. Competitors (Odoo 'Show cost' rights, SAP B1 authorisations, Zoho role-based price visibility) hide cost from sales by default.
findings.recommendation: Add a 'See costs & margins' right on roles (on by default for Admin and Finance only). Gate the Inventory page's cost, margin and value columns, the product 'Average cost' field and COGS in reports behind it, and route-guard /app/accounting. Long term (with ACCO-01), serve role-filtered data from server views so the ledger never reaches roles without finance rights.

findings.title: Document number prefix can be changed after posting, made to collide with another module, or emptied, which breaks the numbering series
findings.area: Numbering control (builder ModulesTab.tsx, engine.ts nextNumber, validate.ts)
findings.evidence: ModulesTab.tsx:444 lets an admin edit numberPrefix at any time. The input strips everything except A-Z (so a typed Arabic or numeric prefix becomes ''). Once it is '', the `mod.numberPrefix &&` guard hides the field, so it cannot be restored. engine.ts:452 uses `mod.numberPrefix ?? 'DOC'`, which keeps the empty string, and my probe posted invoice number '-2026-0001'. validate.ts has no prefix checks (no uniqueness across modules, no non-empty check, no lock after posting). Setting the purchase-bill prefix to 'INV' makes bills draw from the INV-2026 counter (engine.ts:400), so bills get tax-invoice numbers and the invoice series has gaps.
findings.impact: The gapless, unique tax-invoice series that ETA and auditors rely on can be broken by one keystroke in the builder, with no warning and no audit entry. The publish health check still shows green.
findings.recommendation: Lock numberPrefix once a module has any posted document (show a lock icon with 'Used by 37 posted invoices'). Validate it as non-empty and unique across all document modules. Allow a series change only as a new series that starts at the next fiscal year and is logged. Keep the sequence key independent of the prefix (sequence id per module plus fiscal year), so renaming never resets or merges counters.

strengths: Stock is a ledger and is never typed in. On-hand is the sum of immutable StockMove rows (engine.ts:419-421). The product's 'stock' and 'cost' fields are system read-only (roles.ts:213,216; ro() at roles.ts:120). cleanValues skips read-only fields, so neither import nor edits can overwrite them. A product that has movements can't be deleted (engine.ts:298).

Perpetual inventory is posted in the same transaction as the document. A purchase bill posts Dr 1300 Inventory / Dr 1400 VAT input / Dr 5100 for non-stock lines / Cr 2100 AP (engine.ts:489-497). A sales invoice posts revenue, VAT output and AR plus Dr 5000 COGS / Cr 1300 at the moving-average cost (engine.ts:465-474). Every journal is checked for balance before it is written (engine.ts:404-410).

The moving-average formula on receipt is correct: (oldQty*oldCost + qty*unitCost)/newQty. The unit cost is net of line discount (engine.ts:479-483), so supplier discounts are capitalised, as IAS 2.11 requires.
Overselling is blocked by default. Quantities are first added up per product across all lines of the document. The error message is clear and names each item ('need 5, have 3') (engine.ts:439-448).

Document numbering is gapless and the number is taken only after every check has passed (engine.ts:450-452). Posted bills and invoices can't be edited, only voided, and voiding writes mirror reversal entries (engine.ts:505-527).

There are useful early P2P controls: payables ageing (engine.ts:867-885), an approval for large purchases with no self-approval (packs.ts:171, engine.ts:756), a reorder alert that de-duplicates its task (engine.ts:694-706), and a purchase line that pre-fills the average cost (RecordPage.tsx:263).
The Inventory screen exists and is easy to read: stock value, tracked items, items at or below reorder level, a margin per item, and movements coloured +/- (Inventory.tsx).

scorecard.rationale: The base is sound: a perpetual ledger, moving average on receipt, posting tied to the GL, and overselling blocked. But void-of-bill can drive stock negative (SUPP-01), the subledger drifts from the GL after invoice voids, rounding and negative-stock sales (SUPP-04/05/17), and there are no adjustments, opening stock, returns, lots or expiry, UoM, warehouses, landed cost or period lock. It doesn't yet meet IAS 2 or common WMS and P2P practice.

Only two flows are verified end to end (bill → stock and invoice → stock). Procure-to-pay (PO/receipt/3-way match), order-to-cash (SO/delivery), returns, counts, transfers and production are missing. The probes showed the existing void flow breaks invariants the 33 tests don't cover.

The posting rules are logical and the guardrails on read-only stock and cost are good. But the setup contradicts itself: the 'stock off by default' help text vs track_stock=true in the engine, services templates that can't invoice, a product's stock type that can be toggled once stock exists, a manufacturing template promising stock moves it doesn't make, and a void message pointing to a refund action that doesn't exist.

There are four KPI tiles and two flat tables. There's no stock card, valuation as of a date, ABC/XYZ, days on hand, dead stock, expiry risk or stock-vs-GL reconciliation, and stock moves aren't available to the report builder.

Against Odoo Inventory, Zoho Inventory, BC or SAP B1 (and local Daftra/Qoyod) the supply-chain scope is far behind: no POs, deliveries, warehouses, lots, UoM, barcode, landed cost or returns. Only a very small single-store trader could run on it today.

Very simple today and the language is plain. But much of the simplicity comes from leaving features out, and some of it misleads users (the unticked checkbox that is actually ticked, a free-text line that skips stock). Users will hit dead ends that create complexity.
Users can add custom fields and modules, but nothing custom can take part in stock or posting (production orders, transfers, surveys). Flexibility stops exactly where the ERP rules begin.
The only supply-chain automation is a reorder notification and task. There's no automatic diagnosis of stock-vs-GL drift, negative stock, uncategorised purchases or expiring lots, and no forecasting.

vision: Best-in-class for Bonyan's supply chain means an Egyptian distributor, pharma wholesaler or workshop never has to think about inventory accounting, and the books still pass an IAS 2 audit. Every product has a clear type (stockable, consumable or service), proper UoMs (carton of 24, piece) and an optional lot or serial plus expiry tracking. Every quantity lives in a warehouse, location or van. Purchasing runs as one visual chain: suggested reorders → PO (approved by amount, sent by WhatsApp) → mobile goods receipt by camera scan, capturing lot and expiry → supplier bill matched 3-way with variances highlighted → payment run approved by a second person. Landed costs fold freight and customs into item cost. Sales run quote → sales order that reserves stock → FEFO pick list → signed delivery note → ETA e-invoice, with credit and debit notes for every return. Cycle counts happen on a phone with variance approval, and opening stock imports in minutes. Every move posts through a server-side transaction, so two storekeepers can never double-sell or lose a posting. A live reconciliation tile proves stock value equals GL 1300 every day. The inventory cockpit beats Zoho and Odoo visually: an ABC/XYZ heatmap, days-of-cover gauges per SKU, an expiry-risk timeline in money, dead-stock cards with suggested markdowns, supplier on-time and price-variance scorecards, and warehouse tiles with value and fill. An AI assistant watches all of this. It flags negative or drifting stock, bills entered as free text that should have been stock, lots about to expire with the customers most likely to buy them, and min/max levels that no longer match sales velocity. It proposes the fix as a one-click draft (adjustment, transfer, PO) that a person approves.

findings.title: Voiding a purchase bill after its goods were sold makes stock and the Inventory GL negative, and ignores the no-negative-stock policy
findings.evidence: voidDocument (engine.ts:505-527) reverses every StockMove of the bill. It never checks onHand against company.allowNegativeStock; the oversell check exists only for invoices at engine.ts:445. Cost is re-averaged only when remaining > 0 (engine.ts:519). Probe in scratchpad (distribution template, negative stock OFF): bill 10 @60, invoice 10, then void the bill. Result: onHand = -10, avg cost 60, GL 1300 = -600. The void succeeded without any error.
findings.impact: The balance sheet shows a negative inventory asset and the stock list shows negative quantity, even though the company chose 'never negative'. This is the most common real-world action: a wrong bill is reversed after part of the delivery has already been sold. Books and stock are then wrong and nothing warns anyone.
findings.recommendation: In voidDocument, for role 'purchases', simulate the reversal and block it if any product would drop below 0 while allowNegativeStock is false. The message should send the user to the right document: 'Goods from this bill were already sold. Create a Purchase return for the unsold quantity instead.' Add an engine test. Longer term, replace 'void' with proper reversal documents (see SUPP-03).
findings.auditor: Reproduced with an engine probe on the distribution template (allowNegativeStock=false). Bill 10@60, invoice 10, void bill gives onHand -10, cost 60, GL 1300 = -600, with no error. Selling 4 of 10 and then voiding gives -4 and -240. voidDocument (engine.ts:508-532) never reads allowNegativeStock, and the only check is for invoices (engine.ts:445). Correction to the recommendation: blocking only when onHand would go below 0 is not enough. When stock stays positive, the same re-averaging at engine.ts:519 drives the average cost negative (see MISS-02). The guard should be 'the bill's received qty is still fully on hand', otherwise require a purchase return.

findings.title: No stock adjustment, physical count or opening-stock document: corrections are only possible through fake bills or invoices
findings.evidence: The only stock writers are postDocument and voidDocument (engine.ts:460, 484, 521). The Inventory page tells users: 'To correct stock, post a bill or invoice — never type it in.' (Inventory.tsx:25). createRecord forces stock=0 and cost=0 on new products (engine.ts:254-257). There is no opening balance equity account in CHART (types.ts:43-53).
findings.impact: A company migrating from Excel or Odoo can only load opening stock as a supplier bill. That creates fake AP and fake recoverable VAT input, which is a tax-reporting problem with the ETA. Shrinkage, breakage, expiry write-offs and count variances can only be booked as a sales invoice, which inflates revenue and VAT output. Cycle counting, a basic WMS discipline, is impossible. Any company that goes live mid-year can't start with correct books.
findings.recommendation: Add an engine-level 'Stock adjustment' document with lines (product, counted qty or +/- qty, reason code: count variance, damage, expiry, sample, internal use, opening balance) and post it to new accounts: 3900 Opening balance equity for opening stock, 5200 Inventory adjustments/shrinkage for the rest. Add a 'Stock count' flow: freeze the expected qty, enter or scan the counted qty (mobile friendly), show variances with value, require approval above a threshold, then post one adjustment. In onboarding, add an 'Import opening stock (qty + unit cost)' step after the products import.
findings.auditor: Confirmed. Inventory.tsx:25 tells users to correct stock with a bill or invoice. createRecord forces stock=0 and cost=0 (engine.ts:254-257). cost and stock are readOnly (roles.ts:213,216), and checkLines rejects qty<=0 (engine.ts:392), so there is no negative-quantity workaround either. The panel understates the CHART gap (types.ts:43-53): it has no equity accounts at all, not just no opening balance equity, so no opening balance of any kind (stock, AR, AP, cash) can be posted. One mitigation: a user can set VAT to 0 on an 'opening' bill and avoid fake input VAT. Fake AP remains.

findings.title: No sales returns, credit notes, purchase returns or refunds; the void error points to a function that doesn't exist
findings.evidence: The only document actions are post, void and registerPayment (engine.ts:424-552). voidDocument refuses paid documents: 'This document has payments. Refund or reverse them before voiding.' (engine.ts:512). Searching engine.ts for refund, credit note, reverse payment or return finds nothing. The README lists credit notes as future work.
findings.impact: A pharmacy returns 2 of 10 cartons from a paid invoice, or a supplier takes back a damaged batch. Neither can be recorded. The user hits a dead end, so stock, COGS, AR/AP and VAT stay wrong. ETA e-invoicing requires credit and debit notes as their own e-documents that reference the original invoice. Every competitor (Odoo, Zoho, BC, SAP B1) has RMA and credit notes.
findings.recommendation: Add 'Credit note' (sales return) and 'Debit note' (purchase return) document roles linked to the original document. They should allow partial quantities up to what was invoiced or received minus earlier returns. Customer returns bring stock back at the original COGS cost and re-average. Purchase returns remove stock at the bill cost and post the price difference to a variance account. Both reverse VAT. Also add 'Refund' and 'Reverse payment' actions. Add an RMA status (requested → received → inspected → restock/scrap) for distributors and medical devices.
findings.auditor: The only document operations are post, void, payment and quoteToInvoice (engine.ts:423-565). Void refuses paid documents (engine.ts:512), and the Void button is only rendered when status==='posted' (RecordPage.tsx:85), so partially paid or paid documents have no reversal path at all. No refund, credit note or return code exists. README.md:97 lists credit notes as future work. ETA does require credit/debit notes that reference the original document.

findings.title: 'Allow negative stock' posts COGS at zero or stale cost and never corrects it, leaving phantom inventory value
findings.evidence: SettingsTab.tsx:36-37 lets an admin turn on allowNegativeStock. An invoice then posts COGS at p.values.cost, which is 0 before the first receipt (engine.ts:458-460). The next receipt resets cost to unitCost when oldQty <= 0 (engine.ts:483) and debits the full bill value to 1300. Probe: sell 5 with no stock, then buy 5 @60. Result: onHand 0, but GL 1300 = 300 and COGS = 0.
findings.impact: Gross margin is overstated and the balance sheet carries inventory that doesn't exist. Many Egyptian distributors invoice before the paperwork for goods arrives, so this setting will often be turned on and the books will quietly go wrong.
findings.recommendation: When a receipt covers a negative balance, post a cost correction for the negative quantity: Dr 5000 COGS / Cr 1300 at (receipt cost - cost used at sale), as Odoo and Business Central do. Then base averaging only on the positive remainder. Show a 'Negative stock items' warning tile on Inventory and in the health check. Or remove the option and offer 'Invoice now, deliver later' through a delivery note (SUPP-10).
findings.auditor: Probe reproduced it: sell 5 with no stock (COGS 0, since cost=0), then buy 5@60. Result: onHand 0, GL 1300 = 300, COGS 0. engine.ts:458-460 and 483. Downgraded from critical because the setting is admin-only, off by default (recommend.ts:170) and labeled 'not recommended — stock and cost reports become unreliable' (SettingsTab.tsx:37). The claim that 'many Egyptian distributors' will turn it on is speculation. The engine should still never produce phantom value.

findings.title: Voiding a sales invoice brings stock back at its historical cost without re-averaging, so the stock subledger and GL drift apart
findings.evidence: In voidDocument, cost is recomputed only when mod.role === 'purchases' (engine.ts:516-520). Stock re-enters at the old mv.cost, but p.values.cost keeps the current average. Probe: bill 10@60, sell 5, bill 10@90 (avg 80), void the invoice. Result: onHand 20, stock value onHand*avg = 1,600, GL 1300 = 1,500.
findings.impact: The 'Stock value' KPI on Inventory (Inventory.tsx:13) no longer matches the trial balance and nothing detects it. Auditors check exactly this reconciliation first, and an SME owner loses trust in the numbers.
findings.recommendation: Treat every inbound move (receipt, void of sale, customer return, positive adjustment) the same way, with one weighted-average update function. Add a health check, shown in Accounting and on the dashboard, that compares sum(onHand * cost) with the 1300 balance and explains any difference.
findings.auditor: Probe reproduced it exactly: avg 80 after the second bill. After voiding the invoice: onHand 20, onHand*avg = 1600, GL 1300 = 1500. The re-average branch is gated on mod.role==='purchases' (engine.ts:517). Stock re-enters at the move's old cost while p.values.cost stays unchanged. The Inventory KPI (Inventory.tsx:13) then disagrees with the trial balance, and nothing in validate.ts checks stock against the GL.

findings.title: Concurrent warehouse and sales users: a losing save silently discards a posting the user already saw as 'Posted'
findings.evidence: The whole workspace, including stock and journal, is one JSON row. flush() writes with .eq('version', version). When 0 rows match it calls reload(ws.id) and sets sync='reloaded' (store.ts:67-71), which throws away the local mutation. The oversell check (engine.ts:445) runs on the browser's possibly stale copy. The only signal is a small amber 'Reloaded latest' pill (Shell.tsx:87-88).
findings.impact: Two storekeepers post at the same time. One gets a 'Posted. Stock and accounts are updated.' toast (RecordPage.tsx:80), may print INV-2026-0005, and that posting then disappears. The number is given again to another document, so two printed invoices carry the same number, which breaks gapless and ETA rules. This makes real multi-user warehouse operation impossible.
findings.recommendation: Move posting to a server transaction: a Supabase RPC or Edge Function that locks the product stock rows, checks availability, takes the sequence number and writes stock_moves and journal_lines tables in one transaction. Until then, on conflict re-apply the queued engine commands to the fresh document (command replay) instead of discarding them, and show a blocking dialog when a posting couldn't be kept.
findings.auditor: store.ts:68-72: when 0 rows match the version, it calls reload() and sets sync='reloaded'. The local mutation (including a posted invoice and its consumed sequence number) is discarded. The only signal is the amber pill (Shell.tsx:86-88), while RecordPage.tsx:82 has already shown 'Posted. Stock and accounts are updated.' The store has no realtime subscription (no channel or subscribe in store.ts), so copies stay stale until the next conflicting save. The oversell check runs on that stale copy. The duplicate printed number scenario follows from nextNumber reading the local sequences map (engine.ts:399-404).

findings.title: No lots, batches, serials or expiry/FEFO, even though the Medical template sells 'batches and expiry'
findings.evidence: The medical template tagline is 'Hospitals, tenders, EDA registrations, batches and expiry…' (templates.ts:59). Its only expiry field is 'EDA expiry' on the product master (templates.ts:86-87), which is a registration date, not batch expiry, and no automation is attached to it (nothing in packs.ts or recommend.ts). StockMove has no lot, serial or expiry (types.ts:33-41). Device serial is free text on a maintenance ticket (templates.ts:104). The distribution template targets 'food' and 'fmcg' (templates.ts:220).
findings.impact: Pharma and medical distributors in Egypt need batch traceability (EDA track & trace, tender delivery documents list batch and expiry, hospitals reject short-expiry lots). Without FEFO, expired stock is sold or written off unseen, and a recall can't find the customers who received a batch. Selling this template as covering 'batches and expiry' is a misrepresentation risk.
findings.recommendation: Add an item tracking type per product (none / lot / serial) with lot, expiry and manufacturing date captured on receipt and adjustments. On delivery or invoice, suggest lots in FEFO order and block expired lots (warn below a minimum shelf life the customer can set, e.g. 6 months for hospitals). Add an expiry dashboard (expiring in 30/60/90 days, value at risk) and a two-click recall report (lot → customers, quantities, invoices). Print lot and expiry on invoices and delivery notes. Until then, change the template tagline.
findings.auditor: The tagline says 'batches and expiry' (templates.ts:59). The only date is 'EDA expiry' on the product (templates.ts:87), which is a registration expiry, and nothing in src/lib references eda_expiry. StockMove has no lot, serial or expiry (types.ts:33-41). Device serial is free text on Maintenance (templates.ts:104). Rated high, not critical: it is a missing vertical capability and a marketing misstatement, not data corruption. The tagline fix is effort S. Lot/expiry/FEFO is XL. The highlight 'EDA registration & expiry tracking' (templates.ts:64) is literally true as a field, but there are no alerts.

findings.title: 'Track stock' silently defaults to true while the form shows it unticked, so services companies can't invoice; turning it off later orphans stock and GL
findings.evidence: createRecord sets track_stock=true whenever the value is missing (engine.ts:229). The new-record form starts with values {} and renders the checkbox as checked={Boolean(value)} = unchecked (RecordPage.tsx:28, 209). For services answers, recommend.ts:152-156 only changes the help text to 'stock is off by default'. Probe on the realestate, services, education and blank templates (no Purchases module): a new 'Consulting' service fails to post with 'Not enough stock: Consulting (need 1, have 0)'. Toggle probe: with 10 on hand, setting track_stock=false is allowed (no guard). The next invoice posts no COGS and no stock move, GL 1300 keeps 600, and the item disappears from Inventory (filter at Inventory.tsx:11).
findings.impact: A first-day user in a service business gets a confusing stock error on their very first invoice, which hurts first-session activation. A product switched to untracked keeps an inventory balance that can never be relieved, and the books are permanently wrong.
findings.recommendation: Replace the checkbox with a product type (Stockable / Consumable / Service) shown as cards. Default it from onboarding answers (a.sells, a.inventory) and from whether a Purchases module exists. Show the real default in the form. Lock the type once movements exist and require a zeroing adjustment first. Add a health check: 'tracked products but no Purchases module'.
findings.auditor: Confirmed: track_stock defaults to true when undefined (engine.ts:229). The form starts from {} and renders the checkbox unchecked (RecordPage.tsx:28, 209). The services hint only changes help text (recommend.ts:152-156). Probe: a product created without track_stock fails to invoice with 'Not enough stock: P (need 1, have 0)' on realestate, services, education and blank. Correction: with default onboarding answers (purchasing: true, recommend.ts:47) those templates DO get a Purchases module via extraSpecs (recommend.ts:132-135), so 'no Purchases module' is only true when sells==='services'. Toggle probe confirmed: switching to untracked with 10 on hand leaves GL 1300 = 600 permanently, and later sales post COGS 0. Automations can also flip track_stock (engine.ts:656-660, see MISS-03).

findings.title: Procure-to-pay is only 'post a bill': no requisition, RFQ, PO, goods receipt, 3-way match or duplicate-bill control
findings.evidence: ModuleRole has suppliers and purchases only (roles.ts:80-93). Posting a purchase bill is the goods receipt itself: stock is increased inside postDocument (engine.ts:474-486). There is no GRNI (goods received not invoiced) account in CHART (types.ts:43-53). 'Supplier ref.' is plain non-unique text (roles.ts:246), so the same supplier invoice can be entered twice. There is no partial receipt, backorder or expected-delivery tracking.
findings.impact: The warehouse can't receive goods before the supplier's invoice arrives, which is the normal case. Nobody can compare what was ordered, received and billed, so over-billing and short deliveries go unnoticed. Without POs there's no open-commitment view or supplier on-time performance. Odoo, Zoho Inventory, BC and SAP B1 all ship PO → receipt → bill with matching as standard.
findings.recommendation: Add 'Purchase order' (approval by amount, sent to the supplier as PDF or WhatsApp) and 'Goods receipt' documents. The receipt posts Dr 1300 / Cr 2150 GRNI at the PO price and supports partial receipts and backorders. A bill created from the PO or receipt clears GRNI, flags quantity/price variances over a tolerance (e.g. 2%) for approval, and posts the price variance. Add a uniqueness rule on supplier + supplier_ref. Make requisition and RFQ optional steps that guided setup can switch on.
findings.auditor: Roles for purchasing are just suppliers and purchases. postDocument both receives goods and books AP (engine.ts:474-497). There is no GRNI account (types.ts:43-53). supplier_ref is plain non-unique text (roles.ts:246). There is no PO, partial receipt or matching. Also see MISS-04: even the receipt-by-bill can only be posted by finance.

findings.title: Order-to-cash goes straight from quote to invoice: no sales order, reservation, delivery note or partial delivery
findings.evidence: quoteToInvoice copies quote lines into a draft invoice (engine.ts:556-565) with no stock check or reservation. Stock leaves only when the invoice is posted (engine.ts:455-463). The distribution template's 'Orders pipeline' is a CRM deal pipeline (templates.ts:227) with no lines and no link to stock. There is no concept of committed or available quantity: the line editor shows only 'On hand' (RecordPage.tsx:285).
findings.impact: Distributors can't confirm an order, hold stock for it, pick and pack, ship partially and invoice what was delivered. Two reps can promise the same last units. Drivers have no delivery note for the customer to sign, which matters for B2B and tender deliveries to hospitals.
findings.recommendation: Add a 'Sales order' document that reserves stock (available = on hand - reserved) and a 'Delivery note' that moves stock (Dr COGS / Cr Inventory, or to a 'goods delivered not invoiced' account) with partial delivery and a printable form with signature and lot lines. 'Invoice from deliveries' then bills what was shipped. Show On hand / Reserved / Available on product pages and in line pickers. Keep the existing quote → invoice shortcut for simple shops behind a 'simple mode' switch.
findings.auditor: quoteToInvoice (engine.ts:556-565) copies lines with no stock check or reservation. Stock leaves only on invoice posting. The distribution 'Orders pipeline' is a deals module (templates.ts:227) with no lines. The line editor shows only 'On hand' (RecordPage.tsx:285). Also, the distribution template's 'Credit limit' field is never enforced (see MISS-05).

findings.title: Single location only: no warehouses, bins, transfers or van stock
findings.evidence: StockMove {id, product, qty, cost, doc, ref, date} has no location (types.ts:33-41). onHand sums across everything (engine.ts:419-421). The distribution template has a 'Route' field on customers (templates.ts:226) but no van or route stock. The README lists 'multiple warehouses' under next steps.
findings.impact: Most target SMEs (a distributor with a main store plus branch, or van sales; a water-treatment firm with site stock; a contractor with materials on site) can't see where stock is, transfer it, or count one store at a time. This rules them out against Odoo, Zoho Inventory and Daftra, which all handle multiple warehouses.
findings.recommendation: Add warehouse and location (and optional bin) to moves and documents, a default warehouse per user or role, and a 'Transfer' document (with optional in-transit state). Show per-warehouse on hand on the product and Inventory screens, with a warehouse filter. Let the builder show warehouses as cards with capacity and value. Model van sales as a warehouse per rep, loaded and unloaded by transfer.
findings.auditor: StockMove has no location (types.ts:33-41). onHand sums all moves (engine.ts:419-421). Route is just a customer select (templates.ts:226). README.md:97 lists multiple warehouses as next. Accurate.

findings.title: No units of measure or conversions, and quantities are rounded to 2 decimals while the GL keeps the full value
findings.evidence: 'Unit' is a free select field (roles.ts:218) that no Line or engine code reads (types.ts:7-15). onHand applies round2 (engine.ts:420) and stock moves store qty unrounded. Probe: receive 1.2345 kg @100. onHand shows 1.23 while GL 1300 = 123.45.
findings.impact: Buying in cartons of 24 and selling in pieces, or buying a drum in litres and issuing in ml, can't be modelled. Users invent duplicate SKUs or do conversions in their heads, and stock is wrong. Chemical, pharma and food businesses (the water and medical templates) need 3-4 decimal quantities.
findings.recommendation: Add UoM categories (unit, weight, volume, length, time) with a base unit, purchase and sales units, and a conversion factor per product. Lines get a UoM, converted to the base unit in moves. Quantity precision is set per UoM (0-4 decimals). Show 'Carton (24 pcs)' in pickers, and print UoM on documents (needed for ETA unitType codes).
findings.auditor: Probe: receive 1.2345 @100 gives onHand 1.23 while the move qty is 1.2345 and GL 1300 = 123.45. Worse than stated: the oversell check compares the rounded onHand (1.23) with the requested qty (engine.ts:446), so the user cannot sell the full 1.2345 kg they bought. Unit is a free select (roles.ts:218) that no engine code reads. The UoM-conversion gap is a competitive gap (high). The precision part alone would be medium.

findings.title: The manufacturing template promises 'Raw vs finished stock' and 'Production orders', but production never moves stock
findings.evidence: The highlights read ['Raw vs finished stock', 'Production orders', …] (templates.ts:291). The production order is a plain custom module (item, quantity, status select) (templates.ts:297-305). The engine posts only invoices and purchases (engine.ts:427). There is no BOM, component consumption, finished-goods receipt or WIP account.
findings.impact: Raw material stock only ever goes up and finished goods only ever go down, so the valuation is meaningless. The marketing promise fails in the first week of use.
findings.recommendation: Add a BOM (components, qty per unit, scrap %) and a postable Production order. Completing it consumes components at their moving-average cost and receives finished goods at the rolled-up cost (plus optional labour or overhead), posting through 1350 WIP. The builder should let a user drag components onto a BOM card. Until this ships, remove or soften the highlight.
findings.auditor: The production order is a plain custom module (templates.ts:297-305) and the engine posts only invoices and bills (engine.ts:426), so production never moves stock. Confirmed. Overstated part: 'Raw vs finished stock' is partly delivered as a classification. Items have an 'Item type' select (Raw material / Semi-finished / Finished good / Packaging, templates.ts:296), so the split can be reported. It just can't transform. The core critique stands: raw materials can only leave stock by being invoiced.

findings.title: No landed costs, customs or foreign-currency purchases, so import costs aren't capitalised as IAS 2.11 requires
findings.evidence: Purchase bill lines without a tracked product post to 5100 'Purchased services & expenses' (engine.ts:493). Freight, customs duty and clearance on a separate bill therefore become expenses and never enter item cost. Bills have no currency or exchange rate (roles.ts:241-247; company.currency is used everywhere). Import VAT paid at customs has no separate path.
findings.impact: Importers, who make up a large share of Egyptian distributors and medical suppliers, understate inventory cost and margin, overstate expense in the month of import, and get wrong margins per item. Pricing decisions are made on false costs.
findings.recommendation: Add a 'Landed cost' document that links one or more cost bills (freight, duty, clearance, insurance) to a receipt or bill and allocates them by value, quantity or weight into item cost (Dr 1300 / Cr the cost-bill clearing account), then re-averages. Add document currency and exchange rate on supplier bills, with realised FX on payment, and an import VAT line type.
findings.auditor: Non-tracked or free-text bill lines go to 5100 (engine.ts:477-478, 493). Bills have no currency or rate field (roles.ts:241-247). The currency is locked company-wide once anything is posted (SettingsTab.tsx:23-26). The IAS 2.11 reference is correct: costs of purchase include import duties and transport.

findings.title: Inventory reporting is a snapshot plus the last 40 moves: no stock card, valuation as of a date, movement, slow-moving or ABC analysis
findings.evidence: Inventory.tsx:15 shows ws.data.stock.slice(0, 40) with no filter, search or product drill-down. The report builder (reports.ts:33-38) works only on module records, so ws.data.stock can't be reported on. The only stock report pack is 'Stock on hand' grouped by name (packs.ts:52). The product record page shows no movement ledger (relatedRecords, RecordPage.tsx:177-185, follows relation fields only, not document lines).
findings.impact: Owners can't answer the basic questions: what is dead stock, what sells fastest, how many days of cover do I have, what was the stock value at 31 Dec (needed for year-end and tax filing), and why is this SKU short. Zoho Inventory, Odoo and Cin7 all ship these reports out of the box.
findings.recommendation: Add (1) a stock card per product: running balance, cost and value with document links, filterable by date and warehouse; (2) valuation as of any date; (3) an inventory analytics dashboard with an ABC (value) and XYZ (variability) matrix, days on hand, turnover, a dead or slow stock list (no sale in N days) with value, a stock ageing heatmap, an expiry-risk bar and a stock-vs-GL reconciliation tile; (4) expose stock moves as a virtual 'Stock movements' source in the report builder so users can drag product, warehouse, month and reason fields.
findings.auditor: Inventory.tsx:15 shows stock.slice(0,40) with no filter. runReport only iterates module records (reports.ts:33-35). The stock pack is the single 'Stock on hand' table (packs.ts:52). relatedRecords follows relation fields only (RecordPage.tsx:177-185), so a product page has no stock card. Accurate.

findings.title: Reordering is one threshold, alerts only fire when an invoice is posted, and they go to the person who posted it
findings.evidence: reorderAlert reads a single reorder_level (engine.ts:694-706) and is called only from invoice posting (engine.ts:462). It isn't called after a bill void, an adjustment or a change to the level. The task goes to ctx.user.id, the poster, usually finance (engine.ts:704), not purchasing. There is no max level or reorder quantity, no lead time, no preferred supplier on the product (roles.ts:208-219), and no suggested purchase.
findings.impact: Stock-outs are found late and the alert lands with the wrong person. The buyer still has to work out what to order and from whom by hand. SAP MM and Odoo offer min/max rules with automatic draft POs, and Zoho has reorder points with a preferred vendor.
findings.recommendation: Add min, max (or reorder qty), safety stock, lead time and preferred supplier with last purchase price to products. Recalculate after every move. Route alerts to a 'Purchasing' role. Add a 'Replenishment' screen listing suggested quantities = max - available - on order, with one click to create draft POs grouped by supplier. Later, an AI forecast from sales velocity and seasonality (Ramadan, summer) can suggest the min/max values.
findings.auditor: reorderAlert is called only from invoice posting (engine.ts:462). The task is assigned to ctx.user.id (engine.ts:704). Products have only reorder_level (roles.ts:217). Additional detail: the notification is added on every qualifying invoice with no dedupe (engine.ts:702); only the task is de-duplicated. So notes pile up.

findings.title: Cost is rounded to 2 decimals on every receipt, so valuation drifts from the GL with no reconciliation
findings.evidence: p.values.cost = round2(...) (engine.ts:483), the move cost is round2(unitCost) (engine.ts:484), and COGS = q * rounded cost (engine.ts:459). Probe: receipts 3@10, 7@10.01, 11@9.37, then 20 single-unit sales. Result: 1 unit left, valued 9.67 in stock and 9.74 in the GL. With thousands of SKUs and moves the gap grows and nothing reports it.
findings.impact: Small differences between the stock valuation and the trial balance that nobody can explain. Accountants have to post manual true-ups, which the product doesn't support (SUPP-02).
findings.recommendation: Track inventory value per item, not only unit cost: keep value and qty, average = value/qty. Store cost with 4-6 decimals and round only the journal amounts. When the last unit leaves, relieve the exact remaining value so qty 0 means value 0. Add the stock-vs-GL check from SUPP-05 to the validator and the health check.
findings.auditor: Probe reproduced it exactly: 1 unit left, 9.67 in stock vs 9.74 in GL. Cost is round2 at engine.ts:483, and the move cost is round2 at 484. Correctly rated.

findings.title: Stock posting ignores dates: backdated sales before receipt are allowed, there's no period lock, and voids are dated today
findings.evidence: onHand ignores StockMove.date (engine.ts:419-421), so availability is checked against all-time stock. Probe: bill dated 2026-03-01, then invoice dated 2026-01-01. It posts with no error. Moving average follows posting order, not date order. voidDocument uses todayISO() (engine.ts:513). company.fiscalYearStart exists (recommend.ts:171) but nothing locks closed periods.
findings.impact: Stock and COGS for past months change after reports or VAT returns were filed. Valuation as of a date can't be trusted, and month-end close (a core accounting control) doesn't exist.
findings.recommendation: Check availability as of the document date. Add a 'lock date' (period close) in company settings that blocks posting or voiding on or before it, with an admin override that is logged. Let the user pick the void date (default the original date if the period is open), and warn when a document is backdated more than N days.
findings.auditor: Probe: bill dated 2026-03-01, then invoice dated 2026-01-01 posts fine (onHand 8). onHand ignores dates (engine.ts:419-421). Void uses todayISO() (engine.ts:513). fiscalYearStart exists (recommend.ts:171, SettingsTab.tsx:29-33) but nothing reads it for locking. Also, automations can rewrite a posted document's date after posting (MISS-03), which makes this worse.

findings.title: No barcode or GS1 support, and the line picker is a plain dropdown of every product
findings.evidence: 'Barcode' is an optional text field only in the distribution template (templates.ts:229). Nothing validates a GTIN check digit, enforces uniqueness or prints labels. LinesEditor uses a <select> of all products (RecordPage.tsx:280-283) with no search, scan input or keyboard-first entry.
findings.impact: At 500-5,000 SKUs a storekeeper or cashier can't find items quickly, and receiving or counting without a scanner is slow and error-prone. Every modern inventory app (Zoho, Odoo barcode, Square) scans with the phone camera.
findings.recommendation: Make barcode or GTIN a system field on products with uniqueness and GS1 check-digit validation, plus several barcodes per UoM (piece vs carton GTIN). Replace the select with a type-ahead combobox that accepts scanner input (Enter adds a line, scanning again adds +1). Add camera scanning (BarcodeDetector API) for receiving and counting on mobile, and label printing (GS1-128 with lot and expiry AIs for medical).
findings.auditor: Barcode is a plain text field only in distribution (templates.ts:229). The LinesEditor is a native <select> of all products (RecordPage.tsx:280-283). Accurate.

findings.title: Weak P2P controls: one finance role creates suppliers, posts bills and pays them, payments need no approval, and the supplier master is minimal
findings.evidence: The finance pack gives ALL rights on purchases and suppliers (packs.ts:105). registerPayment is gated only by canPost (engine.ts:530) and approvals cover only 'post' and 'stage' (engine.ts:715). The default approval is only for bills over 100,000 (packs.ts:171). Suppliers have only name, phone, e-mail and tax ID (roles.ts:234-239): no bank account, payment terms, currency, lead time or category, and no audited bank-detail changes.
findings.impact: A single employee can set up a fake supplier, post a bill and pay it, which is the classic AP fraud that segregation of duties (SoD) exists to prevent. Due dates are always +30 days (engine.ts:236) instead of the supplier's agreed terms.
findings.recommendation: Add supplier fields for payment terms (driving due date), bank/IBAN with an approval required to change it, currency, lead time and an approved/blocked status (no bills on unapproved suppliers). Add a payment approval rule type and a 'Payment run' screen (select due bills, approve, export bank file or mark paid). Add an SoD check to the health check that warns when the same role can create suppliers, post bills and pay.
findings.auditor: Finance has ALL on purchases and suppliers (packs.ts:105). registerPayment checks only canPost (engine.ts:530). Approvals only cover post and stage. Supplier fields are minimal (roles.ts:234-239). The due date is +30 (engine.ts:236). Correction: the default 'Large purchase > 100,000' approval is created only if a non-admin role whose name matches /manag|owner|director|مدير/ exists (packs.ts:166-171). Many workspaces will have no approval rule at all, which makes SoD weaker than the panel states.

findings.title: Free-text purchase lines skip inventory, and the first purchase price defaults to the selling price
findings.evidence: LinesEditor offers '— free text —' on every document (RecordPage.tsx:281). A product bought as free text posts to 5100 expense and stock never increases (engine.ts:477, 493). On a purchase bill the price pre-fills with p.values.cost || p.values.price (RecordPage.tsx:263), and cost is 0 for new products (engine.ts:256), so the first bill is pre-filled at the selling price.
findings.impact: Clerks who type 'Membrane 8040' instead of picking the product create invisible stock and expensed inventory. The next invoice is blocked for 'not enough stock' or forces negative stock. Accepting the pre-filled selling price inflates the first average cost.
findings.recommendation: On purchase bills, allow free text only for non-stock lines (choose an expense category), and warn when the text matches an existing product name or SKU. Pre-fill with the last purchase price from that supplier, otherwise leave it empty and require a value. Add an 'Uncategorised purchases' check to the health check.
findings.auditor: '— free text —' is offered on every document (RecordPage.tsx:281). The purchase price prefill is cost||price (RecordPage.tsx:263), and cost is 0 on new products, so the first bill is pre-filled at the selling price. Free-text lines go to 5100 (engine.ts:477-478, 493).

findings.title: Moving average is the only valuation method, with no FIFO and no NRV or obsolescence write-down
findings.evidence: Costing is hard-coded to moving average in postDocument (engine.ts:479-483). There's no company setting for the method and no provision account in CHART (types.ts:43-53). There's no way to write stock down to net realisable value for expired or damaged goods.
findings.impact: Weighted average is acceptable under IAS 2 and EAS 2. But businesses with expiring goods or volatile import prices often need FIFO, and IAS 2.9 requires a lower-of-cost-and-NRV review. Without it, expired medical stock stays on the balance sheet at full cost.
findings.recommendation: Make the valuation method a company setting (Average or FIFO), chosen at setup and locked after the first move, with a FIFO layer table per item, by lot when lots exist. Add an 'Inventory write-down' adjustment reason posting to a 1310 provision account. Suggest write-downs automatically from expiry and slow-moving analysis (SUPP-15).
findings.auditor: Moving average is hard-coded (engine.ts:479-483) and there is no provision account (types.ts:43-53). The NRV/write-down gap (IAS 2.9, 2.28-2.33) is real and matters for expiring medical stock. Overstated: weighted average is fully IAS 2.25 / EAS 2 compliant, and FIFO is not 'needed' for expiring goods. FEFO is a physical picking rule tied to lots (SUPP-07), not a cost-flow method. FIFO as an option is a nice-to-have (low). The NRV write-down is the medium part.

findings.title: Sample data (on by default) is posted into the live books using the company's real product names, uses up the gapless numbers, and the promised 'remove from Settings' does not exist
findings.evidence: Suggest.tsx:17 defaults sample=true, and Suggest.tsx:97 promises 'Remove it any time from Settings.' On first publish, Builder.tsx:63-68 calls seedSampleData with names taken from w.answers.products, which is the user's real catalog. seed.ts:150-176 creates and POSTS 2 purchase bills and up to 12 invoices with registerPayment, so real stock moves, journals, payments and BILL/INV-YYYY-0001.. sequences are written into ws.data. SettingsTab.tsx (whole file) has no remove-sample function, and no function in src does it. The data can't be undone manually either: paid documents can't be voided (engine.ts:512, RecordPage.tsx:85), posted documents can't be deleted (engine.ts:288), and products with movements can't be deleted (engine.ts:289).
findings.impact: A new company that accepts the defaults goes live with invented stock quantities and average costs on its real products, a fake AR/AP/VAT history, and its first real invoice numbered after the sample ones (e.g. INV-2026-0013). That breaks gapless numbering for ETA. Nothing can clean it up, so the books are wrong from day one and the only fix is a new workspace.
findings.recommendation: Seed sample data into a separate demo workspace, or tag every seeded record, move, journal, payment and user with demo:true. Add a 'Remove sample data' button in Settings (and a banner on the Dashboard while sample data is present) that deletes all tagged rows and resets sequences. Block posting real documents until the sample data is removed, or until the user confirms keeping it. Never seed against the user's typed product names.

findings.title: Voiding a bill while stock remains positive can make the average cost negative and post negative-amount journal lines
findings.area: Engine / void purchase bill / journal guard
findings.evidence: voidDocument re-averages with (q*cost - mv.qty*mv.cost)/remaining whenever remaining>0 (engine.ts:516-520), with no floor. journal() only checks that debits equal credits and accepts negative amounts (engine.ts:406-411). Probe: bill 10@10, bill 10@100 (avg 55), sell 5, void the second bill. Result: onHand 5, avg cost -35, GL 1300 = -175. The next invoice of 2 posts lines {5000 debit -70} and {1300 credit -70}, and COGS falls to 205. SUPP-01's proposed 'block if onHand < 0' guard would not catch this case.
findings.impact: Products show negative cost and margins above 100%. COGS is reduced by phantom credits. The journal contains negative debit and credit lines that no accounting standard or export (ETA, auditors, Excel to accountant) accepts. It happens after an ordinary 'wrong bill, void it' action.
findings.recommendation: In voidDocument for purchases, refuse when any product's current onHand is less than the bill's received qty ('Part of this bill was already sold. Use a purchase return.'). Clamp cost to >= 0 as a safety net. Make journal() throw on any negative debit or credit and auto-swap sides for legitimate reversals. Add engine tests for void after partial consumption across two cost layers.

findings.title: Automations' 'Set field' action changes posted invoices and bills (date, due date) and products' Track stock, bypassing the posted-document lock
findings.evidence: updateRecord blocks edits to posted documents (engine.ts:266). The workflow executor writes rec.values = cleanValues(...) directly for any non-readOnly field (engine.ts:656-660), and postDocument fires runWorkflows(ctx, rec, 'updated') right after posting (engine.ts:505). AutomationsTab.tsx:144 lets users pick any non-readOnly, non-relation field, which includes Invoice date, Due date, Bill date and Track stock. Probe: workflow 'Invoices updated → set date 2020-01-01, due date 2030-01-01'. After posting, the invoice shows date 2020-01-01 and due 2030-01-01 while its journal stays dated 2026-01-11.
findings.impact: The document date no longer matches the GL date, ETA submission date and VAT period. AR/AP ageing can be hidden by pushing due dates out. A product automation can silently turn off stock tracking and leave inventory stuck on the balance sheet (as in SUPP-08). The 'posted documents are locked' guardrail can be bypassed without code.
findings.recommendation: In execute(), skip set_field when the record is a document with status !== 'draft', or route it through updateRecord so the same lock applies. Mark date, due_date, supplier, customer and track_stock as 'locked after posting / after first movement' in the role field definitions. Hide them in the Automations field picker for document and product modules. Log a 'blocked by guardrail' note when this happens.

findings.title: Only finance can move stock: storekeepers and operations can draft bills but can never receive or issue goods
findings.evidence: postDocument and voidDocument require canPost, which is role.admin || role.finance (engine.ts:35-38, 425, 510). The 'operations' team preset gets RW on products, purchases and suppliers but finance:false (packs.ts:104, 114). No permission separates the physical receipt from the financial booking, and the RecordPage Post button is hidden for non-finance users (RecordPage.tsx:81).
findings.impact: In a real warehouse the storekeeper receives goods when they arrive, and finance books the bill later. Here every receipt waits for an accountant, so stock is understated for days, sales are blocked by 'Not enough stock', and companies will give finance rights to storekeepers, which breaks segregation of duties the other way.
findings.recommendation: Add a separate 'stock' permission (receive, deliver, count, transfer) distinct from 'post to ledger'. Once Goods receipt and Delivery note documents exist (SUPP-09/10), let operations roles post those, with GRNI or interim accounts, while bills, invoices and payments stay finance-only. In Access (Roles tab), show a clear matrix 'Can move stock / Can post to accounts / Can pay'.

findings.title: The distribution template's 'Credit limit' is never enforced on quotes, invoices or deliveries
findings.evidence: credit_limit is defined only at templates.ts:226, and grep finds no other reference in src. postDocument (engine.ts:423-506) checks stock and approvals but not customer exposure (open AR + this invoice). The customer record shows no available-credit indicator.
findings.impact: Distributors, the template's main audience, are given a field that looks like a control but does nothing. Reps keep shipping to customers who are over their limit or overdue, which is exactly the 'late collections' problem the onboarding asks about. Odoo, BC and SAP B1 all warn or block on credit limit.
findings.recommendation: Make credit_limit a system field on accounts when invoices exist. On invoice post (and later on sales order confirm), compute open balance + document total.
