Above the limit (or with invoices more than N days overdue), block with 'Over credit limit by EGP X: ask a manager to approve', handled by an approval rule type. Show a credit gauge (used / limit / overdue) on the customer page and in the line editor header.

findings.title: Any workspace member can rewrite stock, costs and journals directly, because every guardrail runs in the browser
findings.evidence: The RLS policy 'members save their workspace' allows UPDATE of the whole workspaces.doc for any member (supabase/migrations: for update using private.is_member(id) with check private.is_member(id)). canPost, the oversell check, the posted-document lock and the gapless sequences are enforced only in engine.ts in the client (engine.ts:35-38, 445-448, 266, 399-404). A sales-role user with read-only product access can send a supabase.from('workspaces').update({doc}) from devtools that edits ws.data.stock, ws.data.journal or product cost.
findings.impact: Stock levels, inventory valuation and the GL can be altered without any trace by a user who has no posting or edit rights. That defeats segregation of duties and audit trails (OWASP ASVS V4 access control, and IFRS audit evidence). For warehouses it allows theft to be hidden by editing stock moves.
findings.recommendation: Move stock moves, journal lines, payments and sequences into their own tables written only by SECURITY DEFINER RPCs or Edge Functions that re-check role permissions and stock (same as SUPP-06). Restrict the doc column update to admins, or to schema and non-ledger data only. Add an append-only audit table. Until then, at least add a server-side trigger that rejects doc updates which change data.journal or data.stock entries that already existed.

strengths: Business rules are enforced in the engine, not only the UI: stage gates, validation rules, required and conditional fields, permissions, and approvals that become invalid when the record changes and can't be self-approved (engine.ts:307-311, 186-212, 715-761).
Every UI action runs in an atomic transaction (transact plus structuredClone), so a failed move or conversion leaves nothing half-done (store.ts:97-106, useApp.ts:34-43).

The pipeline validator matches what good CRM admins enforce by hand: exactly one Won and one Lost stage, open stages first, Won probability 100 and Lost 0, monotonic probability warnings, and gates that reference existing fields (validate.ts:204-226).
Per-stage deal rotting in the Pipedrive style, with idle-day badges on cards and records, plus lead scoring and a weighted forecast out of the box (engine.ts:152-160, packs.ts:128-161).

Vertical templates show real domain insight: a tender pipeline with a tender-number gate and bid bond, EDA registration and expiry, rep visits, a site-survey-to-project flow, unit and reservation, Egyptian governorates, and Saturday-first calendars (templates.ts, ModuleView.tsx:237).
Quote → invoice in one click carries lines over, and the CRM is tied to real books: posted invoices drive receivables, VAT, stock and ageing, which point CRMs like Pipedrive or monday can't match.

CSV import auto-matches columns (including Arabic), validates each row like a form save, and returns a per-row error report, with Arabic 'نعم' accepted for checkboxes (ImportModal.tsx, engine.ts:785-852).
Automations can't loop, because actions never re-trigger, and every automation run is written to the activity feed (engine.ts:632-670).

scorecard.rationale: Lead → deal → quote → invoice → payment runs end to end in the engine, with atomic transactions. But probes show broken links in the chain: conversion duplicates accounts and creates EGP 1 deals, stage gates are bypassed by skipping stages, quotes are never numbered and declined quotes can be invoiced, tasks aren't linked to records, history is lost after 500 events, and concurrent edits are discarded. Capture (forms, WhatsApp, e-mail), dedupe, assignment, activities, SLA and e-sign are missing.

Pipeline setup logic is solid (exactly one Won and one Lost stage, open stages first, probability warnings, gates and rotting, references checked before delete). Several defaults are illogical, though: gates aren't cumulative, the funnel includes Won and Lost, 'Deals won' is all-time though the fix promises this month, workflow conditions on lookups never match, discount approval can't be configured on quotes, and the credit limit field is never enforced.

Against Pipedrive, HubSpot Starter, Zoho CRM and Odoo CRM, Bonyan wins on guided vertical templates and the built-in link from CRM to books. It loses on what drives buying decisions: omnichannel capture (WhatsApp is the key local channel), activities and timeline, forecasting and quotas, record-level security, mobile and offline, quote PDF and e-sign, real-time multi-user, and Arabic UI. Against local players such as Daftra, the lack of Arabic and ETA e-invoicing is decisive.

Simplicity is a real strength. Onboarding builds a working CRM, the screens are uncluttered, and terms are plain language. Simplicity is partly from missing depth (no activities, no forecasting UI), and some flows push complexity onto users, such as convert-then-fix-duplicates, window.prompt for views, and the mention syntax.

Custom modules, fields, lookups, rollups, validation rules, gates, scoring and automations give good flexibility under guardrails. Gaps that limit building a real CRM: no multi-relation or polymorphic relation (so no activities or stakeholder roles), no record-level sharing, automations limited to 3 actions, and no per-quote approval type.

Automations exist but are limited (3 actions, run in the browser when the app opens, lookup conditions broken). There is no AI: no next-best-action, deal-risk summary, duplicate suggestion, call or WhatsApp summarization, or pipeline diagnosis. The health check validates schema, not data or process health.

vision: A world-class Bonyan CRM for Egyptian, and then global, SMEs should feel like Pipedrive's simplicity with HubSpot's timeline and Odoo's link to the books, Arabic-first. Leads flow in without typing: a WhatsApp Business inbox, hosted web forms with UTM tracking, Meta Lead Ads, and e-mail BCC. Each lead is matched against normalized phone numbers, offered as a merge when it's a duplicate, and assigned round-robin or by governorate in seconds, with a 'call within 15 minutes' SLA clock on the card. Every record has one unified timeline across its account, contacts, deals, quotes, invoices, payments and tickets, with one-tap 'Log call', 'WhatsApp' and 'Schedule next step', and deals without a next step are flagged in red. Stage gates are cumulative, Won and Lost ask for reason and competitor, and the conversion and win/loss dashboards read straight from stage history. Quotes are numbered and versioned, built from price lists, held for approval when the discount or margin crosses a role's limit, and sent as a bilingual branded PDF link the customer can accept and e-sign. Acceptance marks the deal Won and starts the invoice and the installment or warranty schedule. Managers get a live forecast by close month (commit, best case, pipeline) against each rep's quota, a pacing gauge, and stage-conversion and velocity analytics. Reps see only their own and their team's records, and export is a separately granted, logged permission. Field reps use an offline-capable PWA with a 'My day' screen, GPS check-in on visits, and a swipeable board. An AI copilot reviews the pipeline every morning ('7 deals worth EGP 1.2M have no next step; 3 quotes expire this week; Ahmed's Cairo leads convert at half the team rate because first contact takes 2 days') and offers one-click fixes: create the tasks, reassign, or draft the WhatsApp follow-up in Arabic.

findings.title: Two reps saving at the same time lose work silently, and nobody sees colleagues' changes live
findings.area: Cloud store / multi-user pipeline (all CRM screens)
findings.evidence: src/lib/store.ts:56-72: each save rewrites the whole workspace JSON with `.eq('version', version)`. When another user saved first (`data.length === 0`), the code calls `reload(ws.id)` (store.ts:141-149), which replaces local state with the server copy and sets `dirty=false`. The local edit is thrown away. The only signal is a small amber 'Reloaded latest' pill (Shell.tsx:87-89). There is no realtime subscription anywhere, so a rep's board and records stay stale until their next save conflicts.
findings.impact: A 10-rep team moves cards, logs notes and edits deals all day, and every overlapping 600 ms save window drops one person's change: a moved deal, a new lead, a logged call. Reps stop trusting the CRM and go back to WhatsApp and Excel. Salesforce, HubSpot, Pipedrive and Zoho all save per record and update other users live.
findings.recommendation: Move CRM records out of the single doc into per-record rows (records table keyed by workspace and module, with RLS), with per-record optimistic versions and field-level merge. Subscribe to Supabase Realtime so boards and record pages update live and show 'Sara is editing'. On a real conflict, show a merge dialog ('Your value / Their value') instead of discarding. Until then, at least replay the failed local transaction on top of the reloaded version and toast 'Your change was re-applied'.
findings.auditor: Checked store.ts:47-75 and 141-149. flush() sets dirty=false before the await (line 53). When the update matches 0 rows it calls reload(), which overwrites the local workspace and sets dirty=false again. So the losing user's edit is dropped, along with anything they typed while the save was in flight. The only signal is the amber 'Reloaded latest' pill (Shell.tsx:87-89). There is no realtime channel anywhere in src. The panel actually understates this: the doc holds the whole workspace (schema, books, notes, activity), so any two users editing anything collide, not only two reps on the same deal. Critical is the right rating.

findings.title: Record history and audit trail are wiped after 500 events across the whole workspace
findings.evidence: engine.ts:216-219 `log()` unshifts into one global `ws.data.activity` array and truncates it to 500 (`if (ctx.ws.data.activity.length > 500) ctx.ws.data.activity.length = 500`). Field history ('Amount: EGP 100 → EGP 250', engine.ts:275-278), stage moves, conversions, approvals and payments all go only to this array. RecordPage.tsx:52 reads a record's history from it. Probe: after 600 edits to one account, the lead's history held 0 entries (total stayed 500).
findings.impact: The README sells 'Field history (Salesforce)', but in a busy team a deal's history disappears within days. Managers can't answer 'who changed the amount, or moved this to Won?' Disputes over commissions and audits can't be resolved. Win-loss and stage-duration analytics have nothing to work from (stageHistory survives, but who and why does not).
findings.recommendation: Store an append-only, per-record audit log (its own table, or at least a per-record array with no global cap) holding the user, timestamp, field, old and new value, and source (UI, import, automation). Keep the global feed as a capped view only. Show a full, filterable History tab on each record, and keep field-history retention at 18 months or more, as Salesforce does.
findings.auditor: engine.ts:216-219 keeps one global array capped at 500. updateRecord's field history (275-278), moveStage, approvals and payments write only to that array. RecordPage.tsx:52 filters it per record and shows only 15 entries. execute() at engine.ts:669 unshifts without truncating, but the next log() call cuts the array back to 500. Downgraded to high: the books are safe (journal, stock and payments are separate arrays without a cap), comments are not capped, and stageHistory survives. What is lost is the who/what/when of CRM field changes. Serious for a product that sells field history, but no wrong books or loss of business data.

findings.title: Lead conversion creates duplicate customers and EGP 1 'placeholder' deals, and skips gates and automations
findings.evidence: engine.ts:329-348 `convertLead` always creates a new account (line 338) without searching existing accounts. The probe, with 'Kasr Al Ainy' already existing, ended with two 'Kasr Al Ainy' accounts. Deal amount is `Number(lead.values.budget ?? 0) || 1` (line 340), so every lead without a budget (all templates except real estate) becomes an EGP 1 deal, which passes the 'amount > 0' rule (packs.ts:164) and the amount stage gates. The lead stage is set directly (lines 342-345), skipping moveStage, its gates, approvals and `runWorkflows`, and updatedAt isn't touched. There is no lead→account/deal back-link (no `links`), lead `source` isn't copied to the account or deal, and the user can't choose 'attach to existing account' or 'don't create a deal'.
findings.impact: Duplicate customers split the 360 view, receivables and rollups. EGP 1 deals pollute pipeline value, the weighted forecast and win rate. Source-to-revenue attribution, the main question an Egyptian SME running Facebook and WhatsApp ads asks, is impossible because source is lost at conversion. Salesforce, HubSpot and Zoho all show a conversion dialog with duplicate matching.
findings.recommendation: Build a conversion dialog: (1) suggested matching accounts and contacts by normalized phone, e-mail and fuzzy company name, with 'Use existing' or 'Create new'; (2) an optional deal with required amount and close date, or 'no deal yet'; (3) carry over source, campaign, owner and notes. Write `converted_to` links on the lead, show 'Converted from lead X' on the deal, and run the move through moveStage so gates and workflows fire. Remove the `|| 1` hack.
findings.auditor: engine.ts:329-348 confirmed. It always creates a new account (338) with no matching, uses `|| 1` for the amount (340), and sets the lead stage directly with no gate, approval, workflow or updatedAt (342-345). It also skips need(edit) on the lead itself. Source, links and notes are not carried over. The deal's createRecord is not silent, so the deal's 'created' workflows do fire; only the lead's stage_changed path is skipped. A deal amount of 1 passes the deals rule `amount gt 0` (packs.ts:164) and checkGate, which treats only 0 or empty as missing (engine.ts:309).

findings.title: Stage gates can be bypassed by skipping stages; no lost reason and no exit criteria
findings.evidence: engine.ts:307-311 `checkGate` checks only the target stage's `requires`. moveStage (313-327) allows jumping to any stage. Probe on the medical template: moving to 'Technical offer' failed ('fill in: Tender no.'), but moving straight to 'Financial offer', then 'Awarded', then 'Won' succeeded with no tender number and an amount of EGP 1. The Lost stages in roles.ts:163 and every template have no requirement, there is no lost-reason field anywhere (grep finds it only in a test), and the RecordPage stage path (RecordPage.tsx:95-106) moves on one click with no confirmation.
findings.impact: The 'guardrails keep it correct' promise breaks on the main sales object. Tender pipelines can show Won with no tender number. Without lost reasons, win/loss analysis (why we lose to competitor X on price) is impossible. Salesforce Path and HubSpot required-properties-per-stage enforce gates cumulatively, and Pipedrive asks for a lost reason by default.
findings.recommendation: Make gates cumulative: entering stage N requires every `requires` of open stages ≤ N. Add an option to forbid skipping more than one stage without a manager role. Add system 'Lost reason' (select: Price, Competitor, No budget, Timing, No response, Other) and 'Competitor' fields to the deals role, required on entering the Lost stage. Moving to Won or Lost opens a small modal that collects them. Add a validator warning when the Won stage has no gates.
findings.auditor: checkGate (engine.ts:307-311) checks only the target stage's requires, and moveStage (313-327) allows any jump. The medical template puts tender_no only on 'Technical offer' (templates.ts:79), so moving from Tender announced straight to Financial offer or Won skips it. No stage in roles.ts:140-164 or the templates requires anything on Lost, and no lost-reason field exists. The stage path moves on a single click (RecordPage.tsx:100). Caveat for the recommendation: purely cumulative gates would be wrong for the medical 'Type = Direct order' deals, which have no tender number. Gates need conditions (showIf-style), not only accumulation.

findings.title: Quotation lifecycle is incomplete: no numbering, no accept step, declined or expired quotes can be invoiced, and quotes can be edited after invoicing
findings.evidence: Quote numbers come only from `nextNumber` inside postDocument (engine.ts:452), and quotes are never posted (engine.ts:427). recordTitle shows `Draft · Customer` (engine.ts:64) and the print shows 'DRAFT' (RecordPage.tsx:351). Probe: `quote number undefined`. The status 'accepted' exists (types.ts:4) but nothing sets it. RecordPage offers only Mark sent, Accept & invoice, and Declined (RecordPage.tsx:72-78). quoteToInvoice (engine.ts:557-565) checks only `status === 'invoiced'`; probe: a declined quote was invoiced, and `valid_until` is never checked. updateRecord exempts quotes from the posted lock (engine.ts:267), so an invoiced quote's header was edited in the probe. Quotes have no deal link, so a deal's amount never syncs from its quote. There are no revisions (Q-0001 rev 2), no shareable link, no e-signature, and the 'PDF' is window.print (RecordPage.tsx:340).
findings.impact: Customers in Egypt (especially hospitals and government tenders) need a numbered, dated, versioned offer. Today every printed quotation says DRAFT. Sales can't tell which version the customer accepted, and an invoice can come from a rejected or expired offer. HubSpot Quotes, Zoho, Odoo and Pipedrive Smart Docs all number and version quotes, link them to the deal, and support online accept or e-sign.
findings.recommendation: Give quotes their own gapless numbering when first sent (QT-2026-0001), with revision suffixes, and lock a sent revision ('Revise' clones it to rev+1). Add a deal relation on quotes: create from the deal, sync primary quote total to deal amount, and set the deal to Won when a quote is accepted. Allow 'Accept & invoice' only from Sent/Accepted and before valid_until, unless a manager overrides. Add a branded PDF template (logo, terms, bank or InstaPay details, Arabic/English) and a public share link where the customer can accept with name and signature, recording timestamp and IP.
findings.auditor: Quotes have prefix 'QT' (roles.ts:68), but the only place a number is assigned is postDocument, which rejects quotes (engine.ts:427). So rec.number is never set: titles read 'Draft · …' and the print reads DRAFT (RecordPage.tsx:351). 'Accept & invoice' shows for any status except invoiced, including declined (RecordPage.tsx:72-75), and quoteToInvoice checks only invoiced (560) and never checks valid_until. One partial overstatement: after invoicing, the UI does lock the header and lines (docLocked, RecordPage.tsx:33). Only the engine (updateRecord:267) would allow the edit, so a user can't do it from the screen. One gap the panel missed: deleteRecord also exempts quotes (engine.ts:297), and the invoice doesn't reference the quote (only quote.links.source = inv.id), so an invoiced quote can be deleted, breaking the offer→invoice trail. 'Mark sent' (setQuoteStatus, RecordPage.tsx:170-175) records no sent date, no log entry and no updatedAt.

findings.title: No pricing governance: unlimited discounts, no discount approval, no price lists, and the credit limit is ignored
findings.evidence: checkLines (engine.ts:390-397) accepts any discount from 0 to 100%. Probe: a quote with a 100% discount was saved and invoiced at total 0. ApprovalRule.action is only 'post' | 'stage' (schema.ts:128), and validate.ts:302-303 rejects anything else. Quotes have neither posting nor stages, so a discount approval on quotations can't be configured. LinesEditor (RecordPage.tsx:263) uses the product's single `price` field: no price lists, customer-specific prices, minimum price or margin-below-cost warning. The distribution template defines `credit_limit` (templates.ts:226), but postDocument (engine.ts:423-506) never checks customer balance against it.
findings.impact: Discount leakage is a top margin killer for distributors. A rep can give 40% off or sell below cost with no trace or approval, and finance learns at month-end. Selling over the credit limit creates the 'customers pay late' problem the product claims to fix. Odoo, SAP B1, Zoho and Salesforce CPQ ship price lists, discount thresholds with approval, and credit checks as standard.
findings.recommendation: Add (1) Price lists: module-level lists per customer segment or channel with validity dates and an override per customer, auto-applied in LinesEditor. (2) A max-discount-per-role setting and a minimum margin %, with lines over the limit flagged in red. (3) A new approval action 'quote_send' or 'discount' with a condition 'max line discount > X' or 'margin < Y', which blocks Mark sent until approved. (4) A credit check on invoice posting: block or require approval when open balance plus invoice total exceeds credit_limit, with the exposure shown on the customer card.
findings.auditor: checkLines (engine.ts:390-397) allows a discount from 0 to 100%. ApprovalRule.action is 'post' | 'stage' (schema.ts:129), and validate.ts rejects 'post' on anything except invoices and bills, so quotes, which have neither posting nor stages, can't get an approval. LinesEditor.pick (RecordPage.tsx:260-265) takes the single product price, with no margin or cost warning even though the average cost is available. credit_limit exists only in the distribution template (templates.ts:226) and nothing reads it. Invoices of a large amount can be gated with an approval at posting, so some control exists for big tickets, but not for discount or credit.

findings.title: No activity model and no customer 360: tasks link by free text, there are no calls or meetings, and the timeline covers only the record itself
findings.evidence: The tasks role's `related` field is plain text (roles.ts:256). Automations fill it with `recordTitle(...)` (engine.ts:655), e.g. 'Draft · Kasr Al Ainy' in the probe, so tasks can't be opened from or listed on the deal or customer. Tasks have only a due *date* (no time), no type (call, meeting, WhatsApp, visit), no outcome or duration, and no reminder notification. Comments (engine.ts:765-775) don't update `updatedAt`, so logging a call doesn't reset rotting (engine.ts:156-157), while any trivial field edit does. The RecordPage 'Linked records' panel lists up to 20 directly related records with no grouping or totals (RecordPage.tsx:177-185), and History/Comments show only this record (RecordPage.tsx:52, 424).
findings.impact: Reps can't answer 'when did we last talk to this hospital, and what's next?' in one place. Managers can't measure activity (calls per rep per day) or enforce a 'next step' on every open deal. Rotting flags reward fake edits instead of real customer contact. HubSpot, Pipedrive and Salesforce are built around the activity timeline and the 'next activity' column.
findings.recommendation: Add an 'activities' system role with a polymorphic relation to any record (the related record ID plus its account), type (call, meeting, WhatsApp, e-mail, visit, task), date-time, duration, outcome, done, and reminder (notify X minutes before). Add one-click 'Log call' and 'Schedule next step' on the deal card and record header. Show a unified, filterable timeline on the account page that merges activities, comments, field changes, quotes, invoices, payments and tickets of the account and all its contacts and deals. Base rotting on last completed activity, and show a 'No next step' badge on deals without a future activity.
findings.auditor: tasks.related is a text field (roles.ts:256), and execute() fills it with recordTitle (engine.ts:655), which gives 'Draft · Customer' for quotes. The Dashboard shows it as plain text with no link (Dashboard.tsx:57). addComment (765-775) doesn't touch updatedAt, while rotting() uses updatedAt (157), so a logged note doesn't reset the idle flag but any field edit does. relatedRecords stops at 20 records with no grouping (RecordPage.tsx:177-185). Tasks have only a due date. All accurate.

findings.title: No lead capture channels: no web forms, WhatsApp, e-mail or Facebook leads, no click-to-call, and imports skip automations
findings.evidence: There is no web-to-lead endpoint, WhatsApp, e-mail or Meta lead-ads integration. README 'What comes next' lists WhatsApp and e-mail as future work, and grep finds no `tel:`, `wa.me` or `mailto:` anywhere in src. Phone fields render as plain text (engine.ts displayValue default branch; RecordPage.tsx:246). `importRows` creates records with `{ silent: true }` (engine.ts:799), so the 'Call every new lead within 24 hours' workflow (packs.ts:70) never fires for imported leads, and no owner other than the importer is assigned (engine.ts:227).
findings.impact: The top challenge in onboarding is 'Leads get lost in WhatsApp and calls' (packs.ts:14), yet every lead must be retyped by hand. For Egyptian SMEs, WhatsApp is the main sales channel. HubSpot, Zoho, Bitrix24 and Odoo all ship embeddable forms, inbox capture and WhatsApp connectors. Local players such as Daftra and Bitrix24 promote WhatsApp in Arabic.
findings.recommendation: Phase 1 (M): render phone fields as click-to-call and wa.me links with a prefilled template, and e-mail as mailto. Add a public hosted lead form per workspace (Supabase Edge Function + captcha + rate limit) with UTM capture into source and campaign. Make import optionally 'run automations and assignment rules'. Phase 2 (XL): WhatsApp Business Cloud API inbox (incoming message creates or matches a lead by phone and logs the conversation on the timeline), Meta Lead Ads webhook, and e-mail BCC-to-CRM logging.
findings.auditor: grep for tel:, wa.me and mailto: across src returns nothing. A phone field renders as input type=tel in the form (RecordPage.tsx:246) and as plain text in lists and cards. importRows calls createRecord with silent:true (engine.ts:799), which skips runWorkflows (260), so the 'Call every new lead' workflow (packs.ts:70) never fires for imported leads. The owner defaults to the importer (engine.ts:227). README lists WhatsApp and e-mail as future work, so this is a known roadmap gap, but high is fair against competitors. The click-to-call and wa.me part is S effort and should be split out.

findings.title: No duplicate detection or merge, and phone numbers aren't normalized
findings.area: Data quality: leads, contacts, accounts, import
findings.evidence: The only uniqueness check is an exact case-insensitive string compare on fields flagged `unique` (engine.ts:204-207), and no CRM system field is unique by default (roles.ts:177-207). PHONE accepts any 7-20 chars of digits, spaces and punctuation (engine.ts:172) and stores the raw string. Probe: leads with '01001234567' and '+20 100 123 4567' (same number) were both created, each with its own 'Call…' task. Import has no 'update existing when matched' (upsert) mode (engine.ts:785-807), and there is no merge function.
findings.impact: The same person messaging on WhatsApp, calling and filling a form becomes three leads owned by three reps who all call them, a classic poor first impression. Reports double-count leads by source. Every serious CRM (HubSpot, Zoho, Salesforce duplicate rules, Odoo) has matching rules and a merge tool.
findings.recommendation: Normalize phones to E.164 with Egypt as the default country (01x → +201x) on save and import, and store the normalized value for matching. Add matching rules per role (lead or contact by phone or e-mail, account by tax ID or fuzzy name) that warn on create ('Possible duplicate: Dr X, owned by Ahmed. Open it or create anyway'). Add an import upsert mode keyed on a chosen field, and a 'Merge records' action that re-points relations, activities and comments, keeping the audit trail.
findings.auditor: The unique check is an exact lowercase string compare (engine.ts:204-207). No CRM system field is marked unique; only the product SKU is (roles.ts:211). The PHONE regex (172) stores whatever raw string was typed. There is no merge function and no upsert in importRows. The relation import (engine.ts:840) matches on title, which means duplicate account names make imports link to whichever duplicate comes first, so the damage compounds. High is fair.

findings.title: No record-level ownership: every rep sees and edits every deal and customer, and anyone with view rights can export the whole database
findings.evidence: `can()` checks permissions per module only (engine.ts:28-33). The sales preset grants view, create and edit on all accounts, contacts, leads and deals (packs.ts:103). There is no 'own records only' or team scope. The Export button is shown to anyone who can open the module (ModuleView.tsx:83) and exports all filtered rows with every field (ModuleView.tsx:60-70). Owner can be changed by any editor (the owner field is a normal user select, RecordPage.tsx:236-241).
findings.impact: In Egyptian SMEs, a departing rep exporting the customer list to a competitor is a real and common risk, and reps 'stealing' each other's deals by changing the owner damages commissions and morale. Salesforce (OWD plus role hierarchy), HubSpot ('team only / owned only') and Zoho (data sharing rules) all provide this. Without it, larger SMEs won't adopt.
findings.recommendation: Add a per-role, per-module scope: All / My team / Only mine (owner or assignee), enforced in list, findRecord, search, reports and export. Make export a separate permission, off for sales by default, and log exports in the audit trail. Allow only managers or admins to reassign the owner, or require approval. Add teams (a manager plus members) so 'My team' and team dashboards work. Mirror this in server-side RLS once records move to rows (see SALE-01).
findings.auditor: can() checks only module and permission (engine.ts:28-33). The sales preset is RW on accounts, contacts, leads and deals (packs.ts:103). Export has no separate permission (ModuleView.tsx:83). The owner field is an ordinary user select (RecordPage.tsx:236-241). The panel understates the problem: every module permission is enforced only in the browser. RLS is per workspace (migrations: 'members read their workspace' and 'members save their workspace'), and every member downloads and can rewrite the entire doc. So a rep can read invoices, journals and all customers from the API response even for modules their role can't view, and can change any record server-side. The record-scope part belongs here as high. The missing server-side enforcement is critical, but it belongs to the security panel.

findings.title: Forecasting and sales performance are rudimentary: no period, quotas, win rate, velocity or forecast categories
findings.evidence: The weighted forecast (Dashboard.tsx:73-79) sums amount × probability over all open deals regardless of close date or owner. It is a single muted line of text, hard-coded to `amount`. 'Deals won' is an all-time count (packs.ts:44), although the challenge fix promises 'won-this-month KPIs' (packs.ts:15). 'Pipeline by stage' uses `filters: []` (packs.ts:47), so the funnel includes Won and Lost amounts and isn't a conversion funnel. There are no quota or target objects, no forecast category (pipeline, best case, commit), no win rate, average deal size, sales-cycle length or stage-conversion report, and report filters can't express relative dates (FilterOp has no 'this month' or 'last N days', schema.ts:137).
findings.impact: The owner can't answer the three questions they care about: will we hit this month or quarter, who is behind target, and where do deals die? This is the core of HubSpot Forecasts, Salesforce Forecasting and Pipedrive Insights. Without it, Bonyan loses the head-to-head demo to any of them.
findings.recommendation: Add (1) relative date filters (this/last month, quarter or year, next 30 days) on any date field, (2) a Targets module (owner or team, period, amount) with an 'attainment vs target' gauge and a pacing line, (3) a forecast view by close month showing closed-won, commit, best case and pipeline, with a rep-editable forecast category on deals, (4) built-in analytics: stage-to-stage conversion from stageHistory, average time in stage, win rate by source and owner, and sales velocity, (5) 'Pipeline by stage' limited to open stages by default, with a separate true conversion funnel.
findings.auditor: The weighted forecast (Dashboard.tsx:73-79) covers all open deals with no date or owner filter, shows as one muted line, and is rendered with no can(view) check on the deals module, so a role without access to deals still sees the pipeline value. 'Deals won' counts all-time won deals (packs.ts:44), which doesn't deliver the 'won-this-month' promise (packs.ts:15). 'Pipeline by stage' has filters [] (packs.ts:47), so Won and Lost amounts appear in the funnel. FilterOp (schema.ts:137) has no relative dates. No targets, win rate or velocity exist. All verified.

findings.title: Automations are shallow: lookup and rollup conditions never match, there are only 3 actions, and date triggers run only when someone opens the app
findings.evidence: runWorkflows calls `matches(ctx.schema, rec, w.conditions)` without `ws` (engine.ts:640), and so does runScheduled (engine.ts:683). pseudoValue computes lookup and rollup values only when `ws` is passed (engine.ts:586-589), so a condition such as 'Customer governorate = Cairo' or 'Balance due > 0' on a customer is always evaluated as empty. The builder still offers those fields (AutomationsTab.tsx:114-117). There are only three actions: create_task, set_field and notify (schema.ts:160-163). There is no assign or round-robin, no e-mail, WhatsApp or SMS, no webhook, no 'wait N days', no create-related-record and no sequence. Date-based rules run once, inside whichever browser opens first (Shell.tsx:23-28), under that user's identity. Overnight and weekend reminders don't fire, and two users opening at once can both run them before the save conflict.
findings.impact: 'Assign new Facebook leads round-robin to the sales team', 'WhatsApp the customer when the quote is sent' and 'escalate a deal idle 7 days to the manager' are the automations every SME asks for first, and none can be built. The silently failing lookup conditions damage trust in the builder.
findings.recommendation: Pass `ctx.ws` in both calls now (S) and add a test. Then add actions: assign owner (fixed, round-robin among a role or team, or by territory such as governorate), send e-mail or WhatsApp template, webhook, create related record, update parent, and wait/delay. Move scheduled and date triggers to a server cron (Supabase pg_cron plus an Edge Function) running as a system 'Automation' user, with a run log per automation showing what ran, on which record and any errors.
findings.auditor: Confirmed: runWorkflows (engine.ts:640) and runScheduled (683) call matches() without ws, so lookup and rollup conditions such as customer_governorate (packs.ts:148) or balance_due always evaluate as empty. fieldOptions (ReportsTab.tsx:48-51) still offers those fields in the Automations builder. There are only 3 action types (schema.ts:161-163), and scheduled runs fire once from Shell.tsx:23-28 under the identity of whoever opened the app. Wrong: the claim that two users opening at once 'can both run them' and get duplicates. The optimistic version check (store.ts:58-60) lets only one save land; the loser's copy is discarded on reload, so duplicate tasks can't persist. At worst the loser sees a misleading 'N automations ran' toast. The panel also missed that the 'updated' trigger fires on every save (see the missed item).

findings.title: Notifications are marked read for everyone, and @mentions match by first name only
findings.evidence: Note.read is a single boolean on a shared note (types.ts:77-86). Opening the bell sets `n.read = true` on every visible note (Shell.tsx:77), including broadcast notes with no user, such as 'Deal won' (packs.ts:75), and role notes, so the first person to open the bell clears them for the whole team. addComment notifies every user whose first name equals the mention (engine.ts:769-773): '@Mohamed' pings every Mohamed, the most common first name in Egypt, and can't reach 'Mohamed Ali' specifically. There is no @-autocomplete (RecordPage.tsx:429-431 only prints the first 4 names), and addComment has no permission check (engine.ts:765).
findings.impact: Approval requests and overdue-invoice alerts show as already read for the people who were supposed to act. Mentions go to the wrong person or to several people. These small breaks quickly train teams to ignore the bell.
findings.recommendation: Store read state per user (a `readBy: string[]` on each note, or per-user rows). Replace first-name parsing with an @-autocomplete that inserts a user ID token (`@[u_123]`), rendered as a chip. Add the record's `view` permission check in addComment, and allow editing or deleting your own comments within 15 minutes.
findings.auditor: Note.read is one boolean (types.ts:77-86). Opening the bell marks every visible note read (Shell.tsx:77), including broadcast notes with no user and role notes such as the 'Deal won' broadcast and the finance overdue alert, for every viewer. addComment matches on the first token of u.name (engine.ts:771) and has no permission check (765). The hint lists only the first 4 users (RecordPage.tsx:431). Accurate.

findings.title: Global search matches record titles only and can't find a caller by phone or e-mail
findings.evidence: Shell.tsx:35-37 filters by `recordTitle(...).includes(q)` only. Phone, e-mail, tax ID, SKU and tender number aren't searched. Results are capped at 4 per module and 10 overall, with no 'see all'. ModuleView search covers in-list columns, but only inside one module (ModuleView.tsx:46).
findings.impact: The most frequent action for an Egyptian rep or receptionist is: a WhatsApp or phone call comes in from 010…, who is this? Today they must open each module and search. HubSpot, Zoho and Pipedrive all search phone, e-mail and custom fields globally.
findings.recommendation: Index every text, phone (normalized, digits-only matching on the last 9-10 digits), e-mail, and number field marked searchable in global search. Group results by module with the matched field highlighted. Add a 'Create lead with this number' action when nothing matches, and a Ctrl/Cmd+K shortcut.
findings.auditor: Shell.tsx:35-37 matches only on recordTitle, with 4 results per module and 10 in total. ModuleView search covers only the title and the first 7 inList columns (ModuleView.tsx:43-46). It does find a lead by phone inside the Leads list, because phone is inList, but not from global search. Medium is fair; S effort is realistic.

findings.title: Field sales on a phone is barely workable: the board can't scroll, calendar events are hidden, and there's no offline mode or visit check-in
findings.area: Mobile use: Board, Calendar, Rep visits
findings.evidence: styles.css:342 sets `.kcard { touch-action: none }` and at phone width each column is 82vw (styles.css:403), so almost every touch on the board starts a drag instead of a scroll. The board uses only PointerSensor with a 6 px distance (ModuleView.tsx:179). On ≤760px, calendar events are `display: none` (styles.css:434) and tapping a day does nothing (ModuleView.tsx:259-263 has no day handler). There is no PWA manifest or service worker (public/ has only favicon.svg), no offline queue, and the medical 'Rep visits' module (templates.ts:95-103) has no geolocation check-in, photo or signature capture.
findings.impact: Medical reps, distributors' route sales and site engineers, the core personas of the templates, work from phones in hospitals and on sites with patchy 4G. Salesforce, Zoho, Odoo and Pipedrive ship native or offline-capable mobile apps with check-in. Without this, field teams won't use Bonyan.
findings.recommendation: Use dnd-kit TouchSensor with a 250 ms press delay and drop `touch-action: none` (or set it only on a drag handle). Add a mobile list mode for boards (stage chips plus a swipe action to move). Make calendar days tappable to open an agenda list. Ship a PWA (manifest, offline cache, queued writes). Add a 'Check in' action on visit-type modules that records GPS, time and a photo, plus a 'My day' mobile home screen (today's visits, tasks, overdue follow-ups).
findings.auditor: styles.css:342 sets touch-action:none on .kcard, and styles.css:403 sets columns to 82vw. Board registers only PointerSensor with distance 6 (ModuleView.tsx:179), so a finger on a card starts a drag instead of scrolling. styles.css:434 hides .cal-ev at ≤760px and underlines the day number as if it could be tapped, but the day cell has no click handler (ModuleView.tsx:259-263). public/ has only favicon.svg, so there is no manifest or service worker. The visits module (templates.ts:94-103) has no GPS, photo or signature. The board and calendar fixes are S; the PWA and offline work is L or more.

findings.title: Kanban and lists won't scale and aren't keyboard-accessible
findings.evidence: Board renders every record of every stage, including all historical Won and Lost deals, with no date window, collapse or paging (ModuleView.tsx:187-195). The table renders all rows with no pagination or virtualization (ModuleView.tsx:132-140). `findRecord` scans every module's array (engine.ts:50-57) and is called per relation cell and per recordTitle, so rendering is O(rows × total records). Only PointerSensor is registered (ModuleView.tsx:179), with no KeyboardSensor, so cards can't be moved by keyboard (WCAG 2.2 SC 2.1.1 and 2.5.7 dragging alternative), and the stage path is the only alternative on the record page.
findings.impact: Real-estate Facebook campaigns produce 5-20k leads a quarter, and the template targets exactly that. The board and table will slow to unusable, and a JSON doc of that size also slows every save (SALE-01).
findings.recommendation: Add an ID→record index map in the engine (or server queries after the move to rows). Paginate or virtualize tables (e.g. 50 rows plus infinite scroll). On boards, hide Won and Lost by default or show only the last 30 days with a 'show closed' toggle, and lazy-load cards per column. Register KeyboardSensor with announcements, and add a 'Move to…' menu on each card.
findings.auditor: findRecord does a linear scan over every module (engine.ts:50-57). It is called per relation cell, per recordTitle (and recursively for line documents, line 63) and per rollup. The board renders every stage, Won and Lost included, without paging (ModuleView.tsx:187-195), and the table renders every row. No KeyboardSensor is registered, so cards can't be moved by keyboard, and the cards are onClick divs with no move menu. The one-JSON-doc size makes it worse. Medium is fair.

findings.title: Lead scoring is static, hidden from reports and automations, and its thresholds are hard-coded
findings.evidence: score() is computed on the fly from field conditions only (engine.ts:146-149). It isn't stored, and pseudoValue has no `__score` (engine.ts:584-596), so reports can't group or filter by score and automations can't trigger on 'score > 40'. The hot, warm and cold thresholds are hard-coded at 40 and 20 in the UI (ModuleView.tsx:163-166). The defaults are only source, e-mail, company and budget (packs.ts:152-161). There are no behavioural signals (replied, opened quote, visited), no decay by age, and no fit/engagement split.
findings.impact: Scoring looks good in a demo but can't drive action: no 'route hot leads to senior reps', no 'hot leads not contacted' report. HubSpot and Zoho scoring are usable in lists, workflows and reports.
findings.recommendation: Expose `__score` as a pseudo-field everywhere filters exist (reports, automations, validation, saved views). Make the hot and warm thresholds configurable in the Rules tab. Add activity-based rules (has a completed call, replied on WhatsApp, quote viewed) and time decay (−N points per week without activity). Show 'why this score' on hover.
findings.auditor: score() is computed on the fly (engine.ts:146-149). pseudoValue has no __score (584-596), so reports and automations can't use it; only the ModuleView sort uses it (ModuleView.tsx:51). The 40/20 thresholds are hard-coded (ModuleView.tsx:163-166), and the default rules are static field checks (packs.ts:152-161). Accurate.

findings.title: B2B stakeholder model is missing: deals and quotes have no contacts, and a contact belongs to only one account
findings.evidence: The deals system fields are title, account, amount, close_date and owner (roles.ts:200-207), with no contact. Quotes have customer, date and validity only (roles.ts:220-226), with no 'Attention' contact. A contact's `account` is a single relation (roles.ts:186). Relations are single-valued (FieldDef.target, schema.ts:39), so 'many contacts on a deal, each with a role' can't be built.
findings.impact: In the medical, water and construction tender verticals, a deal involves a procurement officer, a head of department and a technical committee. Reps can't record who the decision maker is or who signs, and quotes print with no addressee. Salesforce Opportunity Contact Roles, HubSpot associations and Zoho Contact Roles are standard.
findings.recommendation: Add a primary contact relation on deals and quotes (printed as 'Attention' on the PDF), plus a many-to-many 'Deal contacts' sub-list with a role picklist (Decision maker, Influencer, Technical, Procurement, Signer). Support a multi-relation field type so builders can model the same pattern on custom modules.
findings.auditor: The deals system fields have no contact (roles.ts:200-207), quotes have none either (roles.ts:220-226), the contact has a single account relation (186), and FieldDef.target is single-valued. The print has no 'Attention' line (RecordPage.tsx:357-361). Accurate.

findings.title: Service tickets have no SLA, contact, channel or warranty link, and no CSAT
findings.evidence: The tickets role has only subject, account, priority, engineer and description (roles.ts:258-265). The only time control is a 2-day rotting flag (packs.ts:129). There are no first-response or resolution targets per priority, no breach alerts, no requester contact, no channel (phone, WhatsApp, e-mail), and no link to the product, serial or invoice that proves warranty. The medical template adds a text 'Device serial' and a manual 'Under warranty' checkbox (templates.ts:104). Resolution doesn't trigger a satisfaction survey.
findings.impact: 'Slow after-sales service' is a listed challenge (packs.ts:21), but the module can't measure it. Freshdesk, Zoho Desk, HubSpot Service and Odoo Helpdesk all ship SLA policies and CSAT. Medical device distributors need warranty validation from the sales invoice and serial.
findings.recommendation: Add SLA policies per priority (first-response and resolve-by times, business hours with a Fri/Sat weekend option), countdown badges on cards, and breach automations. Add requester contact and channel system fields, and a relation to invoice line or product plus serial, with warranty auto-computed from invoice date and warranty months. On Resolved, send a 1-5 CSAT via a WhatsApp or e-mail link, and report SLA attainment and CSAT by engineer.
findings.auditor: The tickets role has only subject, account, priority, engineer and description (roles.ts:258-265). The only time control is a 2-day rotDays (packs.ts:129). The medical template has a text serial and a manual warranty checkbox (templates.ts:104). There is no SLA, channel, requester or CSAT. Accurate.

findings.title: Real-estate template allows double-booking a unit, and installments are disconnected from billing
findings.evidence: Reservations link to a unit via a plain relation (templates.ts:139), with no uniqueness across open reservations and no automatic Unit.status update (Available → Reserved → Sold, templates.ts:134). Two reps can reserve the same villa. 'Installments' is a manual custom module with a 'Paid' checkbox (templates.ts:150-158), not generated from the payment plan (down_payment, years on the deal, templates.ts:140-141) and not linked to invoices, payments or receivables ageing. The 'Lead source ROI' highlight (templates.ts:117) has no campaign-cost data to compute ROI from.
findings.impact: Double-selling a unit is the most damaging error a developer's sales team can make, and real-estate CRMs on the Egyptian market are judged on unit locking. Manual installments break collections tracking, which is the developer's cash flow.
findings.recommendation: Add a 'reserve exclusive' option on relation fields (one open record per target), and have the Reserved and Contract signed gates set the unit's status through a system rule, with Cancelled releasing it. Generate an installment schedule from the deal's price, down payment %, years and frequency when the contract is signed, linked to invoices and ageing, with overdue reminders. Add a Campaigns module (cost, period, source) so 'cost per lead' and 'ROI by source' are real reports.
findings.auditor: Reservation.unit is a plain relation (templates.ts:139). The relation picker lists every unit regardless of status (RecordPage.tsx:227-234), and no rule changes Unit.status (templates.ts:134). Installments is a manual module with a Paid checkbox (150-158), not linked to invoices, payments or ageing. There is no campaign-cost data behind 'Lead source ROI' (117). Raised to high: double-selling a unit is the most damaging error in the vertical this template targets, and the product promises guardrails.

findings.title: List views are basic: personal-only saved views, no field filters, no column chooser, no bulk actions
findings.evidence: A saved view stores only free text q, a stage, sort and layout (types.ts:109-118) and is filtered to `v.user === user.id` (ModuleView.tsx:37), so managers can't publish 'Hot leads this week' for the team. The view is named via window.prompt (ModuleView.tsx:39). Columns are the first 7 `inList` fields (ModuleView.tsx:43) with no chooser. There are no per-field filters (owner = me, close date this month, amount > X), no 'My records' toggle, and no multi-select for bulk reassign, bulk stage move or bulk delete.
findings.impact: Sales managers run their week from filtered lists: 'my deals closing this month', 'leads with no activity'. Without shared views, field filters and bulk reassign (needed when a rep leaves), the daily workflow falls back to Excel exports. monday, Airtable, Attio and HubSpot make this their core UX.
findings.recommendation: Reuse the existing Filter/FilterRow components (ReportsTab) as a filter bar on lists, with relative-date operators and 'me' as a user value. Add a column chooser with drag reorder per view, shared views (personal, team, everyone, managed by admin or manager), default views per role ('My open deals'), and bulk actions (assign owner, move stage, add task, export selected) that respect permissions and log to the audit trail.
findings.auditor: SavedView stores q, stage, sort and view only (types.ts:109-118). Views are filtered to v.user === user.id (ModuleView.tsx:37), named via window.prompt (39), and limited to the first 7 inList columns (43). There are no field filters and no multi-select or bulk actions. Accurate.

findings.title: The CRM workspace is English-only, which hurts the local fight against Arabic-first competitors
findings.evidence: README says Arabic covers only 'the landing page, industry names and challenges' and that 'Arabic across the whole app' is future work. All CRM strings are hard-coded English: stage names (roles.ts:141-164), engine error messages (e.g. engine.ts:310 'To move to … fill in'), toasts, buttons and the RecordPage header actions. The Shell language toggle (Shell.tsx:75) doesn't translate workspace screens. Dates print via toLocaleString with no Arabic or Hijri option, and the tax invoice print is English-only (RecordPage.tsx:335-375).
findings.impact: In Egypt, many field reps, receptionists and owners of family businesses prefer Arabic. Daftra, Odoo (Arabic), Zoho (Arabic) and Bitrix24 sell Arabic-first. A bilingual quotation and tax invoice is expected by government and hospital buyers.
findings.recommendation: Move every workspace, engine-message and default-stage string into i18n keys, with full RTL QA of the board, record page and print. Give labels both Arabic and English values in the schema (label and labelAr for fields, stages and options). Offer bilingual PDF templates for quotations and invoices, and Arabic number and date formatting as a company setting.
findings.auditor: README.md:96 lists 'Arabic across the whole app' as future work. Only Shell imports useLang (Shell.tsx:9, 17), and no workspace screen translates its strings. Worse than stated: setLang flips document.documentElement.dir to rtl (i18n.ts:17), so the workspace 'ع' toggle mirrors the whole layout while every label stays English, which looks broken in a demo. The print view is English-only (RecordPage.tsx:330-380). Medium for global, but it is a high local go-to-market risk.

findings.title: Sales reps cannot record a customer's acceptance: 'Accept & invoice' fails for the sales role and the 'accepted' status can't be reached
findings.evidence: RecordPage.tsx:72-78 offers only Mark sent, Accept & invoice and Declined. quoteToInvoice (engine.ts:557-565) calls createRecord on the invoices module without silent, so need(ctx, invoices, 'create') runs (engine.ts:224). The sales preset gives only view on invoices (packs.ts:103). Probe with the distribution template and a Sales team: a rep clicking Accept & invoice got 'Your role can't create records here', and the quote stayed as it was. Nothing in src ever sets status 'accepted' (types.ts:4), although the ModuleView status filter offers it (ModuleView.tsx:93).
findings.impact: The everyday flow (rep wins the offer, finance invoices it) breaks on the default role setup. The rep sees an error and can't even mark the quote as won, so finance has no queue of accepted quotes to invoice, and quote-to-invoice conversion can't be measured.
findings.recommendation: Split the button: 'Mark accepted' (sales, sets accepted with date, user and log entry, optionally moving the linked deal to Won) and 'Create invoice' (finance, or any role that can create invoices). Show accepted quotes in a finance 'Ready to invoice' list on the Accounting page, and hide buttons the current role can't use instead of failing.

findings.title: 'Record updated' automations fire on every save while the condition holds, flooding reps with duplicate tasks
findings.evidence: updateRecord calls runWorkflows(ctx, rec, 'updated') after every save (engine.ts:279), and runWorkflows only re-evaluates the conditions on the current values (633-646). There is no 'changed to' or 'became true' check and no once-per-record memory like workflowRuns for date triggers. Probe: an 'updated' rule 'amount > 1000 → create task Review {title}' and 3 edits to the title gave 3 identical Review tasks. set_field actions also change values without a log entry or updatedAt (656-661).
findings.impact: A reasonable rule like 'when a deal over EGP 100k is updated, notify the manager' spams the manager and the task list on every edit. Users disable automations and stop trusting the builder.
findings.recommendation: Add trigger semantics 'when field X changes' and 'when conditions become true' (compare before/after values passed from updateRecord), plus an optional 'run once per record' toggle. Log set_field changes to the record history as 'Automation'. Add tests.

findings.title: 'Sales by month' buckets invoices by when the draft was created (not the invoice date) and reports VAT-inclusive totals as revenue
findings.evidence: packs.ts:48 groups invoices by '__month' and pseudoValue returns rec.createdAt.slice(0,7) for '__month' (engine.ts:593, used by reports.ts:54). Probe: an invoice dated 2026-09-15 whose draft was created 2026-08-30 is reported under 2026-08. 'Invoiced revenue' (packs.ts:41) and 'Sales by month' sum 'total', which includes the 14% VAT, while the journal credits revenue 4000 with the subtotal only (engine.ts:468).
findings.impact: The owner's headline sales chart disagrees with the P&L, both in which month a sale lands (back-dated or late-posted invoices) and by about 14% (VAT counted as sales). This erodes trust in the dashboard, the selling point against Odoo and Zoho, and misleads month-end performance reviews and commissions.
findings.recommendation: Group revenue reports by the document date (or posting date) field, not createdAt, and measure 'subtotal' (net of VAT) by default, labelled 'Net sales'. Reconcile the KPI with the 4000 account balance and show a 'matches the books' tick. Let report builders choose which date field '__month' uses.

findings.title: Admin 'switch user' performs real writes under the colleague's identity, so the sales audit trail can be forged
findings.evidence: Shell.tsx:90-93 shows a user switcher to admins. switchUser (store.ts:267-272) changes session.userId, and useApp.act builds ctx.user from that user (useApp.ts:36). Every engine write then records the impersonated person: log() writes ctx.user.name (engine.ts:217), and comments, createdBy, approval requests (739) and decisions (755) do the same. decideApproval's self-approval check (753) compares against the impersonated user, so an admin can request an approval as a rep and approve it as the manager, and the trail shows two different people.
findings.impact: In commission disputes or a fraud review, history entries like 'Sara moved the deal to Won' or 'Manager approved' can't be trusted. This defeats the field-history and approval features the product sells against Salesforce and Odoo.
findings.recommendation: Make 'View as' read-only (block act() while selfId ≠ userId), or record both identities on every entry ('Admin as Sara') and forbid approval decisions while impersonating. Show a persistent banner 'You are viewing as Sara'.

findings.title: The record form saves a stale full snapshot, silently reverting changes that arrived while it was open
findings.evidence: Editor initialises local state once from rec.values (RecordPage.tsx:28), keyed only by rec.id (line 22), so it isn't refreshed when the workspace is reloaded (store.ts:141-149) or changed by another action. save() passes the entire values object to updateRecord (RecordPage.tsx:46), and cleanValues copies every key present in the input (engine.ts:176-184). Any field another user or a reload changed is overwritten with the old value, and the history logs it as this user's change.
findings.impact: Even after the conflict handling in SALE-01 is fixed, a rep who keeps a deal open while the manager changes the amount or owner reverts it on Save without knowing. Field-level merge can't work while the form sends unchanged fields.
findings.recommendation: Send only the fields the user actually changed (diff against the snapshot taken at mount). If the stored value changed since mount, show an inline 'Changed by X: keep theirs / use mine' prompt. Refresh untouched fields when the record updates underneath.

findings.title: Quote follow-up runs from draft creation and is never closed; sending, declining and invoicing leave no event
findings.evidence: The default 'Follow up 3 days after a quotation' rule triggers on 'created' (packs.ts:71), so the task is due 3 days after the draft is made, not after it is sent. setQuoteStatus (RecordPage.tsx:170-175) changes the status with no log, no updatedAt, no sent date and no runWorkflows. quoteToInvoice (engine.ts:557-565) likewise doesn't close the open follow-up task. Because the task's 'related' field is text, nothing can find and close it.
findings.impact: Reps get follow-up reminders for quotes not yet sent, and keep getting them for quotes already declined or invoiced. That is the opposite of the 'No follow-up after sending quotes' fix promised in onboarding (packs.ts:18). Time-to-accept can't be measured because no sent date exists.
findings.recommendation: Add a 'status_changed' trigger for document modules and move the default rule to 'quote marked sent'. Store sent_at, accepted_at and declined_at with log entries. Automatically complete open follow-up tasks linked (by record ID, see SALE-07) to a quote once it is accepted, declined or invoiced.

panel: UX, UI, Visual Design, Dashboards & Reporting
strengths: The design foundation is good. styles.css:1-27 defines tokens on :root and the stylesheet uses logical properties throughout (inset-inline, margin-inline-start, padding-inline). That gives a real base for mirroring to right-to-left.

The health check is a feature competitors lack. The health ring and issue list in the builder (Builder.tsx:44-48, 106-139) jump straight to the tab, module or field at fault, and publishing is blocked until errors are fixed. Neither Odoo Studio nor Salesforce Setup offers this guided feedback.

The suggestion step is easy to trust. Suggest.tsx:276-330 shows a match % ring, the plain-language reasons, the modules and the fixes for the user's challenges, so the user sees why that template was chosen.

The report designer is beginner-friendly. Group by / Measure / Only include boxes with a live preview on generated sample data (ReportsTab.tsx:31-46, 170-174) follow Power BI's mental model at a level an SME can manage.

The pipeline screens are well thought out: totals per kanban column, deal-rotting 'idle Nd' badges, lead-score flame pills, and a Salesforce-style stage path on the record page (ModuleView.tsx:192-219, RecordPage.tsx:95-106).
Sample data goes through the real engine (seed.ts), so the first dashboard is populated and the books balance. Screenshots confirm 13 live widgets appear on first run.

Good details already in place: tabular numerals on .num cells, a CSV export with a UTF-8 byte-order mark so Arabic opens correctly in Excel (ModuleView.tsx:64), dir="auto" on free-text inputs and comments, and locked-document banners that explain why the user cannot edit.

scorecard.rationale: The desktop builds look clean and modern, and the token and logical-property base, health check, stage path and kanban are solid. Against that: Arabic and RTL are not real beyond the landing page (UX-01), WCAG AA fails on keyboard and contrast (UX-06, UX-07), the mobile work app is broken (UX-08), posted documents look like editable forms, and every engine error is a fleeting toast. That is well short of Linear, HubSpot or Attio polish.

Sample-seeded dashboards with 7 chart types and a drag-and-drop report designer are a good start. But there is no date range, comparison, target or drill-down (UX-02, UX-05). The owner's key numbers (cash, margin, overdue AR, stock risk) are missing from the home screen (UX-03), several default charts mislead (Lost bar inside the pipeline funnel, months with no sales dropped, distorted axes; UX-04), there is one layout for all roles (UX-12), and there are no alerts or scheduled reports (UX-13).

The concept is simpler than Odoo or SAP: guided onboarding, templates with match reasons, guardrails that explain themselves, and plain-language copy. In practice users are sent into a 7-tab builder before they see a working app (UX-09), daily entry relies on native selects of every record with no bulk or inline actions (UX-10), the dashboard is a flat 13-card grid, and nothing works on a phone. Each of these reintroduces 'system thinking'.

The marketing look is vivid, but the visuals are a generic AI gradient with no brand system or dark mode (UX-16). Charts are hand-rolled SVG with stretching, poor ticks and colour collisions, the chart vocabulary is small (UX-14), the KPI sparkline is a fixed decoration, there is no monitor or TV mode, and there are no AI insights (UX-20). It does not yet beat Zoho Analytics, HubSpot or Power BI on visuals or intelligence.

vision: Best in class for Bonyan is an Arabic-first, role-aware workspace where every person opens to 'my day'. The owner opens a cockpit. Its top row holds Cash & bank, Overdue receivables split by age, Payables due this week, Gross margin % and Weighted forecast against target. Each tile shows a real sparkline, a ▲/▼ delta against the previous period and target progress, all driven by one global period picker (This month / Quarter / Fiscal YTD / Custom, with a compare toggle). Below sit a cash-in/cash-out bar chart, an Egypt governorate sales map, win rate by rep, and a stock-at-risk list with days of cover. Every bar, slice and KPI is a keyboard-focusable link that opens the exact filtered list, ready for bulk action ('Send reminder on WhatsApp to these 7 customers'). An Insights rail writes what changed in plain Arabic or English ('Collections slowed 22%; Delta Foods is 61 days late') and takes questions such as 'مبيعات الإسكندرية الشهر ده مقارنة بالشهر اللي فات' ('Alexandria sales this month vs last month'), returning a chart that can be saved as a widget. Sales reps get My pipeline, Today's follow-ups and Rotting deals; finance gets Documents to post or approve, VAT due and the ageing list; the warehouse gets the reorder list and today's deliveries. Each of these is a preset the admin can rearrange on a drag-and-resize 12-column canvas. Visually, the brand expresses بنيان: a deep ink-teal and sandstone palette, IBM Plex Sans Arabic paired with Inter on an 8-step type scale, three radii, checked tonal colour scales so every user-picked stage colour stays at or above 4.5:1, light and dark themes, and restrained motion that respects reduced-motion. Daily work runs from a Cmd-K palette, type-ahead pickers with 'create new', inline list edits, 'Save & post' and undo. On phones the same app has a bottom tab bar, a quick-add button and a stacked line editor. Monitors and a Sunday WhatsApp or e-mail 'Business pulse' bring the numbers to owners who never log in, and a TV mode puts the pipeline on the sales-floor screen.

findings.title: Arabic is only on the landing page: switching to Arabic mirrors the layout but leaves every screen in English
findings.evidence: i18n.ts:32-59 holds only 26 keys, and only Landing.tsx calls t(). Text is hard-coded English in Auth.tsx:121-156, Onboarding.tsx:13-22, 59-235 (STEPS, CHANNELS, TEAM_KINDS, every question), Suggest.tsx, Builder.tsx:17-25, Shell.tsx:43-95, Dashboard.tsx:21-78, ModuleView, RecordPage and Accounting. setLang only flips <html dir> (i18n.ts:15-18). Playwright screenshots in Arabic (register-d-ar, board-ar, dash-ar) show English text in a mirrored layout with broken punctuation ('.work', '.Free to start', '...Not saved, retrying', placeholder clipped to 'rch customers', '6' moved to the end of the toast). money() is hard-coded to 'en-US' (engine.ts:167-168). Month labels are English (reports.ts:20-21), as are calendar weekdays (ModuleView.tsx:253). Landing.tsx:55 uses className="flip" on the CTA arrow, but no .flip rule exists, so the arrow points the wrong way in RTL. The stage-path chevron clip-path polygon is drawn for left-to-right only (styles.css:308). Even in Arabic mode the landing page still shows English in the BEST and GUARDS sections, the trust row, the CTA paragraph, the template taglines and 'See how it works'.
findings.impact: For an Egypt-first product this blocks launch. Sales reps, storekeepers and accountants who work in Arabic get a mirrored English UI that reads as broken. Zoho, Odoo and Daftra ship full Arabic, so a buyer comparing them will reject Bonyan in the demo.
findings.recommendation: Adopt a real i18n layer (i18next or FormatJS) with ICU plurals. Extract every string, including engine error messages, validator issues, template and module names and field labels (store en/ar label pairs in the schema), and status names. Format all numbers, money and dates with Intl.NumberFormat / DateTimeFormat for ar-EG and en-EG, with an option for Arabic-Indic digits. Add a [dir=rtl] .flip { transform: scaleX(-1) } rule and mirror the stage-path polygon. Add a CI check that fails when a JSX text node is not translated. Arabic users should see 100% Arabic, including the printed tax invoice, with correct bidirectional handling of codes such as INV-2026-0001.
findings.auditor: Confirmed. i18n.ts DICT has 23 keys, not 26. Only Landing.tsx calls t(). Shell.tsx:43-95, Dashboard.tsx:22 and the other files listed are hard-coded English, and setLang only sets html lang/dir (i18n.ts:15-18). money() uses 'en-US' (engine.ts:168). monthLabel is English and gives 'May 26' (reports.ts:20-21). Calendar weekdays are hard-coded (ModuleView.tsx:253). No .flip rule exists, and the stage-path polygon is LTR-only (styles.css:351, not 308). Two corrections: Onboarding.tsx:88/208 and Suggest.tsx:40/89 do show template nameAr and challenge labelAr in Arabic. Several cited line numbers are wrong (Auth.tsx has only 89 lines). Severity stays critical for an Egypt-first launch, because the in-app Arabic toggle (Shell.tsx:75) produces a mirrored English UI. A stop-gap of hiding the toggle in the app is an S fix.

findings.title: Dashboards have no time: no date range, no period comparison, no targets, and the KPI 'sparkline' is a fixed decoration
findings.evidence: ReportDef (schema.ts:145-156) has no date field, period, comparison or target. FilterOp (schema.ts:137) has no relative date operators (this month, last 30 days, YTD). runReport (reports.ts:270-276) aggregates every record ever created. Every default KPI is all-time (packs.ts:41-46: 'Invoiced revenue', 'Deals won', 'Receivables'). The KPI card draws the same hard-coded wave path on every card (Chart.tsx:29-31, 'M0 30 C 30 10, 50 35...'), so it looks like a trend line but carries no data. Dashboard.tsx has no date picker. The subtitle under each KPI is '12 records' (Chart.tsx:28).
findings.impact: An owner cannot answer 'how are we doing this month compared with last month and with target?', the first question every BI tool answers. The fake wave is a data-visualisation integrity problem: users will read it as a trend. HubSpot, Zoho Analytics, Odoo and Power BI all have a global date filter with comparison to the previous period.
findings.recommendation: Add a dateField and a period to ReportDef: presets (Today, This week/month/quarter/year, Last N days, Fiscal YTD using company.fiscalYearStart) plus a custom range. Add a compareTo option (previous period or same period last year) and an optional target, either fixed or per month. Put a global period picker in the dashboard header that every widget inherits, with a per-widget override. Redesign the KPI card: the big value, a ▲/▼ delta % coloured by whether up is good, the comparison value in small text, a real 12-point sparkline (computed by runReport with __month grouping), and target progress. Delete the decorative wave.
findings.auditor: ReportDef (schema.ts:145-156) has no period, comparison or target field. FilterOp has no relative date operators. runReport (reports.ts:32-38, not 270-276) aggregates every non-void record. The KPI wave is a hard-coded path (Chart.tsx:29-30), and the subtitle is 'N records' (Chart.tsx:28). One small mitigation: a gt/lt filter on a date field with a literal ISO date gives a fixed range because compare() does string comparison (engine.ts compare), but nothing is relative or rolling.

findings.title: The owner's key numbers are missing from the home screen or sit on finance-only pages: cash, margin, overdue AR, stock risk, forecast
findings.evidence: The chart of accounts has 1100 Cash & bank (types.ts:47), but no dashboard report shows cash. Gross profit and margin % are calculated only in Accounting.tsx:22-30, which is gated by canPost (line 11). Ageing buckets exist (Accounting.tsx:55-78) but are not on the dashboard, so the 'Receivables' KPI cannot show how much is overdue. Inventory.tsx:115-116 calculates low-stock items, but the dashboard's 'Stock on hand' is a plain table of quantities (packs.ts:52) with no reorder flag. The weighted forecast is a grey footnote under the grid (Dashboard.tsx:72-79). The template reports cannot express cash, margin or overdue at all, because report measures are limited to one module field.
findings.impact: Owners open the app to answer five questions: cash today, who owes me and how late, will I hit the month, am I profitable, what is about to run out. Today they need three screens and finance rights. QuickBooks, Xero and Odoo all open on exactly these widgets.
findings.recommendation: Ship a system 'Owner cockpit' widget set computed by the engine rather than the generic report builder. Top row: Cash & bank (from the 1100 balance, with a 30-day trend), Receivables split into current and overdue (stacked bar of the ageing buckets, click to see the overdue list), Payables due in the next 7 days, Gross margin % this month versus last, and Weighted forecast against the monthly target. Second row: a cash-in/cash-out bar chart for 6 months, Top 5 overdue customers, Stock at risk (on hand ≤ reorder level, days of cover), and Pipeline coverage (open weighted ÷ target). Expose these as report 'sources' so the builder can also place them.
findings.auditor: Cash (1100) appears only in the trial balance, and margin only on Accounting.tsx:22-30, behind canPost. The forecast is a footnote (Dashboard.tsx:73-79). Overstated parts: a Receivables KPI does exist (packs.ts:46), and a 'Who owes us' hbar is added when late_collections is chosen (packs.ts:51). The low-stock count exists on Inventory.tsx:14/22 (not 115-116), not on the dashboard. The core gap is real: report measures are a single module field, so cash, margin % and overdue-vs-current cannot be built.

findings.title: Several default charts are visually wrong or misleading
findings.evidence: (a) The 'Pipeline by stage' funnel includes Won and Lost: packs.ts:47 has no __stagetype filter, and reports.ts:287-290 adds every stage. In the screenshot (dash-d.png) 'Lost EGP 1.7M' is the widest bar, so the 'funnel' shows the opposite of a funnel. (b) __month groups are not zero-filled (reports.ts:291-293), so months with no sales drop out and the 'Sales by month' line joins its neighbours, hiding the gap. (c) monthLabel prints 'May 26' (reports.ts:21), which reads as the 26th of May. (d) Bar and line charts use a fixed viewBox width of 520 with preserveAspectRatio="none" (Chart.tsx:105, 115), so axis text and points stretch with card width. In 'Tickets by stage' the labels are squashed to unreadable ('In progress', 'Waiting fo...'). (e) Y-axis ticks are max×0.25 steps passed through compact() (Chart.tsx:112, 125), giving '0.8, 1.5, 2.3' on a count chart. (f) The donut's slice colours come from each select option's own colour, so Facebook, Exhibition and Cold call all render purple in the screenshot. The legend is capped at 8 entries (Chart.tsx:96) while up to 24 slices are drawn. (g) Horizontal-bar labels truncate to 'Orient Sup...' twice with no way to tell them apart, and 'What we owe suppliers' (packs.ts:53) has no balance > 0 filter, so it shows EGP 0 rows.
findings.impact: A dashboard that misstates the pipeline or hides months with no sales damages trust in the whole product. A BI lead would reject these charts in review. Tableau and Power BI defaults avoid every one of these mistakes.
findings.recommendation: Make the funnel open stages only, with Won/Lost shown as a separate win-rate KPI. Zero-fill continuous date axes between the first and last period. Label months 'May 2026' (or 'مايو ٢٠٢٦'). Measure the container with a ResizeObserver and render at the true pixel width, keeping preserveAspectRatio meet. Use 'nice' tick generation (1/2/5×10^n) with integer ticks for counts. Give categorical series a validated categorical palette with distinct colours, fall back to it when option colours repeat, and group anything beyond the top 7 into 'Other'. Show full labels in tooltips, with mid-ellipsis truncation that keeps the label unique. Add balance > 0 to the payables pack. Add snapshot tests for Chart outputs.
findings.auditor: All points checked. (a) The funnel pack has filters: [] (packs.ts:47), and the screenshot shows Lost EGP 1.7M as the widest bar. (b) There is no zero-fill in the month branch (reports.ts:53-55). (c) monthLabel gives 'May 26'. (d) The chart uses W=520 with preserveAspectRatio='none' (Chart.tsx:105/115), and 'Tickets by stage' axis text is visibly squashed. (e) Ticks are max*0.25, giving '0.8, 1.5, 2.3' on a count chart. (f) Pie colours come from option colours, Facebook, Exhibition and Cold call are all purple in the screenshot, the legend is capped at slice(0,8), and rows go up to 24. (g) The payables pack has no balance>0 filter (packs.ts:53) and shows 'EGP 0'. Additional point: __month is the record's createdAt (engine.ts:593), not the invoice date (see MISS-02).

findings.title: Charts cannot be clicked through to the records behind them, and lists cannot take filters from a URL
findings.evidence: Chart.tsx renders static SVG and divs whose only interaction is a native <title> tooltip (lines 60, 91, 133-134, 145). The card header link goes to the unfiltered module (Dashboard.tsx:41, `/app/m/${r.module}`). ModuleView keeps its search and stage filter in local useState (ModuleView.tsx:31-33), with no URL search parameters, so no link can open a filtered list. Nothing lets a user filter the dashboard by owner, governorate or product.
findings.impact: Every serious BI tool, and HubSpot, Salesforce and Zoho CRM dashboards, lets the user click the 'Overdue' bar and land on the list of those invoices to act on them. Without that, the dashboard is a poster rather than a working tool, and users fall back to Excel.
findings.recommendation: Have runReport return, for each row, the record ids or a filter predicate. Make bars, slices, funnel steps and KPIs keyboard-focusable buttons that open `/app/m/:id?f=<encoded filters>&period=...`. Move ModuleView's filter state into useSearchParams so the 'Saved views' are URLs that can be shared. Add dashboard-level filter chips (Owner, Governorate, Product, Team) that apply to every widget whose module has that field.
findings.auditor: Chart marks have only <title> or title= tooltips. The card header link goes to the unfiltered module (Dashboard.tsx:41). ModuleView q/stage/sort are local useState (ModuleView.tsx:31-33), with no useSearchParams anywhere. Saved views live in ws.data.views, not in URLs. There are no dashboard-level filters.

findings.title: Keyboard and screen-reader access fails WCAG 2.2 AA in the main working screens
findings.area: Accessibility – ModuleView, Shell, RecordPage, Chart, Onboarding
findings.evidence: Table rows are `<tr onClick>` (ModuleView.tsx:133). A Playwright Tab walk of the Invoices list went from 'Save view' straight back to the sidebar, skipping every record. Sort headers are `<th onClick>` with no button and no aria-sort (ModuleView.tsx:122-127). The kanban registers only the PointerSensor (ModuleView.tsx:179; also ReportsTab.tsx:100), so cards cannot be moved by keyboard (2.1.1), and the report designer has no alternative to dragging (2.5.7). Search results and notifications are `<div onClick>` (Shell.tsx:67, 83). PaymentModal (RecordPage.tsx:313-326) and the health drawer have no role=dialog, no aria-modal, no focus trap and no Escape handling. The toast has no aria-live and is a clickable div (Shell.tsx:99-103). There is no skip link: 20 Tab stops come before page content.
