No :focus-visible style exists, and inputs remove the outline (styles.css:53). Segmented toggles and tiles have no aria-pressed (Onboarding.tsx:86, 232-233). The chart <svg role="img"> has no accessible name or data table (Chart.tsx:115). The whole app has only 19 aria-*/role attributes.
findings.impact: The product fails AA, which matters for government and enterprise buyers (the onboarding already offers a 'Government' customer type) and for power users who prefer the keyboard. It also lowers efficiency for every user.
findings.recommendation: Render each row's title cell as a <Link>, or use a roving-tabindex grid with Enter to open. Make headers <button> elements with aria-sort. Add KeyboardSensor with sortableKeyboardCoordinates plus a 'Move to stage…' menu on each card, and click-to-add buttons beside every draggable field. Build one accessible <Dialog> primitive (focus trap, Escape, return focus, aria-labelledby) and one <Popover> listbox for search and notifications. Make the toast region aria-live=polite (errors assertive). Add a skip link and a visible 2px :focus-visible ring token. Give charts aria-label summaries and a 'View as table' toggle. Add axe-core checks to CI with Playwright.
findings.auditor: Confirmed: <tr onClick> (ModuleView.tsx:133); <th onClick> with no aria-sort; PointerSensor only (ModuleView.tsx:179, ReportsTab.tsx:100); clickable divs for search and notifications (Shell.tsx:67/83); PaymentModal (RecordPage.tsx:309-328) has no dialog role, focus trap or Escape; the toast has no aria-live; no skip link; 19 aria/role attributes in total; the chart svg role=img has no name. Corrections: buttons keep the browser's default focus ring (no global outline:none), and inputs replace the outline with a primary border plus a box-shadow ring (styles.css:53), so the claim of 'no visible focus' is overstated. That ring colour (#dfe3ff) is only 1.27:1 against white. dnd-kit attributes do give kanban cards tabindex and role=button, but Enter does nothing, so cards can be focused but not opened or moved by keyboard.

findings.title: Colour contrast fails on the most important buttons, the KPI numbers and the status pills
findings.area: Visual design / styles.css and inline colours
findings.evidence: Measured ratios: white on success #059669 = 3.77:1 (button.success, styles.css:31). That colour is used for Post, Register payment, Convert to customer and Accept & invoice (RecordPage.tsx:70-83). White on the .glow gradient stops #a855f7 / #ec4899 = 3.96 / 3.53 (the main CTA on Landing and Auth). KPI values are painted in the report colour (Chart.tsx:27): #10b981 on white = 2.54 and #f59e0b = 2.15 (the 'Deals won 3' card). Stage and select pills use the option colour on colour+'22' (ModuleView.tsx:135, 172), about 2:1 for amber and green. Ageing 31-60 uses var(--warning) #d97706 = 3.19 (Accounting.tsx:69). The current stage-path step puts white text on the stage colour (styles.css:310), 2.15 for amber. --muted on --bg = 4.48. The Logo inherits link colour #5b5bf6 on the navy auth panel = 3.54 (visible in register-d-ar.png).
findings.impact: Text is hard to read in bright offices and on cheap screens, which fails AA (1.4.3 and 1.4.11). The money actions, the most important buttons, are the least readable.
findings.recommendation: Define semantic tokens with checked pairs: --success-solid #047857 (5.5:1 with white), --warning-text #b45309, --muted #5b6474. Render the KPI number in --text and use the series colour only for an accent bar or icon. Draw pills as tinted background + 700-shade text from a generated tonal scale per colour, so any user-picked colour stays at or above 4.5:1. Clamp user-chosen stage and module colours with a contrast check in the builder, and warn when they fail. Give the logo an explicit colour.
findings.auditor: I recomputed the ratios and they match: white on #059669 = 3.77; white on #a855f7/#ec4899 = 3.96/3.53; #10b981 = 2.54 and #f59e0b = 2.15 on white; option colour on colour+'22' = 1.94 (amber) and 2.24 (green); #d97706 = 3.19; --muted on --bg = 4.48; #5b5bf6 on #141441 = 3.54. The KPI value (2rem, weight 800) counts as large text, so the threshold is 3:1, and it still fails for green and amber. Cited CSS line numbers are off (button.success is styles.css:74). Severity lowered to medium: this is a real AA failure, but it is an S-sized token fix, not a structural one.

findings.title: The work app does not work on a phone; on mobile the landing page also hides Sign in and the Arabic switch
findings.evidence: At ≤760px the sidebar turns into a horizontally scrolling strip of more than 20 links (styles.css:351-352, 367), with no hamburger and no bottom navigation. The topbar wraps to three rows (search, language, bell, sync pill, a full-width user-switch <select>, sign out; styles.css:353-355), which uses about 200px before any content (dash-m.png). The invoice record page renders 802px wide at a 390px viewport and Accounting renders 437px (measured scrollWidth), because the lines table has fixed input widths (RecordPage.tsx:271-290). The calendar hides every event on mobile (styles.css:391). The landing page hides `.nav .btn.secondary, .nav button.ghost` (styles.css:358), so a phone visitor gets neither Sign in nor the العربية toggle (welcome-m-en.png shows only 'Build my system').
findings.impact: Egyptian field sales reps, medical reps and storekeepers work on phones, often over WhatsApp. Pipedrive, HubSpot and Zoho have strong mobile web and native apps. Returning users cannot sign in from the mobile landing page at all.
findings.recommendation: Mobile shell: a 56px top bar (logo, search icon, bell, avatar menu that holds language, user switch and sign out) and a bottom tab bar (Home, Pipeline, Quick add +, Tasks, More). Show documents on mobile as a stacked line-card editor (product, qty × price, swipe to delete) with a sticky total and primary action. Use a list or agenda view for the calendar on mobile. Restore Sign in and the language toggle in the mobile nav. Add a 390px and 768px Playwright check that scrollWidth equals clientWidth on every route.
findings.auditor: Confirmed: the horizontal sidebar strip and wrapping topbar (styles.css:390-410); the invoice page overflows at 390px (screenshot invoice-m-top shows content out to about 800px even though the lines table sits in an overflowX wrapper, because the grid column does not shrink); calendar events are display:none on mobile (styles.css:434), and the underlined day number is a plain span with no click handler, so events cannot be reached at all; the Sign in link and language button are hidden (styles.css:401). Correction: returning users can still sign in from mobile through /register, which links 'Already registered? Sign in' (Auth.tsx:80), so 'cannot sign in at all' is overstated. It is still a discoverability bug.

findings.title: Getting started takes too long, and the promise to remove sample data later is broken
findings.evidence: Suggest.tsx:260-266 always routes to /builder. The owner then faces a 7-tab builder with a three-pane form editor (builder-d.png) and must find 'Publish & go live' (Builder.tsx:91) before seeing a single working screen. The data is seeded only on first publish (Builder.tsx:64-69). Onboarding adds a fixed 2.6s 'Designing your system…' animation (Onboarding.tsx:32-35, 46-68) with checkmarks that reflect no real work. Suggest.tsx:97 promises 'Remove it any time from Settings', but SettingsTab.tsx has no such control and nothing in the codebase removes sample data. Demo users (seed.ts:33-41) and sample invoices stay in the real books.
findings.impact: Simplicity (criterion 8) is decided in the first ten minutes. monday.com and HubSpot drop the user into a working board immediately and leave customising for later. Leaving sample invoices in the general ledger with no way to purge them corrupts the books and breaks a promise made on screen.
findings.recommendation: On Suggest, make 'Start using it now' the primary action (publish v1 with defaults) and 'Customise first' secondary. Inside the app, add a 'Setup checklist' card (add a logo, invite a team-mate, import customers, adjust the pipeline, post your first invoice) that deep-links into the builder. Replace the fake animation with a real ≤600ms transition. Tag every seeded entity (demo:true on records, journal entries, stock moves and payments) and add 'Remove sample data' to the Company tab and the dashboard banner. It should reverse the entries through the engine and leave the books balanced.
findings.auditor: Confirmed: Suggest.tsx:30 always calls nav('/builder'); seeding happens only on first publish (Builder.tsx:64-69); there is a fixed 2.6s timer with cosmetic checkmarks (Onboarding.tsx:32-35); the 'Remove it any time from Settings' copy is at Suggest.tsx:97, and SettingsTab has no such control. Severity raised to critical: sample data is on by default (useState(true), Suggest.tsx:17), and seed.ts:156-175 calls postDocument and registerPayment, so sample invoices and bills write real journal entries and consume the gapless INV numbering. Only users carry demo:true (seed.ts:36), and records, journal entries and payments carry no tag. The company's real first invoice will therefore not be INV-0001, and the GL can only be cleaned by voiding each sample document, which still leaves the entries in the books.

findings.title: Daily data entry needs too many clicks: no type-ahead pickers, bulk actions, inline edit or shortcuts
findings.evidence: The customer, link and product pickers are native <select> elements listing every record (RecordPage.tsx:228-233, 280-283). There is no search, no recent items and no 'create new' option inside the picker. Post is disabled until the user saves (RecordPage.tsx:80, title 'Save first'), so posting is always Save → Post. There is no unsaved-changes guard on the back arrow or the sidebar (RecordPage.tsx:61). The list has no row selection, bulk assign, stage, delete or export, and no inline cell edit (ModuleView.tsx:132-140). Saved views use window.prompt (ModuleView.tsx:39) and deletes use window.confirm (RecordPage.tsx:86, 154). There is no command palette and no keyboard shortcut anywhere. Creating a 3-line invoice for an existing customer takes about 16 interactions: New → customer select → date ×2 → Add line ×3 with product, qty and price → Save → Post.
findings.impact: Sales and accounts staff repeat these flows dozens of times a day. Odoo's many2one type-ahead with 'Create and edit…', Zoho's inline edit and Linear's Cmd-K set the expectation. With 500 products a native select is unusable.
findings.recommendation: Build a <RecordPicker> combobox: type-ahead with Arabic normalisation (أ/إ/ا, ة/ه, ى/ي), recent items, the last price for this customer, stock on hand, and 'Create “…”' in a side sheet. Add a 'Save & post' split button, and Ctrl+S / Ctrl+Enter. Prompt before leaving when the form is dirty, using useBlocker. Add row checkboxes with a bulk action bar (assign owner, change stage, export, delete with undo), inline editing of list cells, and a Cmd/Ctrl-K palette for navigation, 'New invoice' and record search. Replace prompt() and confirm() with in-app dialogs, and offer Undo where reversible.
findings.auditor: Native selects list every record (RecordPage.tsx:228-233, 280-283). Post is disabled when dirty ('Save first', RecordPage.tsx:80). There is no unsaved-changes guard. The list has no bulk actions or inline edit. prompt() is used for views (ModuleView.tsx:39) and confirm() for void/delete (RecordPage.tsx:86/154). There are no shortcuts. The Save → Post friction is worse than described because the dirty flag often never clears after a save (see MISS-01).

findings.title: A posted document still looks like an editable form, and status and date labels are inconsistent
findings.evidence: A locked invoice renders disabled <select> and <input> controls that look editable (invoice-d.png; RecordPage.tsx:113-121, 280-290). A paid, posted invoice still shows a red Delete button (RecordPage.tsx:153) and relies on the engine to refuse. The header can hold 6 actions of equal weight (lines 69-89) with no overflow menu. Status pills print raw engine values in English lower case: 'paid', 'posted', 'instapay' (ModuleView.tsx:136, RecordPage.tsx:66, 128). Date formats are mixed on one screen: browser-locale mm/dd/yyyy in inputs, ISO '2026-10-18' in payments and tasks, and toLocaleString in history. The print view (RecordPage.tsx:330-380) has no logo, no seller or buyer address, no Arabic, and no QR code, although the Egyptian Tax Authority's e-receipt requires one.
findings.impact: Users cannot tell at a glance what is final. Odd labels and dates look unprofessional next to Xero and Zoho Books, and the printed invoice is the thing the customer sees.
findings.recommendation: Show posted, paid and void documents as a read-only document view: a paper-style layout with a status ribbon, payment timeline and a Payments tab, plus 'Duplicate as draft' and 'Void' in a ⋯ menu. Hide actions the user cannot take. Map statuses to translated labels with icons (Draft, Posted, Partly paid, Paid, Void). Use one date formatter (d MMM yyyy / ١٨ أكتوبر ٢٠٢٦) throughout. Redesign the print template as bilingual Arabic and English, with the logo, both tax IDs, the ETA-compliant QR code and the amount in words.
findings.auditor: Confirmed: a locked document renders disabled inputs and selects (RecordPage.tsx:117, 280-290); Delete is shown whenever the role can delete (RecordPage.tsx:153), and the engine refuses posted documents (engine.ts deleteRecord); raw lower-case status strings are printed (RecordPage.tsx:66, ModuleView.tsx:136); dates are mixed (ISO in payments and tasks, toLocaleString in history); the print view has no logo, addresses, Arabic or amount in words (RecordPage.tsx:330-380). Corrections: the most header actions I can construct is 5 (a quote: Mark sent, Accept, Declined, Print, Save), not 6. An ETA QR code is mandatory on B2C e-receipts. A B2B e-invoice instead needs ETA submission and the UUID, and a QR code is not the defining requirement there.

findings.title: Everyone gets the same flat 13-card home screen, regardless of role
findings.evidence: Dashboard.tsx:14 shows every report whose module the user can view, so a sales rep sees company 'Invoiced revenue' and 'What we owe suppliers'. There is no per-role dashboard and no 'my' scope: ReportDef has no owner = me filter, and FilterOp eq has no current-user token. The 13 cards have equal visual weight, sized 1-3 columns with no hero row (dash-d.png). 'Recent activity' is flooded with 'Automation ran' and 'created Task' entries, all at the same second (Dashboard.tsx:64-71). 'My tasks' shows raw ISO dates, near-duplicate 'Collect payment' tasks, and no Overdue / Today / Upcoming grouping (Dashboard.tsx:46-60). The greeting is English-only with an emoji (Dashboard.tsx:21).
findings.impact: This raises cognitive load, the very Salesforce/SAP problem the product promises to avoid. Each role should open to 'my work', and only the owner should see company-wide financials.
findings.recommendation: Add dashboards[] to the schema, each with roles[] and a layout. Ship role presets: Owner (cockpit, see UX-03), Sales rep (my pipeline, my targets, today's follow-ups, rotting deals), Finance (cash, overdue, VAT due, documents to post or approve), Warehouse (reorder list, incoming purchases, today's deliveries). Add a 'me' filter token. Show a Today strip on top (overdue, due today, approvals waiting) with one-click actions. Collapse automation events into one line ('6 reminders created') and let users filter activity by person or type.
findings.auditor: Dashboard.tsx:14 filters reports only by module view permission. There is no per-role dashboard and no 'me' token (compare() has no current-user token). The screenshot shows activity flooded with identical-second 'Automation ran' and 'created Task' rows, near-duplicate 'Collect payment' tasks and raw ISO dates. The greeting has an emoji (Dashboard.tsx:22).

findings.title: No monitors, alerts, scheduled reports, dashboard export or TV mode
findings.evidence: ReportDef has no thresholds or alert rules (schema.ts:145-156). The only push channel is the in-app bell (Shell.tsx:76-86). Notifications are created only by automations, mentions and reorder levels. Dashboards cannot be exported to PDF, PNG or XLSX; the only export is a module CSV (ModuleView.tsx:60-70). No scheduled digest, share link or wallboard mode exists. grep finds no 'schedule', 'email' or 'pdf' in ReportsTab or Dashboard.
findings.impact: Owners of small companies do not log in daily. They expect a Sunday-morning WhatsApp or e-mail digest and an alert when cash or collections cross a line, as Zoho Analytics, HubSpot and Power BI subscriptions offer. Without these, the dashboards go unseen.
findings.recommendation: Add per-widget monitors (a condition such as 'Overdue AR > EGP 200K' or 'Stock below reorder', delivered by bell, e-mail or WhatsApp to a chosen role) and a weekly 'Business pulse' digest rendered on the server with KPI deltas. Add 'Export dashboard' to PDF in both languages and XLSX of the underlying rows, plus a full-screen auto-refresh TV mode for sales floors and warehouses.
findings.auditor: There are no thresholds, schedules or exports in ReportDef or ReportsTab. Notifications exist only in the in-app bell (Shell.tsx:76-86). The only export is the module CSV (ModuleView.tsx:60-70).

findings.title: Too few chart types and analysis options to compete with BI-grade peers
findings.evidence: ChartType has 7 values: kpi, bar, hbar, line, pie, funnel, table (schema.ts:136). A report has one group-by and one measure (schema.ts:151-152), so it cannot do stacked or grouped bars (pipeline by stage × owner), bar + line combos (revenue against margin %), targets or bullets, gauges, heatmaps (activity by weekday × hour), scatter, pivot or matrix tables, or a map. Templates already capture the 27 governorates, but nothing draws them on a map. Date grouping is monthly only (reports.ts:291-293); there is no week, quarter or year. There are no ratio measures (win rate, average deal age, conversion %, DSO).
findings.impact: This criterion asks to 'beat the global peers' on visuals. Zoho CRM Analytics, HubSpot custom reports and Odoo's pivot and graph views all offer a second dimension, pivots and ratios. An owner cannot build the win rate by rep that most sales meetings start with.
findings.recommendation: Extend ReportDef with a secondary series (splitBy), multiple measures with a per-series chart type, calculated measures (a formula over aggregates using the existing formula.ts parser), and a date grain (day, week, month, quarter, year, fiscal year). Add chart types: stacked/100% bar, combo, bullet/target, gauge, heatmap, pivot table with subtotals, and an Egypt governorate choropleth (bundled SVG). Expose these as visual presets ('Win rate by rep', 'Collections vs target', 'Sales by governorate') so SMEs never configure axes by hand.
findings.auditor: ChartType has 7 values. ReportDef has one groupBy and one measure. Date grouping is monthly only, for both __month and date fields (reports.ts:53-55). There are no ratio or calculated measures. Accurate as stated.

findings.title: Loading, error and empty states are bare text or a fleeting toast
findings.area: App states – App.tsx, useApp.ts, Shell, Dashboard
findings.evidence: Loading shows plain 'Loading…' text (App.tsx:24, 36, 43) with no skeleton. There is no React error boundary anywhere (grep), so one render error blanks the whole app. Every engine and validation error appears only as a toast that disappears after 6s (useApp.ts:201-206, 228-231), never inline on the field that failed (for example 'Amount is required' or 'stage gate'). The sync pill 'Not saved, retrying…' (Shell.tsx:87-89) offers no detail, no retry-now and no offline explanation. The empty dashboard 'No reports for your role yet.' has no action (Dashboard.tsx:28-33). Empty module states are the same generic copy for every module (ModuleView.tsx:107-111).
findings.impact: Users cannot recover by themselves (Nielsen heuristic 9) and will call support. If a save keeps failing quietly, data is lost and users stop trusting the product.
findings.recommendation: Make EngineError carry fieldKey, ruleId and fix-hint so RecordPage can show an inline message under the field and focus it. Add a route-level error boundary with 'Reload' and 'Report problem' (attach diagnostics). Use skeleton cards matching the dashboard grid. Make the sync pill a popover that shows the last saved time, the error reason and a 'Retry now' button, and add an offline banner. Write empty states per module role (for example Invoices: 'Create your first invoice' or 'Import from Excel', with a 20-second explainer).
findings.auditor: Loading is plain text (App.tsx:24/36/43). grep finds no error boundary. Error toasts clear after 6s (useApp.ts:16, not 201-206). EngineError carries only a message, so nothing is shown inline on the field. The sync pill has only a title tooltip (Shell.tsx:87-89). The empty dashboard has no action, and the empty-module copy is generic (ModuleView.tsx:107-111).

findings.title: The visual identity is a generic AI-gradient look with no system behind it, no dark mode and no reduced-motion support
findings.evidence: The brand is the same indigo→violet→pink gradient as countless SaaS templates (styles.css:22 --hero, 33 .glow, 58 .logo-mark, 94 .cta, 109 progress, 133 orb). Corner radii include 6, 7, 8, 10, 11, 12, 14, 16, 18, 20, 22 and 28px with no scale. Dozens of hard-coded hex colours sit inline in TSX and bypass the tokens (Dashboard.tsx:29, Accounting.tsx:27-30, Inventory.tsx:120-124, Onboarding.tsx:93, 207). There is no prefers-color-scheme dark theme and no prefers-reduced-motion handling, yet .mock floats infinitely (styles.css:67) and .orb spins (styles.css:133). Emoji appear in product UI ('👋', '🎉', Dashboard.tsx:21, 49). The type scale is ad hoc (0.7–0.98rem in many steps).
findings.impact: The product does not look premium or memorable next to Linear, Attio or Notion, and the brand name (بنيان, 'structure') is not expressed anywhere. Inconsistent tokens make future polish and white-labelling expensive.
findings.recommendation: Build a brand and design-system sprint. Concept: 'بنيان = structure', a grid and brick motif, a deep ink-teal primary (e.g. #0F4C5C) with a warm sandstone accent (#E2A64B) for a local, trustworthy feel, and the gradient used only for marketing hero moments. Use an 8-step type scale with IBM Plex Sans Arabic + Inter (or Cairo kept for Arabic, matched x-heights), a 3-step radius scale (6/10/16), 4px spacing, and elevation tokens. Generate tonal scales (50–900) for semantic and categorical colours. Add a dark theme, reduced-motion overrides and a documented component library (Button, Pill, Card, KPI, Dialog, Combobox, DataTable), and lint against inline hex colours.
findings.auditor: Verifiable parts confirmed: there is no dark theme and no prefers-reduced-motion. .mock floats infinitely (styles.css:110) and .orb spins (styles.css:176), and the infinite .mock animation also touches WCAG 2.2.2. Inline hex colours are used (Accounting.tsx:27 '#0ea5e9', Inventory.tsx:18 '#f59e0b', Dashboard.tsx:29). Emoji appear in the UI. 'Generic AI-gradient look' and the proposed teal/sandstone palette are design opinion, not defects. Line numbers are off.

findings.title: Builder problems: tabs cut off at 1440px, report fields can only be dragged, and the dashboard layout is not visual
findings.evidence: At 1440px wide the builder tab bar clips 'Company' to 'C' with a hidden scrollbar (builder-d.png; .btabs overflow-x:auto with scrollbar-width:none, styles.css:156). Report fields can only be dragged with the PointerSensor (ReportsTab.tsx:100, 131-132); there is no click-to-add. Dashboard order is changed with 13px up/down chevrons in a side list (ReportsTab.tsx:82-84) rather than on a WYSIWYG canvas, and width is limited to Small/Wide/Extra wide with no height. Deleting a report has no confirmation and no undo (ReportsTab.tsx:139). The module header repeats the module name in an input and a badge.
findings.impact: The builder is the product's main differentiator, yet arranging the dashboard (criterion 9: flexibility) feels like filling in a form. Hidden tabs are a discoverability bug.
findings.recommendation: Put rarely used tabs into an overflow 'More' menu, or move the tabs into a left rail. Add a drag-and-resize dashboard canvas on a 12-column grid (react-grid-layout or dnd-kit sortable) with live data, an 'Add widget' gallery of presets, and click-to-add on every draggable item. Add undo and redo across the builder draft (an operation stack in useDraft) and a toast with Undo for deletions.
findings.auditor: Confirmed: .btabs uses overflow-x:auto with scrollbar-width:none (styles.css:199); fields can only be dragged ('Drag fields into the boxes', PointerSensor only); order is set with 13px chevrons (ReportsTab.tsx:82-84); there are only three widths; the delete button deletes immediately with no confirm or undo (ReportsTab.tsx ~139).

findings.title: Every render recomputes over all records, so the interface will lag as data grows
findings.evidence: Dashboard.tsx:37 calls runReport for every report on every store change, scanning every record and resolving lookups and rollups for each. Shell.tsx:49 calls list() for each module to draw the sidebar counts on every render. Global search filters every visible module on every keystroke, with no debounce (Shell.tsx:35-37). ModuleView renders all rows, with no pagination or virtualisation (ModuleView.tsx:132). All of this runs against one JSON document per workspace (store.ts).
findings.impact: With a year of data (5-20k records), typing in search, dragging a card or opening the dashboard will stutter on mid-range laptops and phones. Users read slowness as complexity, which undermines criterion 8.
findings.recommendation: Memoise report results keyed on (report def, data version), run heavy aggregations in a Web Worker, debounce search by 150ms and back it with a prebuilt index, add virtualised tables (TanStack Virtual) with server-side paging once records leave the single JSON document, and set a performance budget (interaction under 100ms at 10k records) in CI.
findings.auditor: runReport runs un-memoised for every report on every render (Dashboard.tsx:37), search has no debounce (Shell.tsx:35-37), and ModuleView renders every row without virtualisation. Correction: the sidebar's list(ws, m.id).length (Shell.tsx:49) is a cheap array lookup, not a scan. Heavier hotspots the panel missed: the ModuleView sort comparator calls fieldValue() or score() on every comparison (ModuleView.tsx:48-58), and relatedRecords() scans every record of every module on each RecordPage render (RecordPage.tsx:177-185).

findings.title: Global search matches titles only and offers no commands
findings.evidence: Shell.tsx:35-37 matches recordTitle only, takes the first 4 per module, and renders results as click-only divs (line 67) with no arrow-key navigation. It has no recent records, no commands ('New invoice'), no matching on phone, e-mail, invoice number or tax ID, and no Arabic letter normalisation. The placeholder is clipped in RTL (board-ar.png).
findings.impact: Staff look up a customer by phone number from a WhatsApp chat many times a day. Search is the fastest route in any CRM, and Attio and Linear set the standard here.
findings.recommendation: Build a Cmd/Ctrl-K palette that searches indexed key fields (phone, e-mail, number, SKU, tax ID) with Arabic normalisation, groups results by module, offers actions (Create, Go to, Switch language), supports full keyboard navigation (combobox ARIA pattern), and shows recent items when empty.
findings.auditor: Shell.tsx:35-37 matches recordTitle only, caps results at 4 per module and 10 overall, renders click-only divs with no keyboard navigation, and has no Arabic normalisation or commands. ModuleView's local search does match visible list columns (ModuleView.tsx:46), but global search does not.

findings.title: Dashboards offer no AI-generated insight, explanation or natural-language questions
findings.evidence: The only 'smart' features are rule-based: the builder health check (validate.ts, Builder.tsx) and lead scoring and rotting. Nothing on the dashboard explains changes, flags anomalies or answers questions. The workspace never surfaces the health check, and runtime data-quality problems (deals with no owner, invoices overdue more than 90 days, products with no cost) are not diagnosed anywhere a user sees.
findings.impact: Criterion 11 and 'beat global peers' set the bar at HubSpot Breeze, Zoho Zia and Salesforce Einstein. These already write 'Collections slowed 22% versus last month; 3 customers make up 70% of the overdue amount' and answer questions asked in plain language.
findings.recommendation: Add an 'Insights' rail on the Owner dashboard. A deterministic anomaly layer (period deltas, concentration, stale pipeline, data-quality checks run on live data) produces facts, and an LLM writes them up in Arabic or English with links to the filtered lists. Add 'Ask Bonyan' for questions in plain language that compile to ReportDef JSON, which can then be saved as a widget. Add a runtime 'System health' page for admins that lists data-quality issues with one-click fixes.
findings.auditor: No insight, anomaly or natural-language feature exists in the workspace. The validate.ts health check appears only in the builder (Builder.tsx). Severity raised from low to medium because the user explicitly asked for AI-assisted diagnosis (criterion 11), and runtime data-quality problems are surfaced nowhere.

findings.title: After editing a saved draft, 'Post' stays disabled ('Save first') and Save stays enabled, because the form never resyncs after a save
findings.evidence: RecordPage.tsx:28 seeds local `values` from rec.values only once (useState initialiser). The Editor is keyed by rec.id (line 22), so it does not remount after a save. Line 36 computes dirty as JSON.stringify(values) !== JSON.stringify(rec.values). On save, engine cleanValues converts number-input strings to Number and trims text (engine.ts:180-181), recomputes formula fields (engine.ts:185), and applyTotals/setLines rewrite subtotal, tax, total and balance (engine.ts:371-388). The stored rec.values then differs from the stale local values, so dirty stays true and the Post button at line 80 stays disabled with the tooltip 'Save first'. Example: open a draft invoice, change a line quantity, click Save. The totals change in the store but not in local state, so Post never enables until the user navigates away and back. A brand-new record avoids this only because create navigates to a new key (line 41).
findings.impact: The single most important finance action, posting an invoice, looks broken right after the user does exactly what the tooltip asks. Users will report 'can't post' and lose trust in the product.
findings.recommendation: After a successful save, reset local state from the store: setValues({...fresh.values}) and setLinesState(fresh.lines), or key the Editor on rec.updatedAt. Compute dirty only over editable, non-computed keys after normalising them through the same cleaner. Add a 'Save & post' action and a vitest/RTL test for edit → save → post.

findings.title: The dashboard's 'Invoiced revenue' and 'Sales by month' include VAT and use the record creation date, so they disagree with the Accounting page
findings.evidence: packs.ts:41 and packs.ts:48 sum the field 'total', and applyTotals sets total = subtotal + tax (engine.ts:368-377). Accounting.tsx:22 shows Revenue as the net 4000 balance. In the seeded screenshots the dashboard shows 'Invoiced revenue EGP 390K' while Accounting shows 'Revenue EGP 341,905.00'. The gap is VAT collected, which under IFRS 15 is not revenue. Separately, '__month' resolves to rec.createdAt (engine.ts:593), not the invoice date or posting date, so an invoice dated last month but entered today is charted in this month.
findings.impact: The owner sees two different 'revenue' figures, and the dashboard one is overstated by about 14%. Monthly sales move between months depending on data-entry date, so the books and the dashboard never reconcile and the product's 'correct numbers' promise is undermined.
findings.recommendation: Change the default packs to measure 'subtotal' (net of VAT) and label them 'Net sales (excl. VAT)'. Add a document 'posted date' pseudo-field and make '__month' on document modules use values.date or the posting date. Add a test that the dashboard net sales equal the 4000 credit balance for the same period.

findings.title: The Stock page and the dashboard forecast ignore role permissions, showing cost, margin and pipeline to every role
findings.evidence: Shell.tsx:53 shows the 'Stock' nav item whenever a products module exists, with no can() check. Inventory.tsx:7-14 has no permission check either and renders stock value, average cost, price and margin % per item (lines 20, 41-44), so any signed-in role can open /app/inventory, including one without view rights on products. Dashboard.tsx:73-79 computes and prints the weighted deals forecast without checking can(user, deals, 'view'). The schema has no field-level permissions (grep finds no hidden or fieldAccess setting), so cost cannot be hidden from sales roles anywhere.
findings.impact: Sales reps and support staff see purchase costs and margins, which is commercially sensitive information that SMEs routinely hide. The role matrix the builder advertises is not enforced on these screens.
findings.recommendation: Gate the Stock link and route with can(products, 'view'), and show the cost, margin and value columns only to finance or admin roles. Wrap the forecast footnote in can(deals, 'view'). Add field-level visibility per role in RolesTab (a 'hide cost and margin' preset) and enforce it in displayValue, export and reports.

findings.title: Sample data shows a bankrupt company, and the KPI cards mislabel negative balances
findings.evidence: With the default seed, the trial balance (acct-d.png) shows 1100 Cash & bank at EGP -1,547,225.10, because seed.ts:150-157 buys about EGP 2M of stock and pays bills while collections are about 181K. The card 'VAT payable (output − input)' shows EGP -236,985.70 (Accounting.tsx:24, 32), but a negative value is a VAT credit or receivable, not a payable. 'Customers owe you' and 'Gross profit 70%' sit next to an inventory balance of EGP 1.93M. The sign and label are never adjusted.
findings.impact: The first dashboard a prospect sees describes an insolvent business and a confusing VAT position. Accountants doing a demo will question the engine, even though the double entry itself balances.
findings.recommendation: Calibrate the seed so purchases are about 40-60% of sales, collections exceed supplier payments, and cash ends positive. Make the VAT card switch its label ('VAT payable' or 'VAT credit carried forward') and colour by sign. Show negative asset balances, such as an overdrawn bank, as an explicit warning rather than a plain number.

findings.title: One click on the stage path moves a deal straight to Won or Lost with no confirmation, reason or undo
findings.evidence: RecordPage.tsx:97-104 renders every stage, including the closed stages, as a button whose onClick immediately calls moveStage(...) with only a success toast. Kanban drops do the same (ModuleView.tsx:182-184, onDragEnd → moveStage). There is no confirm dialog, no lost-reason prompt and no undo, unless a stage gate demands fields.
findings.impact: A misclick or a drag that slips by a few pixels closes a deal as Lost. That distorts win rate and pipeline reports and fires stage automations. Salesforce, HubSpot and Pipedrive all ask for confirmation and a lost reason when a deal is closed.
findings.recommendation: Moving into a won or lost stage should open a small dialog (lost reason as a select, competitor, note) and fire automations only on confirm. Show an 'Undo' toast for 10 seconds on any stage move. Record the lost reason as a reportable field.

findings.title: Draft documents print as 'TAX INVOICE' with no draft watermark
findings.evidence: The Print button is shown for any document status, including draft (RecordPage.tsx:88). PrintView sets the title to 'Tax invoice' for every invoice (line 335) and prints only rec.number ?? 'DRAFT' in small monospace (line 351). A watermark is added only for void documents (line 376). Totals in the printout come from the current lines and do not depend on posting.
findings.impact: Staff can print or PDF an unposted, unnumbered draft that reads as a tax invoice and hand it to a customer, even though it never reached the ledger or ETA. This is a compliance and fraud risk and confuses customers.
findings.recommendation: For drafts, print the title 'Draft – not a tax invoice' with a diagonal DRAFT watermark, or allow only 'Pro-forma' printing. Reserve 'Tax invoice' for posted documents that carry their gapless number (and, later, the ETA UUID/QR).

panel: No-code Builder, Flexibility vs Guardrails, Workflow Logic
strengths: Templates are well made. I ran a scratch probe of all 9 templates against 7 answer variants (services-only, no teams, every challenge, no channels, and others): all 63 generated schemas validate with zero errors. Companion modules are auto-added correctly by recommend.ts:122-150.

Dependency-aware deletes. fieldDependents (validate.ts:33-71) and moduleDependents (validate.ts:73-85) list every report, formula, gate, lookup, rollup, rule, approval and automation that uses an item. ModulesTab shows the reason (ModulesTab.tsx:197-206, 418-423). This is better than Odoo Studio, which lets you break views silently.

Module roles with locked system fields and relation-role enforcement (roles.ts:22-117, validate.ts:100-101, 184-190) keep sales, stock and accounting semantics intact. This is the right 'guardrails' architecture for a citizen-builder product.
Safe formula language: a tokenizer and parser with no eval (formula.ts), type checks that only numeric fields are referenced, and circular-reference detection (validate.ts:139-162).

Pipeline structure is validated (open stages first, exactly one Won and one Lost, probability range) and the publish button is blocked on errors. The health panel has click-to-fix navigation to the offending tab and item (Builder.tsx:44-53, 125-134).
Engine actions are atomic: transact() runs on a structuredClone and commits only if nothing throws (store.ts:97-106), so a failed conversion or post leaves no half-written state.
Approvals stop counting once the record changes (engine.ts:720), and self-approval is blocked (engine.ts:753). These are sound design choices.
Onboarding is genuinely simple: 5 steps leading to a scored, explained template choice (recommend.ts:96-119). This is far less intimidating than Odoo app selection or Salesforce Setup.

scorecard.rationale: The happy-path flows are coherent and the template generation is solid (63 probed combinations, all error-free; 33 tests pass). But the flows break under realistic change. Re-onboarding or restoring after go-live orphans stages and roles (BUIL-01). Automations can mutate posted documents (BUIL-02). 'Updated' triggers duplicate tasks, and rollup conditions never fire (BUIL-04). Leads can be 'converted' without conversion (BUIL-07). Formula chains compute 0 (BUIL-09). The validator passes several of these.

The setup order (industry, sell model, customers, teams, challenges, template, builder, publish) is logical, and module roles plus companion checks keep the structure consistent. Logic within each module is shallow. There are no stage transition rules, no lost reasons, and no pipelines on custom modules. Approvals are single-step and header-only. There are no opening balances for go-live, and several onboarding answers are ignored.

This is the product's best dimension. Five plain-language steps, a scored and explained template, drag-and-drop fields and reports, and click-to-fix health issues make it far simpler than Odoo Studio or Salesforce Setup. Simplicity is undermined by misleading errors after schema changes (BUIL-03), false health errors (BUIL-10), the lack of undo or sandbox (BUIL-12), and Egypt-only defaults that are never asked about.

Custom modules, relations, lookups, rollups, conditional fields, validation rules, scoring and versioned publish give real flexibility, and the dependency guardrails are strong. Key controls and flexibility are missing: record-level and field-level security, multi-level approvals, field-change triggers, cross-record actions, webhooks and messaging, a richer formula language, layout and document designers, and configuration export/import. Guardrails are mostly UI-only and data-blind, so the flexibility it does offer can break control.

Automations exist (3 actions, 4 triggers) with loop prevention, but they run in the browser only when someone opens the app, have no run log or test mode, and failures surface as notifications only. The 'health check' is structural schema linting with an arbitrary score. There is no runtime diagnosis and no AI assistance.

vision: Best-in-class for this panel means an owner can reshape the system on a Tuesday afternoon without a consultant and without any risk to Wednesday's invoices. Every builder change is a reversible patch: undo works, and 'Changes since v12' shows a readable diff with author and note. Publishing opens an impact dialog ('37 deals sit in the stage you deleted — move them to: Negotiation'; '214 records lack the new required field — fill with default or enforce only on new records') and refuses to proceed until every live record, user and document stays valid. A sandbox copy lets the owner fire automations, approvals and posting on cloned data, then promote the change. Access is defined in one matrix with three layers: module rights, record scope (own, team or all) and field visibility, so a sales rep never sees cost or exports the whole customer base. Every pipeline, including custom modules like Projects and Production orders, has a state model with allowed transitions, gates, a mandatory lost reason and multi-step approvals that can test line discounts, price below cost and credit limits. Automations react to field changes and time offsets ('30 days before contract end, every 7 days until renewed'). They update linked records, create documents, and send e-mail, WhatsApp or webhooks from a server scheduler, and each has a test button and a run log. Implementers get an opening-balance wizard, stage-aware import and configuration export, so a partner can roll out 50 clinics from one master template. A 'System doctor' watches the live system (failing automations, empty fields, stuck approvals, records breaking current rules) and proposes one-click fixes, previewed as diffs. This combination of Odoo's depth, Zoho's flexibility, HubSpot's simplicity and stricter guardrails than any of them is what would let Bonyan compete head to head.

findings.title: Re-running onboarding or restoring a version silently replaces the live schema; publish has no data-aware migration check
findings.area: Builder / Onboarding → Suggest → Publish / Version restore
findings.evidence: App.tsx:50-51 guards /onboarding and /suggest with need='admin' only, so they stay reachable after go-live. Suggest.tsx:23-30 build() overwrites w.draft with a freshly generated schema without a confirmation step. generateSchema creates new uid() ids for stages (roles.ts:136-138) and for roles (packs.ts:114, uid('role')). My probe confirmed that two generations share no stage or role ids. SettingsTab.tsx:124 likewise restores any of the last 20 snapshots into the draft. Builder.tsx:50-73 publish() then calls only validate(schema), which takes no data argument (validate.ts:164), so nothing checks records, stock or users against the new schema. The data-safety guards (stage holds records, option in use, field has values) exist only as UI checks inside ModulesTab and PipelinesTab, and both paths bypass them.
findings.impact: An admin who clicks 'Change answers' in the live system, or restores v1, and then publishes will see: every deal, lead and ticket point at stage ids that no longer exist (they drop off boards and funnels); every non-admin user's roleId point at a deleted role, so can() returns false (engine.ts:28-33) and they are locked out; select values orphaned; and approvals lost. This is a one-click production outage with no undo other than finding the right older snapshot.
findings.recommendation: (1) Make validate(schema, data, published) data-aware. Emit errors when records sit in a missing stage, when a used option is missing, when users hold a missing role, when a field type or relation target changed while values exist, and when a field became required or unique while records violate it. (2) After first publish, block /onboarding and /suggest, or turn them into an 'Add a pack' wizard that merges modules instead of replacing the draft. (3) Before publishing, show a 'Publish impact' dialog that diffs draft against published and gives per-change record counts, plus a migration step for each breaking change (for example 'Move 37 records from deleted stage X to: [stage picker]', 'Map old option → new option', 'Fill the new required field for 120 records with a default'). Model it on Salesforce change sets and Odoo module upgrade.
findings.auditor: The core claim holds. Builder.tsx publish() (lines 50-73) calls only validate(schema), and validate.ts:164 takes no data argument. Suggest.tsx build() (line 23-30) overwrites w.draft with no confirmation. My probe confirmed that two generateSchema runs share 0 deal stage ids and only 'role_admin' among role ids (roles.ts:137 uid('st'), packs.ts:114 uid('role')). Three points are overstated. (1) Reachability: nothing in Shell or Builder links to /onboarding or /suggest. The only 'Change answers' button sits on /suggest itself (Suggest.tsx:36), so after go-live an admin has to type the URL. It is not 'one click in the live system'. (2) Module ids are stable (MODULE_IDS in roles.ts:122-134, and templates give custom modules fixed ids such as m_units), so records do not vanish at module level. Only stage ids, role ids and stage-bound automations or approvals break. (3) Restore is at SettingsTab.tsx:52, not :124. It has a confirm() and restores a cloned snapshot whose stage and role ids existed at that time, so the damage is limited to stages and roles created since. Rated high, not critical: the impact would be severe, but the path needs a deliberate URL or restore action. The recommended data-aware publish check is still the right fix.

findings.title: Automations can rewrite posted invoices and bills, which bypasses the immutability guardrail
findings.evidence: updateRecord refuses changes to posted documents (engine.ts:267), but execute() applies set_field directly through cleanValues (engine.ts:656-661). postDocument itself fires runWorkflows(ctx, rec, 'updated') right after posting (engine.ts:505). The validator only blocks readOnly targets (validate.ts:278-283). Probe: an 'Invoices / updated / set Due date = 2030-01-01' automation produced status='posted' with due_date=2030-01-01, and the only health-check message was a warning. Invoice date, due date, and any custom or system non-readOnly field can be changed this way.
findings.impact: Posted tax documents change after numbering. The invoice date no longer matches the journal date. AR ageing (engine.ts:878) and the collection automation run on the altered due date. This breaks the 'posted = immutable' promise in the README and the ETA e-invoice requirement that submitted documents never change. Auditors will reject it.
findings.recommendation: In execute(), apply the same guard as updateRecord: skip, and log 'skipped: document is posted', when mod.lines and rec.status is not draft. In validate(), make set_field on any document module an error unless the automation's conditions include __status = draft. Route all automation writes through updateRecord(…, {silent:true}) so field history and updatedAt (which approvals depend on, engine.ts:720) stay correct.
findings.auditor: updateRecord blocks posted documents (engine.ts:267), but execute() writes set_field through cleanValues directly (engine.ts:656-661), and postDocument fires runWorkflows(...,'updated') (engine.ts:505). Probe: an Invoices/updated/set due_date=2030-01-01 rule produced status 'posted' with due_date 2030-01-01. validate() gave 0 errors and only the generic warning at validate.ts:282. The write also does not touch updatedAt or field history, so approvals (engine.ts:720) and the audit trail cannot see it. The invoice date ('date') is changeable the same way, so the document and journal dates can diverge.

findings.title: Changing a published schema while data exists is unguarded for required, unique, gates and stage type; edits then fail with misleading errors
findings.area: Builder Modules & Pipelines / Engine save path
findings.evidence: The Required and No-duplicates toggles (ModulesTab.tsx:248, 251) do not check existing records. The stage Type select (PipelinesTab.tsx:125-129) can turn a stage that holds records into Won or Lost, which reclassifies history. Adding a stage gate (PipelinesTab.tsx:149) on a stage that already holds records makes updateRecord re-check the gate on every save (engine.ts:270). Probe: after adding a 'PO number' gate to the first deal stage, renaming a deal failed with 'To move to “Qualification”, fill in: PO number' although the user never moved it. Deleting a field with data needs only a confirm (ModulesTab.tsx:200), and a new field whose label slugifies to the same key 'resurrects' the old values under a different type.
findings.impact: After a routine builder change, the team finds old records uneditable, with error text that blames a stage move they did not make. Historic win rates change silently when a stage's type is flipped. This is the classic low-code failure (Airtable or Zoho without migration), and it generates support tickets and lost trust right after go-live.
findings.recommendation: At toggle time, show impact inline, for example 'Making this required: 214 records are empty. [Fill with default…] [Only enforce on new records]'. Store gates and required flags with an effectiveFrom version so they apply to new saves and stage entries only, as Salesforce validation rules can be scoped with ISNEW/ISCHANGED. Run checkGate only when the stage actually changes. Lock stage type when the stage has records. Keep deleted field keys as tombstones so the same key cannot be reused with a different type.
findings.auditor: The Required and No-duplicates toggles (ModulesTab.tsx:248, 251) have no data check. updateRecord re-checks the current stage gate on every save (engine.ts:270). Probe: after adding a 'PO number' gate to Qualification, renaming a deal failed with 'To move to “Qualification”, fill in: PO number'. The stage Type select (PipelinesTab.tsx:125-129) has no records check. The validator's exactly-one-Won rule forces a two-step flip, which is still possible. The delete-field confirm (ModulesTab.tsx:200) openly says values 'come back if you add a field with the same key'. Because slug-key reuse (ModulesTab.tsx:187-193) only avoids live keys, a new field of a different type can inherit the old values.

findings.title: Automation trigger semantics are unreliable: 'updated' fires on every save, rollup and lookup conditions never match, and date rules fire once forever and only when someone opens the app
findings.evidence: runWorkflows fires every 'updated' automation whose conditions match, on every save (engine.ts:638-641), and there is no 'field changed / changed to' trigger (TriggerType, schema.ts:158). Probe: 3 edits of a deal over 500 created 3 duplicate tasks. Conditions are evaluated with matches(ctx.schema, rec, w.conditions) without ws (engine.ts:640, 683), so lookup and rollup fields resolve to undefined (pseudoValue only computes them when ws is passed, engine.ts:586-589). Probe: an Accounts automation 'deal_count > 0' never fired, yet validate accepted it. runScheduled marks workflowRuns[w:rec] permanently (engine.ts:681-684), so an invoice whose due date is changed, or a recurring reminder, never fires again. It runs only in the browser when someone mounts Shell (Shell.tsx:23-28), and executes as that user. There is no 'N days before' offset, so an AMC renewal 30 days before End cannot be modelled.
findings.impact: Teams get spammed with duplicate tasks, which teaches them to ignore automations. Rules that look valid in the builder never run. Collections and renewals, the main SME pain points named in onboarding, are missed whenever nobody logs in, for example over Eid holidays. HubSpot workflows, Zoho Blueprint and Odoo automated actions all handle 'on field change', re-enrolment and time offsets.
findings.recommendation: Add trigger 'field changes' with optional 'from/to' (pass the before-values into runWorkflows). Always evaluate conditions with ws. Change date_passed to 'date is N days before/after' with an optional 're-run every N days until condition is false'. Key runs by w.id:rec.id:dateValue so a changed date re-arms the rule. Move runScheduled to a server cron (Supabase scheduled Edge Function, hourly) that runs as an 'Automation' system user.
findings.auditor: All parts reproduced. 3 saves of a deal over 500 created 3 duplicate tasks. runWorkflows calls matches() without ws (engine.ts:640, and 683 in runScheduled), so an Accounts rule on deal_count > 0 never fired although fieldValue returned 1, and validate gave 0 errors. runScheduled keys by w.id:rec.id (engine.ts:681), so a second run a month later fired 0. It runs only in Shell's mount effect (Shell.tsx:23-28), as the user who opened the app. TriggerType (schema.ts:158) has no field-change trigger or offset. The builder text itself says date checks run 'every time the app opens' (AutomationsTab.tsx:39).

findings.title: The automation action catalogue is too thin to replace a real process: 3 actions, no recipient choice, no cross-record updates, no messages or webhooks, no test run or log
findings.evidence: ActionDef offers only create_task, set_field and notify (schema.ts:160-163). The notify editor has no role or user picker (AutomationsTab.tsx:135-139); a role can only be set by packs (packs.ts:72). set_field can only write the triggering record, and the picker excludes relations (AutomationsTab.tsx:144). create_task always assigns owner, then assignee, then the current user (engine.ts:654). Run history is a single line in activity (engine.ts:669), and failures surface only as a notification (engine.ts:666). There is no 'test with record X' or dry-run.
findings.impact: Common SME flows cannot be built: 'Reservation reaches Reserved → set Unit.Status = Reserved' (real-estate template), 'Deal Won → create draft invoice/project', 'Invoice overdue → WhatsApp the customer', 'Ticket urgent → notify the service manager only'. Against HubSpot, Zoho Flow, monday automations or Odoo server actions, a buyer will see this gap within the first demo.
findings.recommendation: Add actions: update linked record (pick a relation, then field and value), create record in any module with field mapping (templated values), notify user/role/record owner (picker), send e-mail and WhatsApp template (queued server-side), call webhook (POST JSON, HMAC-signed, retry), and wait N days. Add a per-automation 'Runs' tab (time, record, result, error) and a 'Test on a record' button that runs in dry-run mode and shows what would change.
findings.auditor: ActionDef has only create_task, set_field and notify (schema.ts:160-163). The notify editor shows only a message box (AutomationsTab.tsx:135-139), and the role is reachable only through the pack's literal 'finance' (packs.ts:72). The set_field picker excludes relation fields and can only write the triggering record (AutomationsTab.tsx:144). Assignment is fixed: owner, then assignee, then current user (engine.ts:654). The run log is one activity line (engine.ts:669), and failures go only to a note (engine.ts:666). There is no dry run. This is a competitive gap rather than a correctness bug, so high is fair.

findings.title: Access control is module-level only: no record ownership scoping and no field-level security
findings.evidence: RoleDef holds only access: Record<moduleId, Permission[]> plus admin and finance flags (schema.ts:177-185). can() checks module and permission only (engine.ts:28-33). list() returns every record in a module (engine.ts:46-48), and ModuleView, global search (Shell.tsx:35-37) and CSV export (ModuleView.tsx:61-62) use it unfiltered. FieldDef has no permission attribute, so a sales role with view access to Products sees 'Average cost' (roles.ts:213) and margin data.
findings.impact: In an Egyptian SME the biggest data risk is a sales rep exporting the full customer and price list before leaving. Every serious competitor scopes records: Salesforce sharing rules and OWD, Odoo record rules, HubSpot 'team/owned only', Zoho territory. Hiding cost and margin from sales is a baseline expectation. Without it, owners will not put real data in.
findings.recommendation: Add to RoleDef, per module, a scope of 'all | my team | own' (owner, assignee or createdBy) enforced in list() and findRecord(), and a per-field visibility of 'hidden | read-only | edit' for each role, enforced in RecordPage, exports, reports and the engine's cleanValues. Add an 'Export' permission separate from 'view'. In the Access tab, show this as a third column group so it stays simple, as Zoho's profile matrix does.
findings.auditor: RoleDef is module-level only (schema.ts:177-185), can() checks only the module and permission (engine.ts:28-33), list() is unfiltered (engine.ts:46-48), and FieldDef has no visibility attribute. CSV export (ModuleView.tsx:61-70) needs only module view, and it exports every field, including 'Average cost' (roles.ts:213). One correction to the recommendation: every member downloads the whole workspaces.doc JSON (store.ts openFor/reload, read RLS at the migration's line 58-60). Filtering in list() or findRecord() would therefore hide data in the UI but not protect it. Real record or field scoping needs server-side storage per record or table, with RLS.

findings.title: Pipelines have no transition logic; leads can be 'Converted' without conversion; custom modules cannot have a pipeline
findings.evidence: moveStage allows any-to-any moves, including Lost to Won or out of Converted (engine.ts:313-327), from the stage bar (RecordPage.tsx:100) and the Kanban (ModuleView.tsx:116). Probe: moving a lead to 'Converted' on the stage bar created no customer or deal, and convertLead then refused with 'This lead is already converted' (engine.ts:336). No template defines a lost reason or a gate on the Lost stage (roles.ts:157-164). ROLES.custom has no pipeline (roles.ts:111-116; buildModule sets stages only when info.pipeline, roles.ts:298), so Projects, Units, Production orders and Site surveys use a plain Status select (templates.ts) with no board, gates, stage automations or approvals (validate.ts:303 requires stages for approvals).
findings.impact: Dirty funnel data (orphan converted leads, deals reopened from Lost), no loss-reason analytics, and the operational half of the 'ERP' (projects, production, units) gets none of the process control the sales half has. BPMN-wise there is no state model, only labels.
findings.recommendation: (1) Add allowed transitions per stage (default: forward to the next open stage, any stage to Lost, Won/Lost back only for Admin). Show them in the Pipelines tab as arrows. (2) Make the leads Won stage reachable only through convertLead, so the stage bar and board open the conversion dialog. (3) Ship a default 'Lost reason' select, gated on every Lost stage, and a 'Lost reasons' report. (4) Add a 'Use a pipeline' toggle on custom modules that converts a Status select into stages, so Projects and Production orders get boards, gates, approvals and stage automations.
findings.auditor: moveStage has no transition model (engine.ts:313-327). Probe: Lost to Won succeeded. Moving a lead to 'Converted' through moveStage created no customer, contact or deal, and convertLead then refused with 'This lead is already converted' (engine.ts:336). The Lost stages have no gate (roles.ts:147, 155, 163). Custom modules cannot get stages, because buildModule sets stages only when ROLES[role].pipeline is set (roles.ts:298), even though ModuleSpec accepts stages. Approvals require stages (validate.ts:303; RulesTab.tsx:120 disables Add approval).

findings.title: User-added required fields silently break records the system creates (automation tasks, lead conversion, quote→invoice), and conversion fabricates an amount of 1
findings.evidence: execute() creates Tasks with a fixed value set (engine.ts:655), and convertLead creates Account, Contact and Deal with fixed mappings (engine.ts:338-341). Neither ModulesTab (Required toggle, ModulesTab.tsx:248) nor validate() warns when a module the engine writes to gains a required custom field. Probe: adding a required 'Department' to Tasks gave 0 validation errors, and every task automation failed afterwards, visible only as a notification ('could not finish: Department is required'). convertLead sets amount = budget || 1 (engine.ts:340) to pass the default 'amount > 0' rule (packs.ts:164), which inflates pipeline count and value with EGP 1 deals.
findings.impact: A reasonable customisation disables all follow-up automation, and nobody notices for weeks. The pipeline is polluted with fake 1-unit deals. Lead conversion has no field mapping, so a company that adds 'Governorate' (required) to Customers cannot convert leads at all.
findings.recommendation: In validate(), emit an error such as '“Department” is required in Tasks, but automations create tasks without it. Give it a default or make it optional.' Do the same for Accounts, Contacts and Deals when Leads exist, and for Invoices when Quotes exist. Add a default value property to FieldDef. Replace the hard-coded conversion with a 'Conversion mapping' screen (lead field → customer, contact or deal field), as Salesforce lead mapping does, and open a conversion dialog that asks for the deal amount instead of inventing 1.
findings.auditor: Probe: after adding a required 'Department' to Tasks, validate() returned 0 errors. Creating a lead then left only the note 'Automation “Call every new lead within 24 hours” could not finish: Department is required'. convertLead sets amount = Number(budget ?? 0) || 1 (engine.ts:340). In the distribution template, without budget, the probe deal had amount 1. Conversion uses hard-coded pick() mappings (engine.ts:338-341).

findings.title: Formula fields compute wrong values silently: order-dependent chains, rollup references always 0, divide-by-zero returns 0, and no recalculation when a formula changes
findings.evidence: cleanValues evaluates formulas once, in field order (engine.ts:185). Probe: with_vat = net * 1.14, defined before net = amount * 0.9, stored 0 instead of 1026, and validate returned no error. Rollups are skipped in cleanValues (engine.ts:177) and are never in `out`, yet NUMERIC_TYPES includes 'rollup' (schema.ts:225), so the validator accepts formulas like total_invoiced - balance_due, which always evaluate to 0. Division by zero returns 0 (formula.ts:95). Values are stored at save time only, so changing a formula after publish leaves every existing record stale. The language has only + - * / (formula.ts:8), with no IF, ROUND, MIN/MAX, dates (DAYS_BETWEEN, TODAY) or text.
findings.impact: Wrong numbers on unit prices, commissions and margins, with no error shown. 'Days overdue', 'contract end − today' and 'IF(type = Villa, …)' cannot be expressed, although these are the formulas SMEs ask for first (Airtable, Zoho and Odoo all have them).
findings.recommendation: Topologically sort formulas (the cycle detector already builds the graph, validate.ts:139-162) and evaluate them in dependency order. Either compute rollups before formulas or reject rollup and lookup refs in the validator. Return null (shown as '—', with a warning) on divide-by-zero. Add IF, ROUND, MIN, MAX, ABS, DAYS(date1, date2) and TODAY(), with a function picker in the formula chips (ModulesTab.tsx:392-395). Add a 'Recalculate N records' step to publish when a formula changes.
findings.auditor: Probe: with_vat = net * 1.14, defined before net = amount * 0.9, stored net 900 and with_vat 0, and validate gave no error. The formulas are evaluated in a single pass in field order (engine.ts:185). 'rollup' is in NUMERIC_TYPES (schema.ts:225), so total_invoiced - balance_due validates cleanly but rollups are never in `out` (engine.ts:177), and the formula always gives 0. Divide-by-zero returns 0 (formula.ts:95). The grammar has only + - * / and parentheses. Stored values go stale when a formula changes. Medium is fair because the user has to define the chain in the wrong order.

findings.title: Validation rules offer fields the validator then rejects, cannot compare two fields, and all conditions are AND-only
findings.evidence: RulesTab's FieldPicker uses fieldOptions(mod), which includes pseudo fields __stage, __stagetype, __status, __month and __owner (ReportsTab.tsx:48-51; RulesTab.tsx:40-46, 67). validate.ts:197 checks rule fields with fieldByKey, so pseudo fields fail. Probe: a rule 'when Stage type = Won → amount > 1000' reports 'uses a field that no longer exists'. The engine also reads out[w.field] raw (engine.ts:210), so stage-conditional rules could not work anyway. Filters compare against literal values only (schema.ts Filter.value: string), and matches() uses .every() everywhere (engine.ts:599), so there is no OR and no grouping.
findings.impact: The builder offers an option that turns the health check red with a false message, which erodes trust in the guardrails. 'End date must be after Start date' (AMC contracts, installments, projects) and 'Discount OR credit-limit exceeded' cannot be expressed. Salesforce and Zoho validation rules are formula-based for exactly this reason.
findings.recommendation: Either support pseudo fields in rules (evaluate through pseudoValue) or filter them out of the rule picker. Add the value source 'another field' to FilterRow (for example 'End date' > field 'Start date'), and add ANY/ALL condition groups (one level of nesting is enough for SMEs), shared by rules, automations, approvals, reports and showIf.
findings.auditor: Probe: a rule 'when Stage type = won → amount > 1000' gives the error 'uses a field that no longer exists', because validate.ts:197 uses fieldByKey while RulesTab's FieldPicker offers PSEUDO_FIELDS through fieldOptions (ReportsTab.tsx:48-51). The engine evaluates rules on raw out[...] (engine.ts:210), and moveStage never runs rules at all (it calls only checkGate), so stage-conditional rules could not work even if the validator accepted them. Filter.value is a string literal (schema.ts:142), and matches() uses .every() (engine.ts:599).

findings.title: Approvals are single-step, header-only and bypassable, with no check that anyone can actually approve
findings.evidence: ApprovalRule has one approverRole and action 'post' | 'stage' only (schema.ts:124-133). Conditions test record values, so line-level discount %, price below cost or credit-limit breaches cannot trigger approval (filters cannot see rec.lines). guardApproval returns early for any approver-role user or admin without recording an approval (engine.ts:726-728), so a manager's own big deal or an admin's post leaves no sign-off trail. validate.ts:293-305 never checks that the approver role has members or view access to the module. The default 'Management' approver (packs.ts:167-172) is given view-only rights (packs.ts:102).
findings.impact: The controls SME owners care most about (discount above X%, selling below cost, exceeding the customer credit limit, which the distribution template captures as credit_limit but never enforces) cannot be configured. Requests can sit forever when the approver role is empty. Odoo, ERPNext and Dynamics BC all support multi-level, amount-tiered approvals with an audit log.
findings.recommendation: Allow ordered approval steps (step 1 Sales manager, step 2 Owner when total > X), approval on create, edit, delete and 'send quote', and conditions on line aggregates (max discount %, any line price < cost) and on lookup values (customer balance + total > credit limit). Always write an approval record, auto-approved with reason 'approver acted' when the actor is an approver. Add validator errors for approver roles with zero members or no view access, and add an escalation timeout.
findings.auditor: ApprovalRule is single-step with action 'post' or 'stage' (schema.ts:124-133). guardApproval returns early for approver-role users and admins without writing an approval (engine.ts:726-728). validate.ts:293-305 never checks role membership. One sub-claim is weaker than stated: the Management role being view-only (packs.ts:102) does not stop it approving, because decideApproval checks only canApprove (engine.ts:752). The approver simply cannot post afterwards. The distribution template's credit_limit (templates.ts:226) is indeed captured but never enforced. Filters cannot see rec.lines, so discount or below-cost approvals are impossible.

findings.title: No sandbox, undo, diff or authored change log, and builder edits share one JSON row with live transactions
findings.evidence: useDraft.edit() writes every keystroke into w.draft via update(), which autosaves to the cloud (useDraft.ts:11-17; store.ts:91-95). There is no undo stack. Draft and live data live in the same workspaces.doc row, so a conflicting save by any salesperson triggers reload(), which discards the builder's unsaved edits (store.ts:68-72). Publish records note 'Version N' with no author and no description, and keeps only 20 snapshots (Builder.tsx:62-63). There is no draft-vs-published diff view. The report preview uses sample data only when the workspace has no records (ReportsTab.tsx:34-36), and 'Switch user' acts on live data as that user (Shell.tsx:90-93). Deleting automations and reports has no confirmation (AutomationsTab.tsx:73), and changing an automation's module wipes its conditions and actions (AutomationsTab.tsx:80).
findings.impact: An admin can lose an hour of builder work to a background save by a colleague. A destructive change cannot be undone with Ctrl+Z. Nobody can answer 'who changed the discount approval last Tuesday, and what exactly changed', which ISO 27001 and SOX-style change management require. Testing an automation means firing it on real customers.
findings.recommendation: Store the draft in its own row (or table) separate from transactional data. Add an undo/redo stack in useDraft (keep the last 50 patches). Show a 'Changes since v12' panel listing added, removed and changed items, with a required change note and the author's name on publish. Keep unlimited history, with diffs only. Offer a sandbox: 'Test mode' clones the workspace data into a throwaway copy where automations and approvals can be exercised and then discarded, comparable to a Salesforce sandbox or an Odoo staging branch.
findings.auditor: Confirmed: useDraft.edit writes the whole draft on every keystroke into the same workspaces.doc row (useDraft.ts:11-17; store.ts:91-95). There is no undo or diff. Publish notes are 'Version N' with no author, and history is capped at 20. Automation delete has no confirm (AutomationsTab.tsx:73), and changing an automation's module wipes its conditions and actions (:80). Rules and approvals also delete without confirm (RulesTab.tsx:64, 131). Overstated: 'lose an hour of builder work' is not realistic, because flush runs 600ms after each edit (store.ts:45). A version conflict (store.ts:68-72) loses only the edits made since the last successful save, usually seconds, though it can repeat in a busy workspace. The same conflict path silently drops operational changes too, such as a just-posted invoice, which is the more serious data-loss angle for the data panel. Line refs: the history slice is Builder.tsx:63, and the preview logic is ReportsTab.tsx:31-44.

findings.title: Go-live migration and configuration portability are missing: no stage or status import, no opening balances or stock, no schema export or import
findings.evidence: importRows (engine.ts:785-807) calls createRecord without opts.stage, so every imported deal or ticket lands in the first stage. ImportModal offers only non-readOnly fields (ImportModal.tsx:44), so document lines, posted invoices, opening AR/AP and opening stock cannot be imported. Stock can only come from posted bills (engine.ts:474-498), and there is no opening-balance journal anywhere in src. There is also no code anywhere to export or import an AppSchema (JSON), to save a configured workspace as a reusable template, or to clone a workspace.
findings.impact: From an implementation lead's view this blocks go-live. A distributor moving from Excel or Odoo needs open customer balances, supplier balances, stock quantities with cost, and open pipeline stages on day 1. Faking it by posting dummy bills corrupts VAT input. The lack of configuration export also prevents a partner channel (one implementer setting up 50 clinics from a master config), which is how Odoo and Zoho scale in Egypt.
findings.recommendation: Add an 'Opening balances' wizard (cut-off date, then customer balances CSV, supplier balances CSV, stock quantity and unit cost CSV). It posts one opening journal per type against an Opening Balance Equity account and stock moves with ref 'OPENING', with no VAT. Allow mapping a Stage column on import. Add Export/Import configuration (versioned JSON with a schema-version field and a validator run on import), plus 'Save as my template' for partners.
findings.auditor: importRows calls createRecord without opts.stage (engine.ts:799), so every imported record lands in stage 1. ImportModal offers only non-readOnly, non-computed fields (ImportModal.tsx:44), and the Import button is hidden for document modules (ModuleView.tsx:82, `!mod.lines`). A search for 'opening' finds nothing in src, and stock only comes from posted bills (engine.ts:474-498). No code exports or imports an AppSchema.

findings.title: Onboarding asks questions it ignores and skips the ones that matter for correctness outside Egypt
findings.evidence: Answers.salesCycle and size (recommend.ts:15, 18), team sizes (TeamInput.size) and channels such as exhibitions, walkin and phone are collected (Onboarding.tsx:15-18, 157-160) but never used by suggest() or generateSchema(). buildWorkflows ignores challenges (packs.ts:61, `_challenges`) although step 5 promises 'We’ll add the reports and automations that fix them'. Country, currency, VAT rate and tax ID exist in Answers (recommend.ts:28-30) but no step asks for them; they default to Egypt, EGP, 14% and blank (recommend.ts:56-58). 'recurring' and 'projects' affect only the template score: no recurring-invoice or project-billing behaviour is generated.
findings.impact: Users feel the questions were theatre. A Saudi or UAE company gets EGP and 14% VAT unless it finds the Company tab, and currency locks after the first posting (SettingsTab.tsx:23). Expectations set by the 'fix' text go unmet.
findings.recommendation: Add a short 'Country & tax' step: country, then currency, VAT rate, e-invoicing regime (ETA, ZATCA, FTA) and tax-ID format. Use salesCycle to set rotDays and default stage probabilities, team size to pre-create user invites, and channels to populate the lead Source options. Make each challenge map explicitly to the automations it adds, and show 'Added because you said …' in Suggest. Drop any question that drives nothing.
findings.auditor: True: salesCycle, size and team sizes drive nothing. Country, currency, VAT and tax ID are never asked and default to Egypt, EGP, 14% and blank (recommend.ts:56-58). buildWorkflows ignores challenges (packs.ts:61). Overstated: channels whatsapp, facebook, website, tenders and field are used (neededFeatures and extraSpecs in recommend.ts). Challenges do drive buildReports (packs.ts:50-55) and extraSpecs (recommend.ts:131-138, for example lost_leads adds Leads, which brings the call-back automation). So most 'fix' promises are met indirectly. Only the specific channels exhibitions, walkin, phone and referral are unused.

findings.title: Validator blind spots: orphan user roles, deleted option or stage values in filters, notify role ids, set_field value types
findings.evidence: validate() checks only that filter fields exist (validate.ts:254, 274, 304), not that filter values are valid. A report filter 'Stage = <deleted stage id>' or 'Priority = <removed option>' passes and silently returns 0. Users are not validated: my probe added a user with roleId 'role_missing' and got 0 role issues. Notify roles are never checked (packs.ts:72 uses the literal 'finance', which only works because Shell.tsx:32 special-cases it). set_field values are not type-checked: a text value written into a number or currency field fails at runtime inside a try/catch (engine.ts:660, 665). The PipelinesTab gate picker shows only the first 14 fields (PipelinesTab.tsx:146), and checkGate treats 0 as empty (engine.ts:309).
findings.impact: Dashboards that quietly show zero, automations that fail at runtime instead of at design time, and users with no access after role changes. All of this contradicts the 'publishing is blocked until there are no errors' promise.
findings.recommendation: Extend validate(): check filter and condition values against options and stage ids for select, __stage and __status, every user's roleId against roles, notify role or user existence, and set_field values coerced with the target field's type rules (reuse cleanValues). Remove the 14-field cap (use a searchable multi-select). Treat 0 as filled for number fields in gates. Add these as unit tests alongside the template tests.
findings.auditor: Confirmed: filter values are never validated. Notify roles go unchecked, and 'finance' works only because of the special case in Shell.tsx:32. set_field values are not type-checked (an error surfaces only at runtime, engine.ts:660/666). The gate picker is capped at 14 fields (PipelinesTab.tsx:146). checkGate treats 0 as empty: a probe deal with qty 0 was refused for a qty gate. Overstated: orphan user roles cannot arise through the Access tab, because RolesTab disables deleting a role that has members (RolesTab.tsx:49). They arise only through the schema replacement in BUIL-01.

findings.title: No form layout, document or e-mail template designer: sections are dead code and the print layout is fixed
findings.evidence: FieldDef.section exists (schema.ts:49) but nothing reads it, and the form is one flat 2-column grid (ModulesTab.tsx:137-147; RecordPage.tsx:113). There are no tabs, sections, per-role layouts or related-list configuration. PrintView is hard-coded (RecordPage.tsx:330-342), with no way to add a logo position, bank details, terms, Arabic/English bilingual layout or custom fields to the printed quote or invoice, and no e-mail templates exist. CompanyProfile.fiscalYearStart is configurable (SettingsTab.tsx:30) but used nowhere.
findings.impact: Odoo Studio's report editor, Zoho's template designer and HubSpot's quote templates are core reasons buyers pick those tools.
