Egyptian B2B buyers expect bilingual quotations with terms and bank details. Long flat forms (the templates have 10-15 fields) hurt data entry speed, and a setting that does nothing undermines trust.
findings.recommendation: Add drag-and-drop sections and tabs on the Modules canvas (drop a 'Section' divider; collapse it in the app) and per-role 'hide on form'. Add a Documents tab with a block-based template designer (header, party block, lines table, totals, terms, bank, QR placeholder for ETA) bound to field tokens, in AR, EN or bilingual. Add e-mail and WhatsApp message templates that automations can reuse. Either wire fiscalYearStart into reports and period filters or remove it.
findings.auditor: FieldDef.section (schema.ts:49) is read nowhere. RecordPage renders one flat form-grid (RecordPage.tsx:112-122). PrintView is hard-coded (RecordPage.tsx:330-380): no logo, bank details, terms or custom fields, and no Arabic layout. There are no e-mail templates. fiscalYearStart is written only in SettingsTab.tsx:30 and used nowhere.

findings.title: The health check is structural only and the score is arbitrary; there is no runtime diagnosis of the live system
findings.evidence: healthScore = 100 − 15×errors − 4×warnings (validate.ts:315-319) and looks only at the schema. Runtime signals the engine already produces are never surfaced as health: automation failures go into notes (engine.ts:666), along with rotting records (engine.ts:152-160), reorder alerts, never-used modules and fields, approvals pending for N days, and records failing current rules. The Builder health panel lists issues with 'Must fix / Suggestion' and no suggested fix action (Builder.tsx:125-134).
findings.impact: Criterion 11 asks for AI that diagnoses the user's system and suggests fixes. Today the owner learns about broken automations or bad data only by accident. Competitors are moving to 'Copilot'-style admin assistants (Salesforce Optimizer, HubSpot AI, Zoho Zia).
findings.recommendation: Build a 'System doctor' panel. Rules-based first: automation failure rate per rule, fields that are 80% or more empty, modules unused for 30 days, stale pipeline stages, rules failing on existing records, and pending approvals older than 3 days. Each finding gets a one-click fix (for example 'Make field optional', 'Disable automation', 'Add a default'). Then add an LLM layer that reads the schema, issue list and usage stats and proposes concrete patches, which the admin previews as a diff (reusing BUIL-12) before applying. Use a severity-weighted score instead of fixed −15/−4.
findings.auditor: healthScore = 100 − 15×errors − 4×warnings (validate.ts:315-319) and is purely structural. Automation failures go to notes (engine.ts:666), rotting is computed per record (engine.ts:152-160), and none of it reaches the Builder health panel, which has no fix actions (Builder.tsx:125-134). This is a fair gap against criterion 11.

findings.title: Lead conversion and quote→invoice are hard-wired, with no configurable mapping or document flow chain
findings.evidence: convertLead always uses company||name for the account and copies phone, email and owner only (engine.ts:337-341). It cannot attach to an existing customer: it always creates a new account, which causes duplicates when a known customer sends a new enquiry. quoteToInvoice copies customer and lines only, with no link back from the deal (engine.ts:557-565). Quotes have no relation to deals in the role definitions (roles.ts:60-69), so 'deal → quote → invoice' is not traceable and quote acceptance does not move the deal to Won. There are no partial invoicing, sales order or delivery-note steps (no sales orders role at all).
findings.impact: Duplicate customers on every repeat enquiry. The pipeline is not reconciled with revenue (a won deal has no invoice, an invoice has no deal). There is no order-to-cash chain like Odoo's quotation → SO → delivery → invoice, which distribution and manufacturing SMEs need for stock reservation and partial delivery.
findings.recommendation: In the conversion dialog, offer 'match existing customer' (fuzzy on phone, tax ID or name) and use the mapping from BUIL-08. Add a system relation deal on quotes and invoices. When a quote is accepted, offer 'mark deal Won'. Show a document chain strip on the record page (Lead → Deal → Quote QT-… → Invoice INV-… → Payments). Plan a Sales order role with delivery (stock out) separate from the invoice for the distribution and manufacturing templates.
findings.auditor: Confirmed: convertLead always creates a new account (engine.ts:337-338), so repeat customers are duplicated, and quotes have no deal relation (roles.ts:60-69). There are no sales order or delivery steps. Inaccurate in part: quoteToInvoice does store a quote→invoice link (quote.links = { source: inv.id }, engine.ts:563). However, nothing reads or displays it, and there is no reverse link.

findings.title: Builder guardrails, publish validation and admin-only customisation are enforced only in the browser; any member can write any schema
findings.evidence: supabase/migrations/20261024000000_workspaces.sql:67-70 lets any member update the whole workspaces row: using/with check private.is_member(id), with no column or role restriction. The doc contains draft, published, roles and users. Admin status in the app is just user.roleId === 'role_admin' read from that same doc (App.tsx:26; Shell.tsx:56-57, 90). validate() and the 'no errors before publish' gate exist only in Builder.tsx publish(). A sales member with devtools can PATCH doc.published with any schema (stage gates removed, a role with admin:true, their own roleId changed to role_admin) or flip finance:true, and the server accepts it.
findings.impact: Every guardrail the product sells ('publishing is blocked until there are no errors', separation of duties through 'Post & collect', admin-only builder) can be bypassed by any team member. It also makes BUIL-06-style scoping meaningless.
findings.recommendation: Move schema and membership out of the member-writable doc. Store schema versions in a schema_versions table writable only by workspace admins (RLS uses private.is_ws_admin), derive roleId from workspace_members on the server, and run validate() in a Supabase Edge Function or Postgres function on publish. Reject publishes with errors server-side. Operational data writes should not be able to touch the schema or roles.

findings.title: Key lifecycle events never fire automations: payment, void, lead conversion and quote status changes
findings.evidence: registerPayment (engine.ts:532-555), voidDocument (engine.ts:508-530) and quoteToInvoice (engine.ts:557-565) never call runWorkflows, and setQuoteStatus (RecordPage.tsx:170-175) only sets r.status. convertLead sets lead.stage directly (engine.ts:342-345), skipping moveStage, so there is no 'stage_changed' event, no stage gate and no approval check for the Converted stage. Probe: an Invoices automation 'updated, when Document status = paid → notify' passed validation, the invoice reached status 'paid', and the automation never fired.
findings.impact: The most valuable SME automations, such as 'invoice paid → thank-you task or unlock delivery', 'lead converted → welcome call' and 'quote declined → ask for the reason', can be configured, pass the health check, and silently never run. The user sees no error and loses trust in the automation builder.
findings.recommendation: Emit explicit lifecycle events from the engine (document_posted, payment_registered, document_voided, quote_sent/accepted/declined, lead_converted) and expose them as triggers in AutomationsTab TRIGGERS. Route convertLead through moveStage so gates and approvals apply. Until then, have validate() warn when a condition on __status or a stage is combined with a trigger that can never observe it.

findings.title: Rollups count unposted draft documents and cannot be filtered, so the default 'Balance due' on customers disagrees with AR
findings.evidence: fieldValue for rollups excludes only status 'void' (engine.ts:139). Draft invoices carry balance = total, set by applyTotals (engine.ts:378). The rollup definition has no filter (schema.ts:57, `rollup?: { module, via, op, field }`), and the pack auto-adds 'Total invoiced' and 'Balance due' to Customers (packs.ts:139-140). Probe: one unposted draft invoice of EGP 114 made the customer show Balance due 114, while ageing (engine.ts:873, posted/partial only) and ledger account 1200 show 0. Rollups also feed approval conditions, because approvalNeeded passes ws (engine.ts:719).
findings.impact: Sales and finance see an inflated amount owed on every customer card, and it does not reconcile with the receivables report or the trial balance. Any credit-limit approval built on it blocks good customers. This breaks the basic accounting expectation that the subledger equals the GL.
findings.recommendation: Add filters to rollup definitions (reuse Filter[]: for example __status in posted/partial/paid) and edit them in the ModulesTab rollup panel. Make the default document rollups posted-only. Show the filter on the field card, for example 'Sum of Balance due · posted invoices'. Add a unit test that customer balance_due equals the ageing total.

findings.title: Record pages ignore module view permission, and 'Linked records' exposes modules a role cannot see
findings.evidence: RecordPage (RecordPage.tsx:16-23) renders any record by id without can(...,'view'), whereas ModuleView does check it (ModuleView.tsx:23). relatedRecords (RecordPage.tsx:177-185) walks every schema module with no permission check and links to each record. Shell search filters by visible modules (Shell.tsx:36), but this path does not. For example, a Service role with no access to Invoices or Deals opens a customer and sees, and can open, every invoice and deal linked to it, including totals and lines. The PrintView of those invoices is available too (RecordPage.tsx:88).
findings.impact: The Access matrix promises module-level hiding, but any user can browse hidden modules through links from records they are allowed to see. Owners who hide invoices or deals from service or operations staff are exposed without knowing it.
findings.recommendation: Check can(view) in RecordPage before rendering, with a 'Your role can't see this' state. Filter relatedRecords and lookup displays by can(view) on the source module. Add an engine-level assertCanView, used by every read helper, plus a test per role. Long term this has to be enforced server-side (see MISS-01).

findings.title: Quotations have no revision control: sent quotes stay editable, declined quotes can still be invoiced, and 'accepted' is never reached
findings.evidence: updateRecord exempts quotes from the posted lock (engine.ts:267, `mod.role !== 'quotes'`), and setLines allows status 'sent' (engine.ts:383), so a quotation already sent to the customer can be repriced in place with no revision number. RecordPage shows 'Accept & invoice' for any status except invoiced (RecordPage.tsx:72-76), including 'declined'. The status filter offers 'accepted' (ModuleView.tsx:93), but no code ever sets it. Quote numbering only happens through gapless posting for invoices and bills: quotes are never numbered beyond 'Draft' in recordTitle (engine.ts:64), and PrintView prints 'DRAFT' (RecordPage.tsx:351).
findings.impact: The customer's PDF and the system copy can differ with no trace. A declined offer can be invoiced by mistake, and there is no accepted-quote metric for win-rate reports. Odoo, Zoho and HubSpot all lock sent quotes and create revisions (QT-0012-R1).
findings.recommendation: Number quotes on 'Mark sent' (prefix QT, gapless). Lock sent quotes and offer 'Revise', which clones to a new revision and supersedes the old one. Add 'Accepted' as an explicit step that can trigger automations (see MISS-02). Hide 'Accept & invoice' for declined or expired quotes, and warn past valid_until.

panel: Product Strategy, Competitive Position, Automation & AI
strengths: The guardrail core is a real advantage. validate.ts:164-313 checks every reference, pipeline, formula, report, automation and approval. fieldDependents() (validate.ts:33-71) tells the user what would break before they delete something. Odoo Studio and Zoho Creator let admins break their own apps; Bonyan's 'flexible on the surface, strict underneath' promise is backed by code.

Issues are machine-readable: each Issue carries tab, moduleId, fieldId and itemId (validate.ts:10-17), and the Builder health drawer already deep-links to each one (Builder.tsx:121-129). This is most of the plumbing an AI 'system doctor' with one-click fixes needs.

Onboarding goes from answers to a working system in one deterministic step. generateSchema (recommend.ts:141-183) combines the template, extra modules, challenge-specific reports and automations (packs.ts:29-79), team roles and smart defaults (rollups, scoring, rotting, approvals; packs.ts:120-173). Time-to-first-value is minutes, against weeks for Odoo or Dynamics BC partner implementations.

The accounting engine is honest. Postings are double-entry and must balance (engine.ts:406-412), numbering is gapless and taken only after every check passes (engine.ts:443-446), voiding writes a full reversal (engine.ts:508-530), and stock uses moving-average cost. That is a credible base for a 'CRM that also keeps correct books' story against HubSpot, Pipedrive and Salesforce Starter, which have no books.

Egypt-native defaults that competitors bolt on: the 27 governorates (templates.ts:23), a tax ID field labelled for ETA (templates.ts:36), InstaPay as a payment method (engine.ts:532), 14% VAT, and industry-specific Egyptian templates (EDA registration, tenders, real-estate installments).
Automations cannot loop: a depth guard sits in runWorkflows (engine.ts:632-646). A failed action is caught and turned into a notification instead of breaking the save (engine.ts:666-668).
33 engine tests pass and `tsc -b` is clean. Each template is tested to generate with zero validation errors and balanced books (engine.test.ts:34).

scorecard.rationale: There is a real differentiator: guardrailed self-build, plus correct double-entry books and stock inside a CRM, with Egyptian templates. But the table stakes in the home market are missing: ETA e-invoicing, full Arabic, WhatsApp, local payment links, billing, a mobile app and migration import. The single-JSON architecture (store.ts) loses edits with concurrent users. Against Daftra on Egyptian invoicing and Odoo on depth, it loses today. Against HubSpot or Pipedrive on CRM polish, it lacks e-mail, inbox and mobile.

The guided 5-step onboarding into a generated, validated system, dependency explanations and plain-language errors are simpler than Odoo Studio or Salesforce setup. Simplicity is undercut by an English-only app for Arabic-first users, sample data that pollutes real books with no removal, no guided data migration, no tour or checklist, and automations that silently don't run unless someone opens the app.

Custom modules, 16+ field types, formulas, lookups, rollups, conditional fields, rules, approvals and role matrices are protected by strong guardrails (validate.ts). Flexibility stops at shallow automations (3 actions, no chaining or webhooks) and ERP depth the templates imply but the engine lacks (lots, BOM, installments, progress billing).

Automation is basic When/If/Then with 4 triggers and 3 actions, runs client-side, and has no run log. There is no AI anywhere: the onboarding 'analysis' is a timed animation. The schema health check is a good deterministic base (machine-readable issues with deep links) but doesn't look at live data, failing automations or fixes. Nothing predicts cash, stock-outs or lead quality.

vision:
Best in class for Bonyan is an Arabic-first 'business architect in your pocket'. An Egyptian owner describes the business in Arabic, by voice or text. Within 10 minutes Bonyan proposes a working CRM and ERP, explaining each module in plain Arabic, and every AI-proposed change has passed the same validate() guardrails that block broken setups today.

Day 1 is legally live:
- invoices go to ETA automatically and print bilingually with the ETA QR,
- every phone number is a WhatsApp conversation logged on the record,
- every invoice carries a Fawry, Paymob or InstaPay pay link.

Opening balances come in from an Excel or Daftra export with AI column mapping, so the books balance from the first entry. The sample company lives in a separate demo workspace, so real books are never polluted.

Every morning each user gets a WhatsApp digest: their tasks, approvals waiting and deals going cold. The owner gets a 13-week cash-flow forecast with a warning such as 'cash dips below zero in week 6 unless Delta Foods pays', and stock-out predictions with one-tap draft purchase bills.

A permanent 'System doctor' watches configuration and data. It flags failing automations, records broken by a new rule, orphaned tasks, duplicate customers and sequence gaps. It explains the root cause in Arabic and offers one-click fixes that are validated before they apply. An 'Ask Bonyan' bar turns questions like 'أكبر ١٠ عملاء متأخرين في الإسكندرية' (top 10 late-paying customers in Alexandria) into a pinned chart.

Underneath, records are stored per record in Postgres:
- engine postings and date automations run server-side,
- role security is enforced by the database,
- the AI gateway is metered, PDPL-compliant and opt-in.

Priced in EGP below Odoo and Zoho, with AI and WhatsApp in a Pro tier, this beats global suites on time-to-value and localisation, and beats local tools on flexibility and intelligence.

findings.title: Egyptian ETA e-invoicing / e-receipt is missing, so VAT-registered SMEs cannot use Bonyan invoices legally
findings.evidence: The only ETA support is a warning asking for a tax ID (validate.ts:170) and a 'Tax registration no.' text field (templates.ts:36). postDocument (engine.ts:423-506) writes a local number and journal and nothing else. There is no document UUID, no signature, no submission or status field, and no ETA item codes (GS1/EGS) on products. The printed 'Tax invoice' (RecordPage.tsx:335-378) is English-only and has no ETA UUID or QR code. The README lists ETA under 'Before a public launch'.
findings.impact: Egypt requires e-invoices for VAT-registered B2B sellers through the ETA portal, and e-receipts for B2C are being phased in. A Bonyan invoice is not the legal invoice, so the customer must re-key every invoice in the ETA portal or in another system. Daftra and Odoo (l10n_eg_edi_eta) already submit to ETA. Without this, Bonyan is a CRM with a 'pretend' invoice in its home market and loses every comparison on the invoicing module.
findings.recommendation:
Build an 'ETA connector' as a Supabase Edge Function:
- Settings > Tax: ETA client ID and secret stored in Supabase Vault, a branch/activity code, and taxpayer type.
- Products: a required 'ETA item code' field (EGS/GS1) on the products role, enforced by validate.ts when ETA is on.
- Invoices: on post, queue the document, map it to the ETA JSON, sign it (HSM/USB token or a signing-service bridge) and submit. Store eta_uuid, eta_status and eta_submission_id on the record, and poll status.
- Printing: add the ETA QR and UUID.
- Health check: a red badge for invoices the ETA rejected, with the reason. Add the e-receipt POS flow later.
A user posts an invoice, sees 'Submitted to ETA ✓ valid' within seconds, and prints a compliant bilingual invoice.
findings.auditor: Checked the code. validate.ts:170 is only a warning about the tax ID. templates.ts:36 adds a free-text tax_id on customers, and nothing makes it required. postDocument (engine.ts:423-506) only assigns a local number and writes the journal and stock moves. PrintView (RecordPage.tsx:330-378) is English-only and has no UUID or QR. It also prints the heading 'TAX INVOICE' on drafts, with 'DRAFT' where the number should be (line 335, 351). The README lists ETA under 'Before a public launch'. One correction to the recommendation: ETA signing needs the taxpayer's USB token or HSM, or an ETA-approved signing service. A Supabase Edge Function cannot hold that key by itself, so plan a local signer or signing-service bridge from day one. This stays critical for the invoicing module in Egypt.

findings.title: Arabic covers only the landing page; the product an Egyptian SME uses every day is English-only
findings.evidence: i18n.ts:32-59 has 26 keys, all for Landing. Rendering /welcome in Arabic with Playwright still showed 'See how it works', every template tagline (Landing.tsx:97 uses tp.tagline, which is English-only) and the whole 'best ideas' and guardrails sections in English. Onboarding steps and channels are hard-coded English (Onboarding.tsx:13-23). Builder, workspace, field labels from roles.ts and templates.ts, engine error messages, validator messages and the printed tax invoice are all English. Dates and numbers use the default toLocaleString with no ar-EG locale (Dashboard.tsx:68,78). recommend.ts:105 matches free-text industry only against English keywords, so typing 'أدوية' or 'عقارات' matches no template.
findings.impact: The positioning is 'Egypt first', and the stated pain is 'leads lost in WhatsApp', which describes owner-led, Arabic-first teams. Daftra, Qoyod and Wafeq are Arabic-native, and Odoo and Zoho ship full Arabic. A Cairo sales rep or accountant who meets English menus and English error messages ('Your role can't edit records here') sees a foreign tool. That cuts trial-to-paid conversion and undoes the simplicity promise (criterion 8).
findings.recommendation:
Make every user-facing string translatable:
1. Move i18n.ts to a key/ICU catalogue (e.g. a small t() with en/ar JSON).
2. Give schema labels (module, field, stage, option, report and automation names) a label plus labelAr pair, or a Record<Lang,string>, and fill Arabic in all 9 templates and in roles.ts system fields.
3. Have EngineError and validator Issues carry a code and params so they render in either language.
4. Format numbers, money and dates with Intl.NumberFormat('ar-EG') and offer an Eastern-Arabic numerals option.
5. Print a bilingual 'فاتورة ضريبية / Tax invoice'.
6. Add Arabic keywords to Template.industries.
The user picks العربية at registration and never sees English again.
findings.auditor: Mostly accurate. Small corrections: i18n.ts has 23 keys, not 26. Template names (nameAr) and challenge labels (labelAr, packs.ts:14-23, shown at Onboarding.tsx:208) are already bilingual. The Arabic free-text industry match only applies when 'other' is chosen. Further evidence the panel missed: generateSchema hard-codes company.language: 'en' (recommend.ts:169), and money() forces 'en-US' (engine.ts:168). Arabic field labels also produce internal keys 'field', 'field_2' and so on (schema.ts:217-223 with ModulesTab.tsx:188). I re-rate it high, not critical: it is a serious gap against Daftra, Odoo and Zoho, but it causes no data loss and no wrong books.

findings.title: Sample data (on by default) posts real invoices into the live number sequence and books, and the promised removal doesn't exist
findings.evidence: Suggest.tsx:17 defaults the sample checkbox to on. Suggest.tsx:97 promises 'Remove it any time from Settings'. On first publish, Builder.tsx:64-68 calls seedSampleData, which runs the real postDocument and registerPayment (seed.ts:6,152-175). That takes INV/BILL numbers through nextNumber (engine.ts:399-404) and writes journals, stock moves and demo users with @demo.local e-mails (seed.ts:35). Neither SettingsTab.tsx nor any other file contains a clear-sample function (grep for removeSample/clearSample finds nothing). Posted documents can only be voided, which leaves them in the sequence.
findings.impact: A company that tries Bonyan the way the UI suggests and then goes live finds fake invoices INV-2026-0001…00NN, fake receivables and ageing, fake stock cost and fake revenue in its trial balance. The first real invoice is not 0001. Under gapless-numbering rules, and with ETA later, that is a compliance and auditor problem. The only way out is to delete the workspace and start over. This breaks the 'accounting that always balances' trust promise on day one.
findings.recommendation:
Separate the sandbox from production:
- Option A: tag every seeded record, movement, journal and payment with sample:true and use a separate sequence prefix (e.g. DEMO-INV). Add 'Remove sample data' in Company settings that deletes everything tagged and resets sequences. Block it once any real document is posted.
- Option B, better: an 'Explore demo company' workspace kept separate from the customer's real workspace, with a 'Start my real system' button that copies only the schema.
Default sample to on only for the demo workspace.
findings.auditor: Verified: the sample checkbox defaults to on (Suggest.tsx:17), and the promise to remove it 'any time from Settings' (line 97) is false. No code removes sample data. Builder.tsx:64-68 seeds on first publish through the real postDocument and registerPayment (seed.ts:152-175), which uses the live sequences (engine.ts:399-404) and writes journals and stock. It is worse than stated: the migration has no DELETE policy on workspaces, so the user cannot even delete the workspace and start over. Seeding also calls createRecord without silent, so the demo leads and quotes fire automations and create real tasks. The demo users (@demo.local) then fill the owner and assignee pickers.

findings.title: One JSON document per company means concurrent users silently lose edits, and it won't scale
findings.evidence: Every change re-uploads the whole workspace (records, journal, stock, history) after a 600 ms debounce (store.ts:41-46, 56-61). When another user saved first, the update matches 0 rows and the client calls reload(), which replaces local state and sets dirty=false (store.ts:68-72, 141-149). The user's unsaved changes are thrown away and the only signal is the sync status 'reloaded'. Date-based automations run in each browser on open (Shell.tsx:23-28), so they compete for the same row. Every member downloads every record of every module, plus all notes and the journal (store.ts:204-206).
findings.impact: With 5 to 10 active users (typical teams: Sales 5, Finance 2, Management 2 per recommend.ts:49-53), two people editing at once is routine. Reps see their notes and deal updates vanish, the system becomes untrustworthy, and churn follows. Load and save time grows linearly with history: a distributor with 20k invoice lines would push multi-MB documents on every keystroke-save. Salesforce, HubSpot, Odoo and Zoho are all record-level transactional. This is the biggest technical gap to 'compete head-to-head'.
findings.recommendation:
Normalise into Postgres tables now, before the first paying customer:
- workspace_schema(versioned), records(id, workspace_id, module, values jsonb, stage, status, version), lines, stock_moves, journal_entries, journal_lines, payments, approvals, notes, activity.
- Move postDocument, registerPayment, voidDocument and runScheduled into Supabase Edge Functions or SQL RPCs, reusing the pure-TS engine, with a per-record optimistic version. Run date automations from pg_cron, not from someone's browser.
- Add Supabase Realtime so a board updates live.
- On a conflict, merge at field level or show 'Ahmed changed Amount; keep yours / keep theirs' instead of discarding.
This also unlocks server-side RLS by role (the security panel's concern) and the AI features below, which need queryable data.
findings.auditor: Verified in store.ts:49-78 and 141-149. flush() sets dirty=false before the request. On a version conflict, reload() replaces the document, so the user's change in that save, and any edits made while it was in flight, are dropped. Corrections: a save is not per keystroke but 600 ms after each committed action. The loss is not completely silent either: an amber 'Reloaded latest' pill with a tooltip appears (Shell.tsx:87-88), but it doesn't say what was lost. The 'automations compete for the row' sub-claim is weak. The losing browser's runScheduled output is discarded, so it causes conflicts but no duplicates. The core data-loss and scaling claims hold.

findings.title: No AI layer at all; the 'Designing your system…' screen is a timed animation
findings.evidence: There is no LLM, ML or anomaly code anywhere. A grep for claude/openai/ai finds nothing, and package.json has no AI SDK. The onboarding 'analysis' is a fixed 2.6 s setTimeout showing canned lines (Onboarding.tsx:33-37, 46-52). suggest() is keyword plus feature arithmetic (recommend.ts:96-119). Lead scoring is static points per condition (packs.ts:152-161, engine.ts:146-149). docs/BONYAN_PROJECT.md §4 lists 'AI features (AI fields and summaries need the backend)' as future work.
findings.impact: In 2026 every competitor sells an AI story: HubSpot Breeze, Salesforce Einstein/Agentforce, Zoho Zia, Odoo AI fields and OCR, Dynamics Copilot, Pipedrive AI sales assistant. A builder product that must explain itself to non-technical owners gains the most from AI: 'tell me what you want, I build it'. Criterion 11 is essentially unmet.
findings.recommendation:
Ship the AI layer as a Supabase Edge Function 'ai-gateway' that calls the Claude API with:
- per-workspace metering and a monthly token budget per plan,
- PII minimisation (send aggregates and the schema, not raw customer lists, unless the feature needs them),
- prompt caching of the workspace schema,
- tool use whose outputs are JSON patches validated by validate.ts before anything is applied,
- an audit row per AI action (who, prompt, patch, applied?).
Phase 1 (S/M each): system doctor explanations (STRA-06), natural-language report builder (STRA-07), WhatsApp/e-mail drafting (STRA-09).
Phase 2: onboarding from free text ('we import medical devices and sell to hospitals by tender'), which produces Answers and template tweaks as a diff the user accepts.
Phase 3: forecasts and anomalies (STRA-08).
All output must be bilingual Arabic and English.
findings.auditor: There is no AI dependency in package.json and no LLM code in src. The 'Designing your system…' screen is a fixed 2.6 s timer (Onboarding.tsx:33-37). For fairness: those lines use the real answer counts (lines 46-52), and suggest() really runs on the next page. So it is presentation over a deterministic engine, not fabricated results. Criterion 11 is unmet. The phasing is sensible, and the natural-language report builder (STRA-07) needs only the schema, so it does not depend on STRA-04.

findings.title: The health check only looks at the schema; it is not a 'system doctor' for live data, broken automations or rule changes
findings.evidence:
validate(schema) takes no workspace data (validate.ts:164, useDraft.ts:10). So it can't see:
- records that violate a newly added validation rule or a field newly marked required,
- tasks assigned to users removed on Team (Team.tsx:41-49 removes only the user),
- automations that keep failing, which become notification text 'Automation … could not finish' (engine.ts:666-668) and are never counted in health,
- negative stock or products with zero cost,
- invoices stuck in draft,
- duplicate customers,
- deals rotting in bulk (engine.ts:152-160).
healthScore is a linear 100 − 15×errors − 4×warnings (validate.ts:315-319). Issues deep-link (Builder.tsx:121-129) but cannot be fixed in one click.
findings.impact: Owners don't know why 'the system is wrong': sales numbers are off, a reminder never fired, a rep sees nothing. Today they need a consultant, which is exactly the Odoo/SAP pain Bonyan wants to remove (criterion 8). A data-aware doctor with one-click fixes would be a unique feature: no competitor's admin console explains config errors in plain Arabic and fixes them.
findings.recommendation:
Build the doctor in three layers.
1. Deterministic, client or server (M). Add diagnose(ws, schema) beside validate() with data checks:
   - records failing current rules (count + 'show me' link),
   - orphan assignees, automations with N failures in 7 days (keep a workflowErrors log instead of free-text notes),
   - stock ≤ 0 with open quotes, products with cost 0, drafts older than 7 days,
   - duplicate accounts by phone/tax_id, sequence gaps, a trial balance that doesn't equal 0.
   Give each Issue an optional fix: {label, patch: JSON-Patch on schema, or engine action} and an 'Apply fix' button that runs inside transact() and then re-validates.
2. Publish-impact preview (M): before publish, diff the draft against live data ('making Phone required affects 37 existing leads: fill / skip / keep optional').
3. AI (M): the Edge Function sends issues, schema and aggregates to Claude and gets back a plain-Arabic explanation, a root cause across issues, and ranked fix patches. Patches only apply if validate() passes. Schedule a weekly 'system check-up' digest by e-mail or WhatsApp to the admin.
findings.auditor: validate(schema) has no data input (validate.ts:164). Automation failures become broadcast notes (engine.ts:666-668) and are never counted in health. Team.remove only drops the user from ws.users (Team.tsx:42-50), so records and tasks owned by removed users become orphans. healthScore is the linear formula quoted (validate.ts:315-319). The issues cannot be fixed in one click. Accurate as stated.

findings.title: Reports have no date ranges or comparisons, and building one needs drag-and-drop; a natural-language report builder fits this design well
findings.evidence: FilterOp is eq|neq|gt|lt|contains|empty|notempty (schema.ts:137), with no 'between', 'this month', 'last 90 days' or 'vs previous period'. runReport (reports.ts:32-78) has no time window or comparison and caps rows at 24. The dashboard has no global date filter, targets or drill-down. The weighted forecast is a single grey sentence (Dashboard.tsx:73-79). ReportDef is a small, typed JSON (schema.ts:145-156) that validate.ts already checks.
findings.impact: An owner asks 'how did this month compare to last?' or 'who are my top 10 customers by overdue balance in Alexandria?' and cannot answer without building a report. HubSpot, Zoho Zia and Salesforce Einstein answer such questions in natural language. Criteria 6 and 10 (smart dashboards that beat peers) are not met.
findings.recommendation:
1. Engine (M): add relative date filters (today, this_week, this_month, last_n_days, this_fiscal_year using company.fiscalYearStart), a 'compare to previous period' flag returning delta %, a dashboard-level period picker, and target or goal lines on KPI cards.
2. AI 'Ask Bonyan' bar on the Dashboard (M): the Edge Function sends the user's question plus the schema (modules, fields, types, stages; cached) to Claude with a tool `create_report(ReportDef)`. The returned ReportDef runs through validate() and then runReport locally, and the user sees the chart instantly with 'Pin to dashboard'. Answer in the language asked. No record data leaves the browser for this feature, which helps PDPL.
findings.auditor: FilterOp has no date or relative operators (schema.ts:137). runReport has no time window or comparison and caps output at 24 rows (reports.ts:77). The dashboard has no period picker, targets or filtered drill-down; the card link just opens the module (Dashboard.tsx:41). The weighted forecast is one line of text (Dashboard.tsx:73-79). The panel also missed that the default 'Sales by month' and 'Invoiced revenue' KPIs are themselves wrong (see RPT-01 below).

findings.title: No predictive features: cash-flow forecast, stock-out prediction, smart lead scoring, anomaly alerts
findings.impact: SME owners' top worries are 'will I have cash next month?' and 'will I run out of stock?'. Zoho Books and Odoo offer cash-flow forecasts, NetSuite and BC offer demand planning, and HubSpot and Salesforce offer predictive lead scoring. Bonyan has the clean double-entry data to do this better than CRMs, but doesn't.
findings.recommendation:
Server-side jobs (pg_cron + Edge Function) once data is normalised (STRA-04):
(a) Cash-flow forecast (M): expected receipts = open AR by due date × each customer's historical days-late; expected payments = AP by due date, plus recurring fixed costs the user enters. Show a 13-week chart with low/high bands and 'below zero in week 6' alerts.
(b) Stock-out prediction (M): daily usage = EWMA of outgoing quantities over 90 days; days of cover = on-hand ÷ usage; reorder suggestion = lead time × usage + safety stock. Add a 'Create purchase bill draft' button.
(c) Predictive lead score (L): logistic regression on won/lost leads and deals (source, governorate, budget, response time, activity count), retrained weekly per workspace once there are ≥ 50 closed records, otherwise fall back to the rule points. Show 'why' factors.
(d) Anomaly alerts (M): z-score on daily sales, discount %, margin per invoice and voids per user. Claude writes a one-line Arabic explanation.
findings.auditor: The facts are right. Reorder alerts use a fixed threshold (engine.ts:694-707), and lead scoring is static points (packs.ts:152-161, engine.ts:146-149). But predictive forecasting is not a gap against the SME tiers Bonyan sells against (Pipedrive, Zoho and HubSpot starter plans, Daftra). It is not a correctness issue, and it depends on STRA-04. A per-workspace logistic regression needing ≥ 50 closed records will rarely trigger for SMEs; use pooled or industry priors instead. The cash-flow forecast and days-of-cover parts are the cheap, high-value pieces. I re-rate it medium.

findings.title: WhatsApp, the #1 stated pain, has no integration, not even click-to-chat
findings.evidence: The first challenge is 'Leads get lost in WhatsApp and calls' (packs.ts:14), and the default onboarding channels include whatsapp (recommend.ts:44). The 'fix' is a task 'Call {name}' (packs.ts:70). Phone fields are labelled 'Mobile / WhatsApp' (roles.ts:188,194), but there is no wa.me link, tel: link, WhatsApp Business Cloud API, inbox, template message or webhook (grep for wa.me|tel:|mailto: finds nothing in src). Automations can only create_task, set_field or notify in-app (schema.ts:160-163).
findings.impact: In Egypt and MENA, WhatsApp is the CRM's front door. Competitors already ship it: Zoho, HubSpot and Odoo integrate WhatsApp, and local tools sell 'WhatsApp CRM' as the headline. Without it, Bonyan doesn't fix the pain it names first, and it loses the 10-second demo moment ('a lead messages you → it appears in Bonyan → a rep replies from the record').
findings.recommendation:
Build it in three steps.
1. S, this week: render every phone field as a wa.me/<E.164> click-to-chat link and a tel: link, with Egyptian number normalisation (01x → +201x) and a prefilled message from a template ('Hello {name}, about quotation {number}…').
2. L: WhatsApp Business Cloud API through an Edge Function. An inbound webhook creates or updates a Lead (dedupe by phone) and logs messages on the record timeline. Add a new automation action `send_whatsapp(template, to field)` for approved templates (invoice reminder with a payment link, quotation follow-up, appointment). Add delivery and read status.
3. AI: 'Draft reply' and 'summarise this chat' buttons on the record using Claude, bilingual, with the rep approving before sending.
findings.auditor: There is no wa.me, tel: or mailto: anywhere in src. Leads require a 'Mobile / WhatsApp' phone (roles.ts:194), but the phone is plain text, and the PHONE regex (engine.ts:172) does no E.164 normalisation. Building wa.me links therefore also needs 01x → +201x normalisation, which the recommendation already covers. The only automation actions are create_task, set_field and notify (schema.ts:160-163). Accurate.

findings.title: Automation engine is too shallow to compete and depends on someone opening the app
findings.evidence: There are 4 triggers (schema.ts:158) and 3 actions (schema.ts:160-163). There are no delays/waits, branches, e-mail, webhook, 'update related record', 'assign round-robin' or 'create record in another module'. Date triggers only run when a user opens the app: runScheduled is called from Shell.tsx:23-28, and the AutomationsTab copy admits 'date checks run every time the app opens' (AutomationsTab.tsx:37). Run history is just an activity line 'ran …' (engine.ts:670), and failures become free-text notes (engine.ts:667). The depth guard means one automation can never chain to another (engine.ts:634), so 'won deal → create project → notify ops' is impossible. buildWorkflows ignores its challenges argument (packs.ts:61 `_challenges`).
findings.impact: HubSpot workflows, Zoho Flow and Odoo automated actions (with webhooks and delays) set the bar. Overdue-invoice collection, the core cash feature, silently doesn't run over a weekend or holiday when nobody logs in. Owners can't trust automations they can't see running.
findings.recommendation:
1. Run date and scheduled triggers server-side with pg_cron every 15 minutes (needs STRA-04).
2. Add actions: send_email (Resend/SES), send_whatsapp, webhook (HMAC-signed), create_record (with field mapping from the trigger record, e.g. won deal → project), update_related, assign (round-robin among a role), and wait N days.
3. Allow controlled chaining with a max depth of 3 and cycle detection in validate.ts, replacing the blanket block.
4. Add a 'Runs' tab per automation (time, record, outcome, error, retry button) and count failures in the doctor (STRA-06).
5. Make buildWorkflows use the challenges, e.g. 'late_collections' adds a 3-step dunning sequence at −3/+1/+7 days with a WhatsApp payment link.
findings.auditor: Verified: 4 triggers and 3 actions. The depth guard blocks any chaining (engine.ts:634), and the copy admits that date checks run on app open (AutomationsTab.tsx:37). buildWorkflows ignores _challenges (packs.ts:61). The panel also missed that runScheduled marks a run as done before it executes and swallows failures, so a failed run never retries (see AUTO-01 below).

findings.title: No billing, plans or trial limits: nothing to sell, and unlimited free workspaces
findings.evidence: The 'signed-in users create their own workspace' policy lets any authenticated user insert unlimited workspaces (migration lines 64-66). The workspaces table has no plan, seat limit, trial_ends_at or status column (migration lines 6-14). A grep for billing|subscription|pricing|stripe|paymob finds nothing. The landing page has only 'Build my system — free' CTAs (Landing.tsx:40,55,134) and no pricing section.
findings.impact: No revenue path. The team also can't segment features (e.g. ETA, AI or WhatsApp on paid tiers), can't run trials, and can't stop abuse. Egyptian SMEs expect EGP pricing paid by local card, Fawry or InstaPay with annual discounts. Daftra and Odoo publish clear per-user or per-plan EGP prices.
findings.recommendation:
Add subscriptions(workspace_id, plan, seats, status, trial_ends_at, provider, provider_ref) plus an Edge Function webhook from Paymob or Fawry for Egypt (cards, wallets, Fawry reference) and Stripe for global. Enforce seats in addMember (store.ts:275) through an RLS check, and gate modules or features by plan in the Builder with an 'Upgrade' prompt. Offer a 14-day full trial with in-app countdown and read-only after expiry, never deleting data.
Pricing positioning (approximate, to check against current competitor prices):
- Free: 2 users, CRM only.
- Growth: ~EGP 350–500/user/month, CRM + invoicing + stock + ETA, under Odoo Standard and Zoho One.
- Pro: + AI doctor, WhatsApp API, approvals.
- AI usage metered on top.
findings.auditor: Accurate. Any authenticated user can insert unlimited workspaces (migration:63-66). There are no plan, seat or trial columns (migration:6-14) and no billing code. Abuse is limited because e-mail confirmation is required, but no document size cap exists either. This is a go-to-market prerequisite before paid launch, not a product defect, so I re-rate it medium. Seat enforcement belongs in the 'admins add members' RLS policy, not only in addMember.

findings.title: Templates promise industry depth the engine doesn't deliver (batches/expiry, raw→finished stock, installments, progress billing)
findings.evidence:
The template copy promises things the engine doesn't do:
- Medical (templates.ts:59): tagline says 'batches and expiry', but the only expiry is an 'EDA expiry' date on a record (templates.ts:87). Stock moves have no lot or expiry (engine.ts:461, 483) and there is no FEFO.
- Manufacturing (templates.ts:286,293): highlights 'Raw vs finished stock' and production orders, but m_production (templates.ts:298-305) is a plain custom module. It neither consumes raw materials nor produces finished goods, and has no BOM.
- Real estate (templates.ts:150-158): 'Installments' is a custom module with a Paid checkbox, not linked to invoices, receivables or journals.
- Construction (templates.ts:353,358): 'Progress invoices' has no progress-billing or retention logic.
findings.impact: A pharma distributor or factory evaluates the template, discovers in week 1 that the key feature is a label, and churns with a bad review. Odoo, ERPNext and BC do lots, expiry, BOMs and installment receivables natively. Over-promising damages the 'stays correct by global standards' brand.
findings.recommendation:
Either reword the taglines today (S) to what exists, or build the depth (L each):
1. Lot/expiry on stock moves, with a 'track lots' product flag, FEFO picking on invoice post, and expiry alerts in the doctor.
2. A BOM on products plus a production order 'Complete' action that posts raw-material consumption and finished-goods receipt at rolled-up cost (a new engine function with balanced journals 1300↔1300/WIP).
3. An installment plan generator from a Reservation (down payment % + years) that creates scheduled receivable documents, with dunning automations.
4. Progress billing (% complete × contract value, retention %) for construction.
findings.auditor: Verified. Medical 'EDA expiry' is a product registration date (templates.ts:87), not batch or lot expiry, and stock moves carry no lot. m_production is a plain custom module with a Status select (templates.ts:298-305) and posts no stock. Installments has a 'Paid' checkbox and no link to AR (templates.ts:150-158). Construction has no progress-billing logic. The S-effort rewording should be done immediately.

findings.title: No local payment collection: InstaPay is a label; no Fawry, Paymob or Valu payment links
findings.evidence: registerPayment takes a method string (engine.ts:532), and InstaPay is just a button label in PaymentModal (RecordPage.tsx:322). There is no payment link, no gateway, no online invoice page and no reconciliation from a gateway webhook. The 'late_collections' fix is a task plus an in-app note (packs.ts:16, 72).
findings.impact: Collections are the SME owner's main cash lever. Daftra, Zoho Books and Odoo send invoices with 'Pay now'. In Egypt, Fawry reference codes, Paymob card and wallet payments, and InstaPay IPA or QR are expected. Without them Bonyan can tell an owner who owes money but can't help collect it.
findings.recommendation: Edge Function integrations with Paymob (cards, wallets, Valu) and Fawry (reference code), plus an InstaPay IPA/QR printed on the invoice. Add a public, signed, expiring invoice link (/pay/:token) showing a bilingual invoice and a Pay button. The gateway webhook calls registerPayment server-side with method 'card' or 'fawry'. Add an automation action 'send payment link by WhatsApp/e-mail' and use it in the default dunning sequence.
findings.auditor: Verified: the method is only a label. Also, every method (cash, bank, cheque, InstaPay, card) posts to the same account, 1100 (engine.ts:550-556). Bank and wallet receipts therefore can't be reconciled separately, even before gateways are added. A gateway webhook should post to its own clearing account.

findings.title: No trust or compliance layer for Egypt PDPL (Law 151/2020), and no public legal pages
findings.evidence: No privacy policy, terms or DPA link on the landing footer (Landing.tsx:137). No consent fields on leads or contacts (roles.ts lead fields: source, phone, etc.). No data-subject export or erasure. No audit log of who viewed what. The data location is whatever region the Supabase project 'my-crm0' uses (README Cloud backend), with no residency statement. Every member's browser downloads the whole company dataset (store.ts:204-206).
findings.impact: Egypt's PDPL and its executive regulations require controllers and processors to obtain licences or permits from the Personal Data Protection Center, appoint a DPO, restrict cross-border transfers and honour data-subject rights. B2B buyers, especially medical and government-facing ones (two of the nine templates), will ask for a DPA, the hosting region and a security posture. Competitors show trust centres (Zoho, HubSpot, Odoo). Without one, procurement stalls and there is regulatory risk.
findings.recommendation:
1. S: publish Privacy, Terms and a DPA and link them in the footer and at registration with consent checkboxes.
2. M: add consent fields (marketing_consent with date and source) to the lead and contact roles as system fields, with the automation engine refusing WhatsApp or e-mail marketing actions without consent.
3. M: per-record 'Export person data' and 'Erase/anonymise' admin actions that keep accounting records (legal retention) but pseudonymise PII.
4. Pick a Supabase region close to Egypt (e.g. eu-central or me-central where available), document it on a /trust page with the sub-processor list (Supabase, Vercel, Anthropic), and start the PDPC licensing process.
5. The AI gateway must be opt-in per workspace, with a no-training statement.
findings.auditor: The landing footer has only a copyright line (Landing.tsx:137). There are no consent fields on the lead or contact system fields (roles.ts:183-199), no export or erase actions, and no read audit. Every member downloads the full document (store.ts:204-206). The findings are accurate. Exact PDPC licensing obligations should be confirmed with Egyptian counsel; that is not a code fact.

findings.title: Switching from Excel, Daftra or Odoo is hard: CSV only, no Excel, no opening balances, no guided migration
findings.evidence: ImportModal accepts only `.csv,text/csv` (ImportModal.tsx:89). importRows (engine.ts:785-808) creates records only. There is no import of opening stock with cost, open invoices or receivables, chart-of-account balances, or historical deals with stages. The onboarding 'products' answer is a free-text list (recommend.ts:27, Builder.tsx:66).
findings.impact: Most target SMEs live in Excel (the 'manual_invoices' challenge, packs.ts:19) or a local tool. If the first hour means 'convert to CSV, then re-enter balances', time-to-value collapses and the Odoo comparison (with its migration partners) favours the incumbent. Opening balances are also mandatory for correct books from day 1 (criterion 2).
findings.recommendation:
Build a 'Bring your data' step after Suggest:
1. .xlsx parsing in the browser (SheetJS), Arabic headers, Windows-1256 detection for old CSVs.
2. Import presets for Daftra, Odoo, Zoho and QuickBooks exports, with mappings pre-filled.
3. An opening-balances wizard: stock quantity and unit cost per product as an opening stock move and journal against 3000 Opening Equity; open AR and AP invoices as 'opening' documents with their own sequence prefix; cash and bank balances. All go through the engine so books balance.
4. AI column mapping: Claude maps messy headers ('اسم العميل', 'Tel', 'Mob.') to schema fields with confidence scores, and the user confirms.
findings.auditor: Verified: CSV only (ImportModal.tsx:89), and importRows creates plain records only (engine.ts:785-808). It is worse than stated: createRecord forces stock=0 and cost=0 for products (engine.ts:251-254), so opening stock can only be entered as a fake purchase bill. There is no opening-balance journal at all. The import also silently turns Arabic-Indic digits into 0 (see I18N-01 below).

findings.title: Activation and retention basics are missing: invite e-mails, password reset, in-app guidance, notification delivery
findings.evidence: Team.add only inserts a member row and shows a toast telling the admin to send the /join link themselves (Team.tsx:26-28). There is no invitation e-mail. Auth.tsx has no 'forgot password' (grep for forgot|reset finds nothing). Notifications live only inside the doc (engine.ts:663) with no e-mail, push or WhatsApp digest. There is no product tour, checklist, help centre link or in-app chat. Dashboard empty state just says 'No reports for your role yet.' (Dashboard.tsx:28-33).
findings.impact: Each invited teammate who never activates is lost seat revenue, and a locked-out user can't recover without support. Without a daily digest of 'your 5 tasks today, 3 overdue invoices', users don't come back. HubSpot, Pipedrive and monday win on lifecycle e-mail and in-app guidance.
findings.recommendation:
Add these, all small or medium:
- Supabase Auth invite (inviteUserByEmail through an Edge Function) with a bilingual template,
- resetPasswordForEmail on the sign-in page,
- a 'Getting started' checklist card on the dashboard (add teammates, import customers, post first invoice, connect WhatsApp, enable ETA) with progress,
- a contextual '?' linking to a bilingual help centre,
- a daily 8am digest by e-mail or WhatsApp per user (my tasks, approvals waiting, rotting deals) from pg_cron,
- a lifecycle e-mail sequence (day 0/1/3/7/12 of trial) tied to checklist progress.
findings.auditor: Team.add only inserts the member and shows a toast with the /join link (Team.tsx:16-28). There is no forgot-password or reset code in src. Notifications live only inside the document. The empty state is exactly as quoted (Dashboard.tsx:28-33). Accurate.

findings.title: Landing positions Bonyan as a follower ('Inspired by Salesforce…'), with no pricing, proof or demo
findings.evidence: The 'best ideas' grid lists 12 features each captioned 'Inspired by Attio/Salesforce/HubSpot…' (Landing.tsx:8-21, 104-113). It has no pricing section, testimonials, logos, video, live demo link or comparison table, and the hero mock is static (Landing.tsx:142-183). The copy claims accuracy 'بنسبة ١٠٠٪' / '100% correct' (i18n.ts:37-38). Half the page stays English in Arabic mode (see STRA-02).
findings.impact: Telling buyers that each feature comes from a bigger brand invites them to buy that brand. The '100%' claim is a liability once a customer finds an edge case. With no price shown, price-sensitive Egyptian SMEs leave for Daftra or Odoo pages that show it.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite around outcomes and the unique wedge: 'Your own system in 15 minutes, in Arabic, ETA-ready, and it can't break your books.' Replace 'Inspired by' with a comparison table (Bonyan vs Odoo vs Zoho vs Daftra vs HubSpot) on time-to-live, Arabic, ETA, WhatsApp, guardrails, AI doctor and price per user in EGP. Add a 'Try the demo company' button (no sign-up; see STRA-03), a 60-second video, pricing, 3 pilot customer quotes from Egypt and a trust strip (PDPL, hosting region). Replace '100%' with 'balanced by design: every entry checked'.
findings.auditor: The 'Inspired by …' grid (Landing.tsx:8-21, 104-113) and the '١٠٠٪ / 100% correct' claim (i18n.ts:37-38) are as described. There is no pricing, demo, proof or legal links. Template taglines stay English in Arabic mode (Landing.tsx:97). Accurate.

findings.title: Onboarding doesn't learn from free text and builds nothing from the challenges beyond fixed packs
findings.evidence: suggest() scores templates by exact id or English keyword match (recommend.ts:96-119), and an Arabic or descriptive industry gets no industry bonus. Challenges only switch on fixed reports in buildReports (packs.ts:50-55), and buildWorkflows ignores them (packs.ts:61). The 'products' answer (a newline list) is used only for seed names (Builder.tsx:66). Nothing creates custom modules or fields from what the company said.
findings.impact: The onboarding feels like 'pick a template' rather than 'we built YOUR system'. A free-text, AI-tailored onboarding is the clearest way to beat Odoo's app-store complexity and Salesforce's blank org (criteria 8, 9, 11).
findings.recommendation: Add an optional 'Describe your business in your own words (Arabic or English)' box in step 1. The Edge Function sends it plus the answers to Claude with tools `propose_answers(Answers)` and `propose_schema_patch(JSON-Patch on generated schema)`, constrained to the field types in fieldTypes.ts and module roles in roles.ts. Show the patch on Suggest as 'We also added: Batch no. on products, a Tender bond field, a Site visits module' with checkboxes. Every patch must pass validate() with zero errors before it is offered (the existing per-template zero-error test pattern extends to AI output).
findings.auditor: Overstated. Challenges and channels do add modules through extraSpecs (recommend.ts:131-137): lost_leads or a WhatsApp, Facebook or website channel adds Leads, manual_invoices or no_followup adds Quotations, purchasing or stock_mismatch adds Suppliers and Purchases, and service_delays adds Tickets. Challenges also add reports (packs.ts:47-53). What is true: buildWorkflows ignores challenges, no custom fields come from the answers, the 'products' list is used only as seed names, and free text matters only for 'other'. The AI tailoring recommendation is sound.

findings.title: Not field-ready: no PWA/offline, no mobile app; whole-doc save on poor mobile networks
findings.evidence: There are only two layout breakpoints (styles.css:379, 390) and no manifest or service worker (grep finds none). Every save posts the whole workspace JSON (store.ts:56-61), and a failed save retries every 5 s (store.ts:62-66). Templates target field reps: Medical 'Rep visits' (templates.ts:95-103) and the 'field_visits' feature (recommend.ts:68).
findings.impact: Egyptian field reps work on mid-range Android phones and 3G/4G with dead zones. HubSpot, Salesforce, Zoho, Pipedrive and Odoo have native mobile apps with offline capture and GPS check-in. Visit logging, the medical template's key workflow, won't happen reliably.
findings.recommendation:
After STRA-04 (record-level writes), ship a PWA:
- manifest and installable icon,
- service worker caching the app shell,
- an IndexedDB outbox for creates and updates (visits, notes, tasks) that syncs per record,
- a mobile-first record form,
- 'Check in' on the visit module capturing GPS and time,
- a camera upload for receipts and site photos,
- voice note → Claude transcribes and summarises into the visit's notes (Arabic dialect). This is a strong demo differentiator.
findings.auditor: Verified: the only breakpoints are 1100 and 760 px (styles.css:379, 390, 434). There is no manifest or service worker (public/ holds only favicon.svg). Every save sends the whole document, and a failed save retries every 5 s (store.ts:62-66). Accurate. A PWA outbox only makes sense after record-level writes (STRA-04).

findings.title: Quick wins that make the AI 'doctor' explainable today, without an LLM
findings.evidence: Issues carry only message, tab and ids (validate.ts:10-17). The health ring score is linear and unexplained (validate.ts:315-319). Warnings don't say why something matters or how to fix it ('Stage … has a lower probability than the stage before it', validate.ts:225).
findings.impact: Non-technical owners see '73%' and a list of messages, not a path to green. Small explanatory additions make the doctor feel intelligent before any AI is added.
findings.recommendation:
Give each Issue a stable code (e.g. PIPE_WON_COUNT), a why (one sentence on the business consequence), and a fixHint or fix patch for the deterministic cases:
- set the Won probability to 100,
- reorder stages,
- remove a dangling report filter,
- add a missing Tasks module,
- pick the first date field for a date trigger.
Group issues by area with progress bars, and show 'Fix all safe issues (5)'. The codes also become the keys the later AI layer and i18n (STRA-02) attach to.
findings.auditor: Issue has only level, message, tab and ids (validate.ts:10-17). The score is linear and unexplained. Messages have no 'why' or fix. Adding stable codes is the right foundation for i18n (STRA-02) and for the AI doctor. S effort is realistic.

findings.title: Date automations are marked done before running, failures are never retried, and collection tasks go to whoever opened the app first
findings.evidence: runScheduled (engine.ts:676-692) writes workflowRuns[`${w.id}:${rec.id}`] = today BEFORE execute(). execute() catches every action error and turns it into a free-text note (engine.ts:666-668). So a failed run is recorded as done and never retried. The key never re-arms either: an invoice that is partly paid, or whose due date changes, gets no further reminder. create_task assigns rec.values.owner ?? assignee ?? ctx.user.id (engine.ts:650). Invoices have no owner field (roles.ts:227-233), so the default 'Collect overdue invoices' task (packs.ts:72) goes to whichever user's browser ran runScheduled on mount (Shell.tsx:23-28). That can be a sales rep or a read-only manager.
findings.impact: The core cash automation silently runs once per invoice at most, can fail permanently, and hands the collection task to a random person instead of finance. Nobody sees a list of failed or missed runs. Owners will believe dunning is happening when it isn't.
findings.recommendation: Record a run only after every action succeeds, and store {status, error, attempts} in a workflowRuns log. Re-arm the key when the watched date changes or the record's balance changes, and allow a 'repeat every N days while the condition holds' option (dunning). Add an 'assign to' option on create_task (record owner, a specific user, a role's round-robin), and default overdue-invoice tasks to the finance role. Show the runs and failures in a 'Runs' panel and in the health doctor.

findings.title: Default dashboard revenue KPIs are wrong: 'Sales by month' uses the record's creation date, and revenue includes VAT
findings.evidence: packs.ts:46 'Sales by month' groups invoices by '__month', and pseudoValue returns rec.createdAt.slice(0,7) for '__month' (engine.ts:592), not the invoice date. An invoice dated last month but entered today lands in this month. packs.ts:40 'Invoiced revenue' and :46 sum 'total', which is VAT-inclusive, and not 'subtotal'. With Egypt's 14% default VAT, revenue is overstated by 14% against the ledger, where account 4000 is credited only t.subtotal (engine.ts:469). Seed data hides the date problem because backdate() rewrites createdAt (seed.ts:189-194).
findings.impact: The owner's flagship dashboard shows a revenue figure that doesn't reconcile with the books (IFRS 15 revenue excludes VAT collected) and a monthly trend shifted by data-entry date. In the first month-end meeting, the accountant's P&L and Bonyan's dashboard disagree, which undermines the 'accounting that always balances' brand.
findings.recommendation: Add a '__docdate' pseudo-field (values.date for documents, createdAt otherwise) and make it the default 'month' grouping for invoices and purchases. Change the revenue reports to measure 'subtotal' and label them 'Revenue (excl. VAT)'. Add a validate.ts warning when a report sums 'total' under a revenue-like name. Better still, let reports read the journal (account 4000) so dashboard revenue equals the books by construction.

findings.title: Automation conditions on rollup or lookup fields can be configured but never match
findings.evidence: The builder offers every field as an 'Only if' condition through fieldOptions (ReportsTab.tsx:48-51, used at AutomationsTab.tsx:49 and 116), and validate.ts only checks that the field exists (validate.ts:268). But runWorkflows calls matches(ctx.schema, rec, w.conditions) without ws (engine.ts:639), and so does runScheduled (engine.ts:687). Without ws, pseudoValue returns rec.values[key] (engine.ts:584-595), which is always undefined for rollup and lookup fields. Scoring (engine.ts:148), approvals and reports do pass ws.
findings.impact: A natural rule like 'When a customer is updated, only if Balance due > 0 → notify finance' or 'only if Customer governorate = Alexandria' publishes cleanly with a green health check and never fires. Users conclude automations are unreliable.
findings.recommendation: Pass ctx.ws to matches() in runWorkflows and runScheduled, and add an engine test with a rollup condition. Until then, have validate.ts raise an error for computed-field conditions in automations.

findings.title: set_field automations can change a posted invoice's date or due date after it is numbered and journalled
findings.evidence: postDocument ends with runWorkflows(ctx, rec, 'updated') (engine.ts:505). execute()'s set_field branch writes rec.values = cleanValues(...) directly (engine.ts:653-658). It skips updateRecord's guard 'Posted documents can't be changed' (engine.ts:267), the field history log and the updatedAt bump. The invoice system fields 'date' and 'due_date' are sys(), not readOnly (roles.ts:229-231), so AutomationsTab offers them as set_field targets (AutomationsTab.tsx:144). validate.ts only blocks readOnly fields (validate.ts:276).
findings.impact: An admin's well-meant 'When an invoice is updated → set Due date' or a custom-field rule rewrites a posted, numbered, journalled invoice with no audit trail. That breaks the 'posted documents are immutable' guarantee shown on the landing page (Landing.tsx:26) and can shift ageing or the ETA payload.
findings.recommendation: In execute(), refuse set_field on records whose module has lines and whose status is not 'draft', except for an explicit allowlist of non-financial custom fields. Route set_field through updateRecord(..., {silent:true}) so history and updatedAt are kept. Add a validate.ts error for set_field on system fields of invoices and purchases.

findings.title: Notifications share one global read flag, and automation failures are broadcast to every user
findings.evidence: Each note has one boolean read in the shared document. Opening the bell sets n.read = true on every note the viewer can see (Shell.tsx:77). An admin sees all role-addressed notes (Shell.tsx:32), so when the owner glances at the bell, finance's 'Invoice … is overdue' alerts (packs.ts:72, role 'finance') turn read for the finance team too. Failure notes ('Automation … could not finish', engine.ts:667) and reorder alerts (engine.ts:699) have no role or user, so every sales rep sees them. Notes are never capped, unlike activity, which is capped at 500 (engine.ts:217-218), so the document keeps growing.
findings.impact: The alerts that drive collections and stock action are dismissed for everyone by whoever looks first. Technical failure messages are noise for reps and missing for the admin who could fix them. This undermines the planned digest and doctor features.
findings.recommendation: Store read state per user (readBy: string[] or a per-user lastSeen timestamp). Address automation failures to the admin role only, with a link to the automation. Cap or archive notes older than 90 days. After STRA-04, move notifications to a table with a per-user read column.

findings.title: Arabic-first data entry silently corrupts imports: Eastern-Arabic digits import as 0 and Arabic field names get meaningless keys
findings.evidence: convert() for number, currency, percent and rating does Number(raw.replace(/[^0-9.-]/g, '')) (engine.ts:813-816). '١٥٠٠' becomes '' and Number('') = 0, which passes Number.isFinite, so the row imports with 0 and no error. The PHONE regex /^\+?[0-9 ()-]{7,20}$/ (engine.ts:172) rejects '٠١٠…' numbers typed on Arabic keyboards. slugKey strips every non-Latin character (schema.ts:217-223), so a field labelled 'رقم الدفعة' gets key 'field', then 'field_2' (ModulesTab.tsx:188-193). Those keys are what formulas and automation placeholders like {field_2} must reference.
findings.impact: An Egyptian distributor importing an Arabic Excel price list gets every price, budget or quantity silently set to 0. Leads with Arabic-digit phones fail validation. Builders who name things in Arabic (the target user) get opaque formula and placeholder keys. All of this works against the 'Egypt first' and 'simplicity' promises, and the import case is silent data corruption.
findings.recommendation: Normalise Eastern-Arabic and Persian digits (U+0660-0669, U+06F0-06F9) and the Arabic decimal and thousands separators (٫ ٬) to ASCII in one helper. Call it in convert(), cleanValues() and the phone check. Make convert() raise an error when the stripped string is empty instead of returning 0. Transliterate or use a short uid for non-Latin labels, and show the field label rather than the key in formula and placeholder pickers. Add tests for '١٥٠٠' and '٠١٠١٢٣٤٥٦٧٨'.
